valores.Aspecto|Un solo color completamente unif: A single, completely uniform, metallic iridescent color. *Yamabuki Ogon* (yellow-gold), *Platinum Ogon* (silver-white), *Orenji Ogon* (orange).
valores.Aspecto|Negro base con manchas rojas y b: Black base with red and white spots. The black is dominant and envelops the other colors.
valores.Aspecto|Blanco con manchas rojas Y manch: White with red spots and small black spots (*sumi*). The three colors never overlap perfectly.
valores.Aspecto|Bicolor negro + otro color. *Shi: Two-tone: black + another color. *Shiro Utsuri* (black + white), *Hi Utsuri* (black + red), *Ki Utsuri* (black + yellow).
valores.El más \"natural\"|Aspecto que recuerda: Appearance reminiscent of the original color of wild carp.
valores.Cuerpo|Alargado, como el común pero más: Elongated, like the common one but more slender
valores.Cuerpo|Muy redondo, sin aleta dorsal: Very round, without a dorsal fin
valores.Cuerpo|Redondo, joroba pronunciada detrá: Round, with a pronounced hump behind the head
valores.Ojos|Bolsas de fluido bajo cada ojo que: Fluid-filled sacs beneath each eye that wobble
valores.Ojos|Telescópicos — protruyen del cuerpo: Telescopic — protrude from the body in the shape of cylinders
valores.Cola|Simple muy larga y bifurcada — pued: Very long, forked tail—it can be as long as the body
valores.Cola|Doble, con aleta dorsal muy alta: Double, with a very tall dorsal fin
valores.Colores|Naranja, rojo-blanco (\"Red Cap: Orange, red-and-white (“Red Cap Oranda”), black, calico
valores.Colores|Calicó — azul, rojo, naranja, ne: Calico — blue, red, orange, black, and white mixed in a unique pattern. Blue is the most difficult color to achieve and the most highly valued.
valores.Tipos|Doitsu (pocas escamas en línea lat: Doitsu (few scales on the lateral and dorsal lines), Leather Koi (completely scaleless).
valores.Gin Rin|Escamas con brillo plateado o do: Scales with a silvery or golden sheen in the center.
valores.Patrón ideal|Manchas rojas bien definida: Well-defined, symmetrical red markings that do not extend into the fins. A pure, snow-white base.
valores.Patrón ideal|El sumi (negro) en aletas p: The sumi (black) is distributed symmetrically on the pectoral fins and along the body.
valores.Grading|La calidad se juzga por la nitid: Quality is judged by the sharpness of the edges (kiwa), the intensity of the red, and the purity of the white.
valores.Categorías|Tancho Kohaku (solo un círcul: Tancho Kohaku (only one red circle on the head), Ippon Hi (a single long red stripe)
valores.Único|El único koi que cambia de patrón: The only koi that changes color throughout its life. In cold water, it turns black; in warm water, it appears whiter.
valores.Cabeza|Capuchón que envuelve toda la cab: A cap that covers the entire head
valores.Cabeza|\"Capuchón\" (wen) — masa de teji: "Cap" (wen) — a mass of orange/red spongy tissue covering the head
valores.Historia|Surgió en 1927. El tipo \"Kinda: It first appeared in 1927. The modern “Kindai Showa” variety has more white.
valores.Diferencia clave|En el Showa, el negro l: In the Showa, the black color extends to the head and pectoral fins; in the Sanke, it does not.
valores.Diferencia con Showa|El negro del Sanke: The black in the Sanke is on top of the white; the black in the Showa is on top of the base black.

nombres.koi sin escamas o con pocas: Koi with no scales or very few scales

textos.df07c1f93f0eb0dc: **Notes**: Tall body with dark bands. Swims with its head tilted downward, like anostomids. Feeds on soft plants.
textos.aaa944a6ea276efc: **Notes**: Five black bands on a yellowish background. Very hardy, but it grows and becomes territorial.
textos.76ef6eb53d2db481: **Notes**: Large, fleshy corallites with spiny edges, in a wide variety of colors. Responds well to direct feeding.
textos.b6a09ca38a9ce0f1: **Notes**: Known as L155. Juveniles are black with white spots and very attractive, but as adults they grow to over one meter. Suitable only for very large aquariums.
textos.b3011fa956c7f9a5: **Notes**: Known as L193. Solid black with a lyre-shaped tail. Like the Adonis, it grows to a very large size.
textos.492b105dea5922f6: **Notes**: Small loach with a mottled brown and beige pattern. It forages for food by stirring up the sand with its barbels; it prefers clean water and a slight current.
textos.55d2fb556e48ef1c: **Notes**: Body covered with spiny plates; audible sounds when removed from the water. Nocturnal.
textos.015c37e351906355: **Notes**: Black with a teardrop-shaped orange spot near the tail. Highly susceptible to white spot disease and requires high oxygen levels: for experts only.
textos.db4820c754dbdeed: **Notes**: Juveniles are yellow and turn deep blue as adults. They need algae daily.
textos.dbad4fa65006e87c: **Notes**: Dark body with a white spot under the eye and an orange dorsal fin. Slightly hardier than the blue dust.
textos.c9a2c83c5fc8ce29: **Notes**: Sky-blue body, black face, and yellow dorsal fin. Highly susceptible to marine white spot disease: quarantine is essential, and the water must be well-oxygenated and have a strong current.
textos.16b2d6ceaa49a16b: **Notes**: Blue and yellow stripes edged with black. Spectacular, but one of the largest and most aggressive surgeonfish.
textos.56c28e0b4a771b1e: **Notes**: Known as “powder brown”: dark with a white spot on the cheek and yellow bands on the fins.
textos.6e1d8d659c379b6f: **Notes**: Brown surgeonfish with orange spots on its head. Sturdy and a good algae eater.
textos.316698e78f68e2bf: **Notes**: Dark gray with an orange stripe behind the eye. Juveniles are yellow. Large and hardy.
textos.a0b70130c2252a82: **Notes**: Juveniles resemble the lemon angelfish (yellow); as adults, they turn brown with an orange spot behind the pectoral fin.
textos.84806f254c5fc41e: **Notes**: Thin black lines on a light gray background and orange caudal spines. Dominant; requires a very large aquarium.
textos.d8b26dd3f7ec8119: **Notes**: A bluish-brown surgeonfish with a white tail that feeds on plankton. One of the calmest surgeonfish.
textos.4359ecc697f75578: **Notes**: Juveniles resemble Eibl’s dwarf angelfish. As adults, they are dark with a spot behind the eye.
textos.a3e32db69bbc699f: **Notes**: Known as the “threadfin acara” because of the filaments on its dorsal fin. It digs tunnels under the roots.
textos.0ede5c35207df9ef: **Notes**: A giant, single-celled alga shaped like an umbrella. A classic in cell biology.
textos.e1b7b22bc69cd117: **Notes**: The smallest sturgeon, but it still grows to over one meter. It requires cold, highly oxygenated water and a spacious pond free of obstacles. Specific sturgeon food: it does not compete well with koi.
textos.bc7c46bca80df926: **Notes**: Camouflaged like brown algae. Very useful against Aiptasia infestations, although some specimens nip at corals.
textos.e66ddadbe662640c: **Notes**: Thick, sturdy branches found in areas with strong waves. Tolerates strong currents.
textos.d573ba5af1f183a1: **Notes**: Thin branches with short corallites, often with blue or purple tips. Delicate.
textos.dfc892b47470ea31: **Notes**: Short, finger-like branches in compact colonies. Tolerates intense light well.
textos.6903e5d17450e7b9: **Notes**: Thin branches resembling a bottle brush, often in shades of blue or violet. Sensitive to changes in alkalinity.
textos.a54e51d535b6549e: **Notes**: Thick, short branches with bud-shaped corallites. Robust for the genus.
textos.428ed243f4bfb1ab: **Notes**: Horizontal plates with short branches. Common in deeper areas; prefers less light than other Acropora species.
textos.c6ced5444010a93e: **Notes**: Thick, short, finger-like branches. Sturdy for an Acropora.
textos.c69316b68a985970: **Notes**: Forms flat, horizontal tables that provide shade for the corals below. Requires space and bright light.
textos.4610fdc73dd45af8: **Notes**: Thick branches with contrasting-colored tips. Popular in cultivated varieties such as “Purple Monster.”
textos.451d575e8e64284f: **Notes**: Thin, dense branches with small corallites, often green or gray. Grows quickly.
textos.053d64b5905f1c2e: **Notes**: Extraordinary colors: blue, pink, green, orange, multicolored. The most sensitive indicator of water quality—if an A. millepora is doing well, the reef is doing well. Requires nearly perfect NSW parameters. Very sensitive to KH fluctuations. The “Holy Grail” for many reef aquarists.
textos.4b62701d00a39a21: **Notes**: A long-branched staghorn Acropora; formerly Acropora formosa. It grows very quickly.
textos.b2efa5851e491fbd: **Notes**: Thin, compact branches, often green or blue. Popular in SPS reef tanks.
textos.71639d9e6d7288d1: **Notes**: Thick, bush-like branches with contrasting-colored tips. A good Acropora for beginners.
textos.51dbb533fb8ab600: **Notes**: Branches with elongated corallites in deep blue or violet hues. Highly prized for its color.
textos.95c026fd668b1205: **Notes**: The most diverse and demanding genus in the hobby. Highly varied morphologies: branched (staghorn), tabular, digitated, encrusting. Requires ultra-stable NSW parameters. Changes in KH of ±0.5 dKH within 24 hours can cause STN or RTN. Only for aquarists with 2+ years of marine aquarium experience.
textos.7be686d905b47755: **Notes**: Table-shaped branches with brightly colored tips (green, purple, yellow). Like all Acropora, it requires very stable parameters and low—but not zero—nutrient levels.
textos.7aef42fdfac6805c: **Notes**: Twisted branches in shades of pink or blue. Grows in compact clumps.
textos.bfd312d52f32e9aa: **Notes**: Short, thick branches forming a bush-like shape. One of the most tolerant Acropora species, good for beginners in SPS.
textos.2f0c9158189422c2: **Notes**: Long, open branches in shades of green or blue. It grows quickly and is one of the most rewarding Acropora species.
textos.cc4a349167cc4e81: **Notes**: A small red anemone that closes up into a ball when out of the water. Very hardy; lives in the intertidal zone.
textos.ac55757681cc03d6: **Notes**: Known as the saddle acara: greenish body with shiny scales and a dark spot. Robust.
textos.663c82bc1a68c6b5: **Notes**: Dark with white spots and a body covered in spiny plates. It makes sounds when removed from the water. Nocturnal and very long-lived.
textos.405b8652b0ee2dc2: **Notes**: Small stream catfish with yellow and brown bands. Nocturnal and secretive.
textos.db3b9116581c2b65: **Notes**: Smaller than the Congo tetra, with yellow fins and a tail that is elongated in the center in males.
textos.ff2934e82d266045: **Notes**: Slender viviparous fish with a keel on its belly and bluish iridescence. Oxygenated water with a current.
textos.642040061eab0cc2: **Notes**: Red and white stripes. It digs burrows that it shares with gobies such as the yasha: a fascinating pair.
textos.d055844e233a0f0e: **Notes**: A reddish pistol shrimp that digs burrows. It often pairs up with gobies.
textos.1b75b5af9f4a07f5: **Notes**: When it snaps its giant claw shut, it quickly creates a cavitation bubble with an audible pop. Its symbiotic relationship with the pistol goby is fascinating: the (nearly blind) shrimp digs the burrow, while the goby acts as a sentinel. They communicate through physical contact.
textos.e2fab8238917ae5d: **Notes**: Burgundy-red or pink leaves; one of the best plants for adding a touch of red. The “Mini” variety is used in the foreground.
textos.641dfef44bcdfeff: **Notes**: Very tall, laterally compressed body that allows it to squeeze into crevices in search of fry. It grows slowly. Its scales are hard and protect it from attacks.
textos.5634baae1a196c29: **Notes**: Very tall and flattened, with bands and spiny fins; red and golden varieties exist. More robust than the calvus.
textos.fd58a872e5445ec9: **Notes**: Long polyps with twelve tentacles, similar to Goniopora but easier to care for. Prefers fine food.
textos.684a46931427ebef: **Notes**: Vertical black stripes on a gray background. Very hardy, but a breeding pair can take over an entire aquarium. Best kept with other Central American species of similar size.
textos.84889194afcd3708: **Notes**: Known as the “T-bar” because of the T-shaped stripe on its side. A peaceful relative of the convict cichlid.
textos.871186921602cdb2: **Notes**: Small, checkered, and very active in groups; they also swim in the middle of the tank. Nearly extinct in the wild; those sold in stores are bred in captivity.
textos.d8b5f242b88a1e3f: **Notes**: Vertical red stripes and a black spot on the dorsal fin. Small Caribbean hawkfish.
textos.2a54d588c6e2fa08: **Notes**: Pink stripes on a light background, and a tail with red and yellow spots. Forms a symbiotic relationship with pistol shrimp.
textos.c6457c795ae9c5a0: **Notes**: Covered with orange spots on a light background. Lives in symbiosis with pistol shrimp.
textos.4be57c40382c1b96: **Notes**: Orange stripes and a large dorsal fin with a black ocellus. Shares a burrow with pistol shrimp. Requires sand with some coarse gravel.
textos.0377973213835343: **Notes**: Brown stripes on a light background with yellow spots. Shares a burrow with pistol shrimp.
textos.678fa93c2e02a83e: **Notes**: Wide red bands on a white background. Shares a burrow with pistol shrimp.
textos.d986bf1b32cfbc00: **Notes**: Golden yellow with a tall body. In the wild, it lives near gorgonians and corals.
textos.17da1b3348af6f09: **Notes**: Dark vertical stripes on a greenish background. Keeps the substrate stirred up and clean.
textos.0f69b74fbdd9297f: **Notes**: Males have a yellow band on their tails. Extinct in the wild for years and reintroduced thanks to aquarists. Keeping this species helps conserve it.
textos.3d694fbafd11f532: **Notes**: Known as Nesaea crassicaulis: elongated reddish leaves and thick stems. Intense color when treated with iron.
textos.95c3c7753445f9f5: **Notes**: Elongated, orange-red leaves. Stands out beautifully in the background of Dutch-style planted tanks.
textos.6422b5d212510748: **Notes**: A stem plant with lanceolate leaves that turn orange or red in bright light. It is sensitive to iron levels and water stability; the tips become deformed if there is a potassium deficiency.
textos.952190f5434dcafc: **Notes**: Orange or yellow, with a bump on the males’ foreheads. Very territorial; best kept alone or in pairs in a large aquarium.
textos.8986c38c9ce62ef7: **Notes**: Thick lips that are red, orange, or white. It digs and destroys aquarium decorations. One of the parents of the “flowerhorn” hybrid.
textos.ffbe2a064419911f: **Notes**: Three dark spots on the side and green iridescence. Very aggressive; one of the parents of the flowerhorn.
textos.9ce40e8ac656cceb: **Notes**: Orange-brown with two white bands and a light-colored tail. Rarely found in stores and more assertive than the ocellaris.
textos.387133b5462602d1: **Notes**: Dark brown with two white bands and a white tail. Related to Clark's clownfish.
textos.204180b91d36a577: **Notes**: Yellowish-orange with two white bands edged in black. Robust and somewhat more territorial.
textos.1ce04b9536c3ffc7: **Notes**: Brown body with orange fins and two white or bluish bands. One of the largest clownfish.
textos.cf025f671b67989a: **Notes**: One of the hardiest and most adaptable clownfish. It is associated with up to 10 species of anemones. Slightly more aggressive than A. ocellaris when defending its anemone. Variable colors: yellow, orange, and black.
textos.163307db5abec240: **Notes**: Orange-red with a large black spot on the side and no white bands in adults.
textos.7be9dad0c4c9c659: **Notes**: Tomato red with a single white stripe behind the eye. One of the easiest marine fish to keep; it is almost always available captive-bred.
textos.3cde1e92a679ab70: **Notes**: Brown with a very wide white central band and a yellow tail. Rare and highly sought after.
textos.0c3ff268a3d46515: **Notes**: Reddish-orange with a darker body on the sides and a white band behind the eye. Hardy.
textos.5384dcd22357eb3c: **Notes**: Orange with a single white stripe behind the eye and black ventral fins. Rarely found in stores.
textos.69f59e815b790903: **Notes**: The world’s most popular marine fish. In a pair, the larger individual is always the female. If the female dies, the dominant male changes sex. An anemone is not essential, but it naturally coexists with Entacmaea quadricolor and Heteractis magnifica. Choose captive-bred specimens.
textos.c66c32b1d318e6a8: **Notes**: Similar to A. ocellaris but with thicker, more distinct black rings. Care requirements are identical. Many selectively bred varieties (Picasso, Platinum, Snowflake, DaVinci). It is associated with the same anemones.
textos.1c058a64011b4342: **Notes**: Orange-pink with a white line along the back and a white bar behind the eye. Delicate at first; prefers anemones.
textos.7a3309562d850763: **Notes**: A saddle-shaped white patch on the back. Available as a captive-bred specimen.
textos.f2355eb57b9d1d67: **Notes**: Orange with a white stripe running from the snout to the tail. Shy; does best with calm tankmates.
textos.f3f0cb24d0e326e3: **Notes**: Dark brown with two white bands and a yellow tail. In the wild, it lives with the anemone Stichodactyla haddoni.
textos.a1b9c5e8991a104e: **Notes**: The largest mushroom; it can close like a bag and trap fish that are sleeping on it.
textos.e464ec4df7452ea5: **Notes**: Breathes air and can move about out of the water. An escape artist: use a tight-fitting lid.
textos.12b6caf3e270930b: **Notes**: Its eyes are split into two so it can see both above and below the water at the same time. It requires brackish water, shallow depths, and a beach area. Only for very experienced aquarists.
textos.3a711c6f287ea84e: **Notes**: Black females with white spots and a yellow tail. Delicate; requires plenty of microfauna and sand.
textos.a4888f4b19b6abac: **Notes**: The albino and “veil” varieties sold in stores are usually captive-bred crosses. Males develop tentacles on their snouts. One of the best algae eaters for medium-sized aquariums.
textos.0d4e46bfc1adfb23: **Notes**: A small, brown Ancistrus with light spots and yellow fin edges. Ideal for small aquariums.
textos.a4e56dcac901dfce: **Notes**: Known as L183. Black with small white spots and white edges on the fins, like a starry sky.
textos.4450d6efc31ca4c3: **Notes**: Black with large white spots and white edges on the fins. Very striking.
textos.7926cd17d7776e63: **Notes**: Dark Ancistrus covered in white spots. Good algae eater.
textos.81b65a1bb3404518: **Notes**: Known as L034. Matte black with a snout covered in long tentacles. Requires warm, well-oxygenated water with a current.
textos.c2e3555c97c77025: **Notes**: Compatible with Discus if the temperature does not exceed 27–28°C. Cleans algae off the glass. Requires driftwood. The high temperature in a Discus aquarium is at the upper limit of the Ancistrus’s temperature range.
textos.d0243742c1be2450: **Notes**: Transparent body with violet stripes. It lives among the tentacles of anemones and cleans fish.
textos.03028a02050a5b8e: **Notes**: Turquoise-blue lines on the face and shiny scales. Sturdy and fairly calm outside of the breeding season. A good medium-sized cichlid for beginners.
textos.2ced6c9c99cdedef: **Notes**: Metallic green scales and a face with turquoise lines; males have a hump and fins with orange edges. Very territorial: best kept with large, robust cichlids.
textos.3619fc340596cc19: **Notes**: Long green tentacles with purple tips. Very common on Mediterranean rocks; reproduces by fission.
textos.20fe5410c92923bf: **Notes**: Conical shell with yellow and brown stripes. Naturally controls small snail infestations. It also eats small nerite snails and may prey on very young shrimp.
textos.d22a0705e99027b1: **Notes**: A dwarf cichlid with blue-speckled scales and dark spots. Very peaceful, suitable for community aquariums.
textos.7136a0a3021d00f0: **Notes**: Black and gold stripes and an upturned mouth. Swims at an angle with its head down, scraping algae off rocks. In pairs or trios, they fight: best kept alone or in a large group.
textos.995cbb44a199c1c7: **Notes**: Related to the striped anostomus, with thinner black and gold bands and fins without red.
textos.c22aa019f187cfb2: **Notes**: Known as the warty frogfish. It uses a lure on its head to attract prey. It must live alone.
textos.fa64ecf7d62c965d: **Notes**: Long polyps with feathery tentacles that do not pulsate, unlike Xenia. Grows quickly on rock. Some fish nibble on it.
textos.dda58c62ec661230: **Notes**: Flexible, feather-like purple branches. Photosynthetic gorgonians from the Caribbean are the easiest to care for; non-photosynthetic ones, which are red or yellow in color, need to be fed daily.
textos.79626df47722847d: **Notes**: Elongated, spear-shaped leaves. Just as hardy as other Anubias species, but taller, making it suitable for the background of aquariums with herbivorous fish.
textos.ce30c36f67edd5bf: **Notes**: The tough, bitter leaves discourage goldfish from eating it. This isn’t always foolproof with very voracious goldfish. It tolerates hard, alkaline water perfectly.
textos.f61a22af7d9410f0: **Notes**: Plump leaves like those of a coffee plant and reddish new shoots. Just as hardy as other Anubias species and not eaten by herbivorous fish.
textos.695c39839bb24742: **Notes**: A variety of Anubias with narrow, lanceolate leaves. Just as hardy.
textos.bda061ad151379a4: **Notes**: Same care requirements as A. barteri. Its tough leaves protect it from goldfish, although some particularly voracious specimens will attack it anyway.
textos.6150631aa90426f6: **Notes**: The smallest Anubias, perfect for nano tanks and as accents on rocks.
textos.ec5141c388a1d435: **Notes**: Triangular leaves on long stems. Elegant and resistant to herbivorous fish.
textos.bdb1bb0a620e9598: **Notes**: Spear-shaped leaves with lateral lobes. Large, suitable for spacious aquariums.
textos.abcfb49618d6f33d: **Notes**: Elongated leaves with wavy edges. Just as hardy as other Anubias species.
textos.b84a6dd60ed4a8c6: **Notes**: Males have blue spots and a tail with yellow and black bands. Highly adaptable to salinity.
textos.0beb1566dd7567ee: **Notes**: Bluish-silver with red fins. An active swimmer and tolerant of cool water, making it suitable for aquariums without a heater in temperate homes. Requires a cover.
textos.038c55f6c4075722: **Notes**: Known as the red-and-green-tailed tetra: the rear half is red with greenish highlights. Active and hardy.
textos.b22935cee28fc4f5: **Notes**: Males are orange with red spots and a lyre-shaped tail with white edges. Prefers low light, soft water, and a well-planted, well-covered aquarium.
textos.1b60a1b10ddbccc2: **Notes**: Two dark longitudinal stripes and fins with red spots. A rainforest killifish for calm, well-covered aquariums.
textos.4381905a542b347f: **Notes**: Males are blue-green with red spots and fins with yellow edges. Cool water.
textos.28ebc8e038dce923: **Notes**: Males are reddish with blue scales. A simple and hardy killifish.
textos.1a752e75f1485f26: **Notes**: Males are blue with red spots and orange-edged fins. Small and suitable for planted nano tanks.
textos.a7928aee171316bc: **Notes**: Males are a vivid sky blue with red markings. One of the most striking Aphyosemion species.
textos.2b039f36ad90ee12: **Notes**: Bluish body covered with red spots and fins with yellow edges. Quite hardy.
textos.84d040fefdbca8a3: **Notes**: Deep red with green highlights and a rounded tail. Slightly more delicate than other killifish.
textos.28dd012f7ff6c3db: **Notes**: Tiny killifish with red spots on a blue-green background. Cool, soft water; ideal for a dedicated nano tank.
textos.c386db0ad4de62ea: **Notes**: Males are blue-green with red spots, and their tails have red and yellow bands. They prefer cool water.
textos.0717ee6eb52d13de: **Notes**: Males are green with red spots and a red and yellow lyre-shaped tail. A rainforest killifish for cool water.
textos.4adc3b69d199202e: **Notes**: Males are reddish with blue scales. Belongs to the Aphyosemion elegans group.
textos.8224bde2da335830: **Notes**: Males are very brightly colored, with red, blue, and yellow. Soft, cool water is essential.
textos.9225c502ee6ecee0: **Notes**: Males are reddish with blue scales and fins with white edges. Prefers slightly cooler water.
textos.95fb2f7a5d00c11d: **Notes**: Males are blue-green with red spots and a tail with yellow edges. A rainforest killifish for cool water.
textos.3b15a9c57e53b182: **Notes**: Bluish males with red markings and edged fins. Cool, soft water.
textos.fe2cc571b1669db5: **Notes**: Males are blue-green with five horizontal red stripes. Although tropical, this species prefers cool water, low light, and plants.
textos.a0bbd15242903a0e: **Notes**: Males are light blue with small red markings. Peaceful and suitable for nano tanks.
textos.084cbe4b5a83c940: **Notes**: The male has a spear-shaped tail with a colored edge. It prefers soft, acidic water, dry leaves on the bottom, and small caves. There are many color varieties bred in captivity.
textos.0c68056bda7fb74e: **Notes**: Small apistogramma with a red-spotted tail. Soft blackwater.
textos.0d852b3ed1dfd5c6: **Notes**: Males have a tall dorsal fin and reddish fins. Soft, acidic water.
textos.39cb1fbe417fc681: **Notes**: Known as “Inca”: males have yellow faces and reddish fins. Very striking in blackwater aquariums.
textos.5505e16d24c83ced: **Notes**: Two dark longitudinal lines and a dorsal fin with long rays. There are many local forms with different colorations.
textos.2f86870ae175dad3: **Notes**: Males are yellow with blue iridescence on the head. It tolerates cooler, less acidic water than other Apistogramma species, making it an easier choice for beginners interested in dwarf cichlids.
textos.32e790ee73d612cf: **Notes**: The most tolerant of the Apistogramma species. Provide caves (split coconut shells, ceramic caves). The female defends the nest very fiercely. Always keep a ratio of 1 male to 2–3 females.
textos.51bff66106e10ba1: **Notes**: Males have tall fins and blue iridescence. Belongs to the agassizii group.
textos.356a7febca1c87a2: **Notes**: Males have red heads and throats and very tall fins. One of the most challenging Apistogramma species; requires extreme blackwater conditions.
textos.36b99f72f646e19a: **Notes**: Males have tall dorsal fins and a spotted tail. Sturdy and easy to care for within its genus.

textos.d9c87bd732f59558: **Notes**: The sacs can be punctured by sharp edges—substrate and decorations must be completely smooth. No exposed suction filters. The sacs regenerate if punctured. Keep only with their own kind. The most delicate of all the fancy varieties.

textos.07d46d865fc7061e: **Notes**: Beautiful fan-shaped leaves. In low light, it quickly loses its leaves. An invasive species in many countries: never release it into rivers or ponds. Its trade is restricted in the EU.

textos.4c984899c11d3ce8: **Notes**: It covers itself with sponges, algae, and small pieces of coral as camouflage. Fascinating, but it may pull off polyps.
textos.1ca0210225dd1a1b: **Notes**: Extremely long, curved snout for foraging on the bottom. Delicate; requires crystal-clear water.
textos.64d2f443123f6551: **Notes**: A small orange puffer with blue spots and lines on its belly. It may nip at invertebrates.
textos.fa8c16431244cbec: **Notes**: Dark back, light belly, and blue lines. Small Caribbean pufferfish.
textos.47e87d2074423dcd: **Notes**: A small orange pufferfish covered in blue spots. It may nibble on corals and invertebrates.
textos.81792912965f179e: **Notes**: A small pufferfish with black bands on a white background. Its toxic skin protects it from predators. It can bite corals and invertebrates.
textos.2367efc8ee33b7fc: **Notes**: Known as the “Kenya tree.” Very hardy; it reproduces by shedding small twigs that take root on their own throughout the aquarium.
textos.4555d1c86b11ce31: **Notes**: The elongated-bodied goldfish. A fast swimmer. Compatible only with other elongated-bodied goldfish (do not mix with round-bodied fancy goldfish). Can live for more than 20 years. Produces a lot of organic waste: very powerful filtration is required (8–10 times the tank volume per hour).
textos.1bab9eb1caa19271: **Notes**: The original variety from which all others are derived. Extremely hardy. Can survive under ice (as long as there is unfrozen water and O₂). The quintessential pond variety. Jumps frequently.
textos.32680c34831feae3: **Notes**: A wild relative of the goldfish, with a tall, greenish-gold body. Exceptionally resistant to low oxygen levels in winter.
textos.e6b46e20540b22a4: **Notes**: Light green, round leaves. A cold-water plant, ideal for aquariums without a heater.
textos.fdd3ee346c7b9793: **Notes**: A land crab with blue, red, and orange coloring. It needs a large aquaterrarium with moist soil for burrowing.
textos.48f6cf13d4d0f3ce: **Notes**: A shrimp with stripes or green, brown, or reddish coloring, depending on the variety. Easy to care for and hardy; a good alternative to Neocaridina.
textos.44a5d2073eb7cc62: **Notes**: Brown body with blue legs. Like other Sulawesi shrimp, it requires warm, alkaline, and very stable water.
textos.5572267ff54f7a04: **Notes**: The wild form from which Crystal Red, Crystal Black, and Taiwan Bee originate: dark bands on a translucent body. Requires soft, cool water.
textos.dcb85054b53f2c24: **Notes**: Very striking blue and white coloration. The Taiwan Bee varieties (Panda, King Kong, Blue Bolt, Shadow Panda) are the most highly prized in the hobby. They require even purer water than CBS/CRS shrimp. High-quality active substrate is essential. Only for Caridina shrimp experts with prior experience with CBS shrimp.
textos.ccf34b626e27a7f1: **Notes**: Same care and requirements as the CRS. Black and white instead of red and white. Same quality classification (SSS-C). CRS and CBS can be kept together; they interbreed, producing mixed varieties.
textos.c43ed01e7156653e: **Notes**: Requires an active substrate (ADA Amazonia, Tropica Soil, Fluval Stratum) that acidifies and softens the water. Without an active substrate, maintaining water parameters is very difficult. The substrate loses its buffering capacity within 12–18 months and must be replaced. Quality rating: SSS > SS > S > A > B > C. Extremely sensitive to copper (even in trace amounts): never use copper-based medications or water from copper pipes without first testing it.
textos.5c2d3fb53050f80b: **Notes**: Red with white spots shaped like stars. Requires warm, alkaline, very stable water and porous rocks. Endangered species: Purchase only captive-bred specimens.
textos.b4a1bd67ba83a2da: **Notes**: Long, red face shaped like a nose; transparent body. Active and colorful when seen in a group.
textos.4a72b6623e1dba7a: **Notes**: Translucent body with vertical black stripes. More tolerant than crystal Caridina. There are bred varieties, such as the blue Tiger shrimp with orange eyes.
textos.4618310608fa4ae0: **Notes**: The best algae eater in freshwater aquariums. It eats thread algae, green spot algae, and BBA very efficiently. They do not reproduce in freshwater (you must purchase adults). Larger and more active than Neocaridina. Highly valued in aquascapes for algae control.
textos.1c87138d4344de1d: **Notes**: A small shrimp with variable coloring, ranging from green to red. A good eater of fine filamentous algae.
textos.0b285a7c0786806a: **Notes**: Trade name for wild-caught shrimp of various colors. Good cleaners, but they do not reproduce in freshwater.
textos.f9bf00f4aac47b07: **Notes**: Known as “yellow cheek”: reddish body with yellow spots on the head. Sulawesi shrimp for specialized aquariums.
textos.db35cf7efbeefbef: **Notes**: White and red stripes. A Sulawesi lake shrimp for dedicated aquariums with porous rocks.
textos.c6eb5ed3895355ad: **Notes**: Red eyes; males have a red line on their belly. Small softwater pufferfish, suitable for a dedicated aquarium.
textos.7237d8dc48fe8fdc: **Notes**: The only true freshwater pufferfish commonly sold. Best kept in a single-species aquarium. Snails help wear down its beak.
textos.8c7d4f72e5269d8d: **Notes**: Small hatchetfish with a black-edged belly. Soft blackwater; floating plants and a lid are essential.
textos.013fd2691c211dfe: **Notes**: Deep, axe-shaped belly with a marbled pattern. It stays close to the surface and jumps very easily: a lid is essential. It thrives among floating plants.
textos.326f72c269a79ff0: **Notes**: One of the most spectacular corals: large white or green tentacles with purple tips. The tentacles can extend 20–30 cm. Place it on the substrate with plenty of open space around it. It lives in sand, not on top of rocks.
textos.6d7b3d14de642af9: **Notes**: Known as “candy cane” or “trumpet coral.” Branches with round polyps that have green or brown edges. One of the easiest and fastest-growing LPS corals.
textos.c56bad6eeef392a3: **Notes**: Known as “green caviar”: small spheres in clusters. It is also farmed for human consumption.
textos.9bca0ded69d2cdeb: **Notes**: Flat, broad leaves with a deep green color. Less invasive than C. taxifolia. Excellent for nutrient removal in refugiums. More stable than C. taxifolia—lower risk of spore formation. Widely used in Mediterranean and Atlantic refugiums.
textos.6b12818bcb7d761f: **Notes**: Known as “sea grapes” because of its small green spheres. It grows quickly and can take over the rock; it can also suddenly “spore” and cloud the water. Best kept only in the refugium.
textos.7797e9dc53b42c4f: **Notes**: Twisted fronds with serrated edges. Useful in the refugium for exporting nutrients.
textos.4b7485f934292093: **Notes**: Deep green, feathery fronds. Grows quickly and can become invasive; best kept in the refugium.
textos.01a8791b3882a5e0: **Notes**: The easiest macroalgae to grow. An excellent nutrient exporter in the refugium. In the main aquarium, it can grow too quickly and overrun corals. If it starts to stolonize, it may “spore” (release all its cytoplasm at once), killing everything around it—this happens if it is over-pruned or the plant reaches the end of its life cycle. Harvest regularly instead of pruning. Invasive species: never dispose of it outdoors.
textos.ef5042a56c18a99a: **Notes**: It can only see upward—it cannot see food at the bottom. Feed from the surface. Do not mix with other goldfish. Do not use suction filters. The most delicate.
textos.98d65c3dcb1ec4e4: **Notes**: One of the most popular nano-fish in the hobby. Bright white spots on a dark blue background. Males have orange dorsal and anal fins. Slightly hard, cool water (20–24°C) is ideal. Compatible with adult cherry shrimp.
textos.dbc7db375d86bf84: **Notes**: A small, mottled catfish that hides in cracks in the wood during the day. It comes out to feed at night.
textos.11931a0a0ecb0c38: **Notes**: Known as the African pygmy angelfish: dark blue with a yellow back and tail. One of the smallest dwarf angelfish.
textos.8ed29fd2958b3151: **Notes**: Dark blue with a yellow face. Small and hardy; one of the most affordable dwarf angelfish.
textos.e1f6dde905315246: **Notes**: Yellow on the front half and dark blue on the back half. More delicate than the flame angelfish or the coral beauty during acclimation.
textos.421726670a74c107: **Reef Safe**: ⚠️ Use caution (may bite soft corals and LPS corals)
textos.684d5a47537fe53c: **Notes**: Deep blue on the back with orange on the belly. One of the hardiest dwarf angelfish. Eats algae constantly. Behavior toward corals is unpredictable on an individual basis.
textos.d4fc8485ebc28b94: **Notes**: Yellow with a dark blue back. A deep-water angelfish, rarely found in stores.
textos.fd083fd3b9af24bc: **Notes**: Light gray with thin vertical orange stripes and a black-edged tail. Hardy and fairly calm.
textos.b0ec87dab7b9743d: **Notes**: Reddish-brown with dark, rust-colored spots. Unobtrusive and hardy.
textos.f598d7a1e76e3e45: **Notes**: A small orange angelfish with a bluish tail. One of the smallest dwarf angelfish.
textos.07692459e91185a4: **Notes**: Known as the lemon angelfish: bright yellow with blue rings around the eye. It may nibble on soft corals and clams.
textos.e84a09e51e5f84ac: **Notes**: Solid yellow with no blue ring around the eye, which distinguishes it from the lemon angelfish. Somewhat delicate upon arrival.
textos.6e88cd2918c9474b: **Notes**: Yellow front half and black rear half. Rare and highly sought-after.
textos.a5d47b92c51f4b1c: **Notes**: Orange-red with blue-black stripes. Reef-safe behavior varies greatly depending on the individual: some never bother the corals, while others constantly nibble on them. Introduce with already established corals and observe for several weeks.
textos.95a2145bce1ff7ac: **Notes**: White with vertical black stripes and yellow fins. Very shy; one of the dwarf angelfish species that is most gentle toward corals.
textos.8d5f2e9ecd58b0c3: **Notes**: Uniform jet black. Shy at first; spends a lot of time among the rocks.
textos.eed89adba728aa72: **Notes**: Orange with thin dark blue lines. Endemic to Hawaii; prefers mature aquariums with plenty of rock.
textos.9655cb4823ee449e: **Notes**: Orange with thin dark vertical stripes. Similar to the flame angelfish but more subdued.
textos.f7b486299982f2c6: **Notes**: Known as the “keyhole angelfish”: black with a white spot on its side. Large for a dwarf angelfish.
textos.af0a99a181114a34: **Notes**: Pearl gray on the front half and black on the back. Sturdy and a good choice for beginners looking to keep dwarf angelfish.
textos.daa31dd820c0d054: **Notes**: Dark brown with blue spots. Large and voracious; keep only with large fish.
textos.ade07ffafc06eeff: **Notes**: Bright red with blue spots. An ambush predator that requires large caves.
textos.07f9d1d03273d4e9: **Notes**: It has no true roots; it floats or clings to rocks. It absorbs nutrients very quickly and competes with algae. Perfect for cold-water and cichlid aquariums.
textos.d5f5929935a951d0: **Notes**: A relative of the common hornwort with thinner, softer leaves. Rootless; absorbs a lot of nutrients.
textos.9a7a55bc270c1257: **Notes**: Related to the water fern but with wider leaves. When floating, it forms large rosettes that provide shade.
textos.e07d4704ccd66b8e: **Notes**: A fern with finely divided leaves, also known as water sprite. It can be planted or left to float. It produces new plants along the edges of its leaves.
textos.157b1566f23adaf2: **Notes**: It lives inside a tube buried in the sand, with a crown of long, colorful tentacles. It requires a deep substrate.
textos.68d1e9fc21b0bf73: **Notes**: A small snail with a conical shell that cleans rocks, glass, and sand. One of the best members of the cleanup crew; it rights itself if it falls over.
textos.b77f0160c76b4942: **Notes**: Dark oblique lines, a filament on the dorsal fin, and a black ocellus. One of the hardiest butterflyfish. Feeds on Aiptasia anemones.
textos.1d046e7f5bb33bc8: **Notes**: A black ocellus near the rear of the body that confuses predators. Delicate in the aquarium.
textos.01816aa9ef7613d2: **Notes**: Dark body with white bands on the head and a red tail base. Elegant and medium-sized.
textos.e145b11d61645e72: **Notes**: A large white-edged black spot on the rear of the body, against a yellowish-gray background. Large and striking.
textos.fdff027e4bd79d13: **Notes**: Two black saddle-shaped marks on a yellow and white background.
textos.830b2b419602271f: **Notes**: Golden yellow with a dark band across the eye. One of the easiest butterflyfish to feed. May nibble on soft corals.
textos.269ee90eff138658: **Notes**: The largest of the butterflyfish, white with thin vertical lines and a yellow tail.
textos.d08707eaef81f95c: **Notes**: Pattern featuring a black mask over the eye and a black band along the back, similar to a raccoon. Hardy and easy to keep in a FOWLR tank. Eats corals, anemones, and other invertebrates: never keep in a reef tank.
textos.7cd95bd2c4a8fc13: **Notes**: V-shaped pattern of dark lines and an orange rear. Small and easy to feed.
textos.2b27564f157d0768: **Notes**: White with yellow fins and a dark spot on the dorsal fin. Caribbean butterflyfish.
textos.7ea08580381c94a0: **Notes**: Dotted vertical stripes on a yellow background, and an orange bar across the head.
textos.558fe411bf87781d: **Notes**: Yellow with a dark net-like pattern. Elegant, but it nibbles on corals.
textos.2b98819d33beb820: **Notes**: Golden yellow with thin orange vertical lines and a blue spot around the eye. Highly sought after.
textos.659775b65a093095: **Notes**: White with dark vertical bands and yellow-edged fins. Caribbean butterflyfish.
textos.1aa00640270f8fb6: **Notes**: Feeds exclusively on coral polyps; in an aquarium, it almost always starves to death. Purchasing this species is not recommended.
textos.94cc5196cda59adb: **Notes**: Diagonal lines running in two directions and a black band across the eye. One of the hardiest butterflyfish.
textos.cfadbfef7bdc4064: **Notes**: Scales with dark edges forming a net-like pattern and an orange tail. One of the easiest butterflyfish to keep.
textos.8502a5598f26f1b2: **Notes**: Known as the “scarf angel”: dark blue with a yellow stripe and blue lines. Highly sought after.
textos.914d6336d6040343: **Notes**: Known as the Singapore angelfish: light-colored head, dark body, and yellow tail. It looks like a butterfly, but it is an angelfish.
textos.838c4a628572c54c: **Notes**: Sinuous blue stripes on a yellowish-brown background. Prefers slightly cooler water than other angelfish. Bites corals: best suited for FOWLR setups.
textos.053048d6bfd8bc02: **Notes**: The most popular nutrient "scrubber" in marine refugiums. The mass of thick filaments captures nitrates and phosphates very efficiently. It is harvested by removing portions of the mass. There is no risk of sporulation. Amphipods and copepods reproduce among its filaments, providing a source of live food for the main aquarium.
textos.ce8999d03a6e664f: **Notes**: Mountain river pleco: requires cool, well-oxygenated water with a current. A good algae eater that does not grow larger than 10 cm.
textos.2b1e324a16bd3dca: **Notes**: A mountain-river pleco with light-colored spots. Cool, well-oxygenated water with a current. An excellent algae eater.
textos.2f5790ced390665a: **Notes**: Very large silvery scales and a pink tail. A fast swimmer and jumper: requires a long aquarium and a secure lid.
textos.cc16f926b5c91bbc: **Notes**: Cream-colored body with a dark “mask” on the face. Related to the Julidochromis genus, and just as fond of crevices.
textos.9b16f475f3dc4334: **Notes**: Related to the Julidochromis genus, beige with dark lines on the head and body. Care requirements are the same as for Julidochromis: stacked rocks with plenty of caves.
textos.28235b5ebb8e176d: **Notes**: Known as the “Malawi trout.” Elongated, silvery-blue body. A tireless swimmer that needs plenty of open space.
textos.d0cbba137597101a: **Notes**: Dwarf snakehead, blue with orange-edged fins. Suitable for medium-sized aquariums with plants and hiding spots.
textos.5d6c269ecf29a5e0: **Notes**: One of the small snakeheads, with fins edged in orange. Air-breathing: secure the lid tightly. Some countries regulate Channa species; check local regulations.
textos.5835ee0fbff96458: **Notes**: Known as the “darter tetra.” It rests on rocks using its pectoral fins, much like a goby. It prefers a current.
textos.16151c020d64fa92: **Notes**: Males are red with black fins. This species is critically endangered and is maintained through hobbyist conservation programs.
textos.1d841b5bc4f21bfd: **Notes**: Five black stripes and a yellow spot at the base of the tail. It has canine teeth and hunts small fish.
textos.da410374a5f23724: **Notes**: Long snout, orange bands, and a false eye on the dorsal fin. Widely used to control Aiptasia outbreaks. Can be finicky at first when starting to eat.
textos.433164dc6fc7f7ea: **Notes**: Bluish-green front half and red rear half. Endangered in its native lake; those sold in stores are captive-bred.
textos.966e4f4a9e9bae75: **Notes**: Covered in dark spots; swims with its head tilted downward. Peaceful and curious; a good tankmate for large tetras.
textos.2b62f7586ed9bcf2: **Notes**: Covered with fixed spines and a dark hexagonal pattern. Expressive; it’s best not to startle it.
textos.af71f48c376ece3e: **Notes**: Males are light blue with green iridescence. They crush snails with their specialized mouthparts.
textos.21ad3920cd13df01: **Notes**: Elongated body with blue and black bands. Small but very aggressive, especially toward fish with a similar appearance.
textos.e93b19281ea394d2: **Notes**: Pale blue with a black-edged dorsal fin; an albino form exists. One of the easiest mbuna to keep. It used to be sold as Pseudotropheus socolofi.
textos.16c3525aea91ba9c: **Notes**: Black ocelli with white borders along the anal fin. Sold as a juvenile, but easily grows to over half a meter.
textos.80e861188c3b2b63: **Notes**: Orange and white stripes and visible blue teeth. Specimens from Australia have more intense colors. Ideal for large FOWLR tanks.
textos.e28dc860beb1fc8f: **Reef Safe**: ⚠️ Use caution (it doesn't harm corals, but it eats crustaceans)
textos.a929311b61caa45c: **Notes**: Dark brown with a forked tail; juveniles are electric blue. The most common fish found among Mediterranean rocks.
textos.ccec2468af795cb8: **Notes**: Bright blue with a forked tail edged in black. Forms schools in open water above the reef.
textos.401abaaba52fa2ba: **Notes**: Known as the two-colored chromis: dark body with a white rear section.
textos.7d42e68e579c2c31: **Notes**: A small chromis with blue and yellow stripes. It lives in schools.
textos.449ad582163acbec: **Notes**: Iridescent blue-green; forms schools among the corals. Internal fighting will eventually reduce the group size if the aquarium is small.
textos.985ad1fc30d609ad: **Notes**: Orange with three black stripes. Very long-lived and social: it becomes stressed when kept alone. Prone to white spot disease when first brought home. Grows slowly but reaches a large size.
textos.0e69fd013fa1fe1d: **Notes**: Intense electric blue. Very hardy, but territorial: it should be one of the last fish added to the aquarium. Very difficult to catch once it has settled among the rocks.
textos.d24c14253ef38be0: **Notes**: The front half is blue and the back half is yellow. Slightly less aggressive than other damselfish, but territorial toward similar-looking fish.
textos.a64fb4f6ddea1e8b: **Notes**: Bright blue body with a yellow caudal fin. One of the least aggressive damselfish. Once established in its territory, it can make it difficult to introduce other fish.
textos.fa23bfc1a1af9322: **Notes**: Dark gray body with a white or yellow rear section. A very calm damselfish.
textos.59ff54fc51c0ad62: **Notes**: Deep blue with a black stripe along the back. One of the most peaceful damselfish; suitable for nano reefs.
textos.bbf0930146fa7722: **Notes**: Deep blue with a yellow back and tail. Lives in deeper waters; less common.
textos.bb9fb1a8c39e6ecb: **Notes**: Lilac-gray body with a yellow head and a black spot on the dorsal fin. Small and peaceful.
textos.063ca9f050db3353: **Notes**: Electric blue with a yellow belly and tail. Very beautiful but territorial; one of the last fish to be introduced.
textos.5752489e38f0d079: **Notes**: Known as the “peacock bass,” highly prized in sport fishing. It grows very large and requires a lot of food: for public aquariums only.
textos.5b5f99656aa3daa2: **Notes**: Greenish body with dark bands. Sturdy and widely used in behavioral studies.
textos.9cef209d0c86920a: **Notes**: Blue head and sides with a yellowish rear. Very hardy.
textos.0767fb05b1f0ad0a: **Notes**: Greenish body with a black spot near the tail and blue lines on the head. Very active.
textos.a53620bbe09262a6: **Notes**: Small, pink fairy wrasse with a yellow back. Ideal for medium-sized reef tanks.
textos.4c328fbac5735104: **Notes**: Males are red with yellow bellies. Endemic to Hawaii.
textos.166bdd60b3c912f1: **Notes**: A small, yellow and pink fairy wrasse with violet highlights. Ideal for medium-sized reef tanks.
textos.1b7b8ae9f1e5b7fc: **Notes**: Males are pink with yellow longitudinal stripes. Peaceful and suitable for reef tanks.
textos.e648d50f235ef1d5: **Notes**: Dark body covered with blue spots. A sturdy fairy wrasse.
textos.5d68fcc082b525d5: **Notes**: Fairy wrasse are ideal for reef tanks: they do not touch corals or invertebrates. They sleep in a layer of mucus. They jump a lot: use a mesh cover.
textos.bb545c8bbb42f1b3: **Notes**: Males have very long red pelvic fins and a pink body. Elegant and calm.
textos.8ec5c59e2ee1956e: **Notes**: Males are green with a red spot on their side and very colorful fins when on display.
textos.bc1d5cdb99670bba: **Notes**: Males have red heads and bodies with green and violet iridescence. Requires a mesh cover.
textos.d99b2b45a327882d: **Notes**: Reddish spots on a light background and an ocellus on the operculum. Sturdy and easy to care for.
textos.7bc3735defbc59e1: **Notes**: White with red spots and cirri on the dorsal spines. Small and full of personality.
textos.06786e540b73b161: **Notes**: Covered with red or brown spots on a light background. Hardy and easy to feed.
textos.511103f056b1dd2e: **Notes**: Dark body with red lines and cirri on the nape. Feeds on filamentous algae.
textos.c13508294798dc60: **Notes**: Known as cauliflower coral: a soft mass with brown polyps that retract, leaving it white. Very hardy.
textos.7963c24069734847: **Notes**: The only reef-building coral in the Mediterranean, with tubular corallites growing in clumps. A protected species in the wild.
textos.0a67133652a0c0c4: **Notes**: A colonial octocoral that covers rocks and walls. Very hardy. A good indicator of water quality: if the polyps do not open within a few hours, something is wrong. Some have a green or blue fluorescent glow under UV light.
textos.328d779c3f28c3d3: **Notes**: Dark, keyhole-shaped spot on the side. One of the most peaceful cichlids, suitable for community tanks.
textos.e3ea34f7adaccdf0: **Notes**: An essential part of the marine cleanup crew. Eats algae on rocks and cleans the tank bottom. ESSENTIAL: Always provide empty shells of various sizes, or they will kill other hermit crabs to steal their shells. 1–2 extra shells per crab.
textos.8c62dc138c3ecd68: **Notes**: A common red-legged hermit crab found on coastal rocks. It cleans algae and debris.
textos.d862091e0f2dfeda: **Notes**: Blue legs with orange bands. Part of the algae-cleaning crew. Provide empty shells of various sizes to prevent it from preying on snails.
textos.72177fcd10103eb7: **Notes**: Small snail with spines on its shell. Excellent algae eater in nano tanks. May escape from the aquarium: a lid is recommended.
textos.c156e5337f4e296c: **Notes**: A European loach that spends the day buried in the sand. Similar protected species live on the Iberian Peninsula: do not collect it from the wild.
textos.8b32744524294a58: **Notes**: A true freshwater pufferfish, with black bands on a yellow background. Very active; needs snails to wear down its beak.
textos.1759f19d25085c2b: **Notes**: A larger relative of the Amazon puffer, with black bands on a yellow background. Brackish water.
textos.f288eaafe264e099: **Notes**: The fastest and most agile goldfish. Very ornamental long tail. The red-and-white “Sarasa Comet” is one of the most popular varieties in Japanese ponds.
textos.7b786d0fa91e2feb: **Notes**: Long tentacles with pink or violet tips. Does not host Indo-Pacific clownfish; may eat small fish.
textos.9624145240861868: **Notes**: Shell with an orange opening and very expressive eyes on stalks. It moves by hopping and keeps the sand clean. It needs a spacious sand bed.
textos.21d6ce88bbcdb291: **Notes**: Males are deep blue with a white-edged dorsal fin. Peaceful; a good tankmate for peacock cichlids.
textos.8a63c62840095cda: **Notes**: Known as the “redfin hap”: males are blue with red or orange fins, depending on the location. Swims in the middle of the tank over rocks.
textos.5140ecfc1ee8a65c: **Notes**: Males are dark blue with a white dorsal fin and white back. They feed on plankton in the middle of the water column.
textos.2fba88baa11113cb: **Notes**: Utaka with an orange or yellow back and a blue body in males. Swims in groups in the middle of the tank; a good tankmate for peacock cichlids.
textos.0edbc32b152b53fa: **Notes**: Males are dark blue with a white or yellow dorsal fin and back. They feed on plankton in the middle of the water column.
textos.6283431418b46469: **Notes**: Scales with red spots. A larger relative of the splatter tetra, but it lays its eggs on the bottom.
textos.1f5f6f65236c5fe8: **Notes**: Its method of reproduction is unique among aquarium fish. It requires a tight-fitting lid and some space between the water surface and the lid.
textos.37953fb8a59c8420: **Notes**: Juveniles are orange with white spots; adults are greenish with black dots. Grows quite large.
textos.1f1c4f20a91ca953: **Notes**: Juveniles are red with white spots edged in black; adults are blue with spots and a yellow tail. It flips over rocks.
textos.db9f0867fc6a5b6b: **Notes**: Elongated body with a zigzagging orange stripe on males. Burrows into the sand at night.
textos.da1cee5a9c072b7d: **Notes**: Orange spot on the forehead and a black stripe across the white back. More delicate than other corydoras: soft, acidic, and very clean water, and fine sand.
textos.c4c35e74ffb3905d: **Notes**: The most common and hardy Corydoras. Bronze-gold color. Fine sand substrate is required to prevent damage to the barbels. Compatible with almost any peaceful fish.
textos.d1abceb56d2c878e: **Notes**: Speckled with a dark spot on the dorsal fin and a faint band along the back. A classic community Corydoras.
textos.64702eab70ee7b9f: **Notes**: Silvery body covered with small dark spots and a band crossing the eye. Very hardy and active.
textos.c32c2f1ec6676a4a: **Notes**: Light-colored body with a dark band along the back and face. Belongs to the Sterba's corydoras group.
textos.2e785bd4c842fa8d: **Notes**: An arched black band runs along the body from the eye to the tail. Slightly more sensitive to high nitrate levels than other corydoras.
textos.1453540ab8a7f1a8: **Notes**: Its name means “black mask,” due to the dark band on its face. It has a speckled body and resembles Sterba’s corydoras.
textos.ce44e78df4baa9b9: **Notes**: Thin dark lines along the body with pinkish highlights. Rarely found in stores but easy to care for.
textos.477c4d60750c1cc8: **Notes**: Long-snouted Corydoras, covered in dark spots. Peaceful and easy to care for.
textos.9b2b1b2a7cb558e3: **Notes**: Another member of Adolfo’s corydoras group, with a black dorsal stripe and an orange forehead. Requires Rio Negro-type water.
textos.0c8e76c2156ba081: **Notes**: Light gray body with a large black spot at the base of the tail. Sturdy and stocky in appearance.
textos.80af2dbe91a751e0: **Notes**: Uniform gray with a slight pinkish tint and light-colored fins, without spots. Unassuming but very hardy.
textos.8688b48dd42937ca: **Notes**: A pattern of lines and dots similar to that of the trilineatus, with which it is often confused.
textos.0aab5d3c11e332e9: **Notes**: A small corydoras with a black spot under the dorsal fin. Active and sociable.
textos.1f851ba6fb3b8d8a: **Notes**: Golden body with a black band extending from the dorsal fin to the tail. Requires soft, clean water.
textos.d95052c664576545: **Notes**: Very similar to Adolfo’s corydoras, with an orange spot on the forehead and a wider black band along the back. Prefers soft, slightly acidic water.
textos.82560094c82fb04b: **Notes**: A close relative of the spotted corydoras, also found in subtropical waters. Suitable for aquariums without a heater in temperate climates.
textos.80c7520b137fbeac: **Notes**: More elongated than most, with two dark lateral lines. Spends more time in the middle of the tank than other corydoras.
textos.4639e1427a2a7fee: **Notes**: A black spot shaped like a saddle on its back. Similar to the Seuss corydoras but smaller.
textos.bd558722e6b9361d: **Notes**: Copper-colored body with green iridescence and a large black spot on the side. Similar to the Seuss corydoras but smaller.
textos.3cd89b841b7653f1: **Notes**: Long-snouted Corydoras with a dark band along its back. Requires very fine sand for burrowing.
textos.79efc55ec7d71296: **Notes**: A small, light-colored corydoras with fine dark spots. Rare.
textos.66432c5385c86f23: **Notes**: Gray body with orange fins and a dark head. One of the most striking Corydoras species due to its contrasting colors.
textos.e19b760d8a3a420d: **Notes**: A small, slender Corydoras with a dark lateral line. Rare; ideal for nano tanks.
textos.fd16b64d21b762ba: **Notes**: Uniform gray with a slight sheen. Unassuming and hardy.
textos.ca2ae2d6c7064542: **Notes**: Small, with a black spot on its tail; it often swims in groups in the middle of the tank, like dwarf corydoras.
textos.1f321cbf1d375d4c: **Notes**: One of the three dwarf corydoras species, the only one that always stays close to the bottom. It has a pattern of brown spots with a dark lateral stripe. Ideal for nano tanks with fine sand.
textos.9ed620f9a0685e0c: **Notes**: Very similar to Sterba’s corydoras, but with a mottled head instead of a reticulated one. Tolerates warm water; suitable for discus aquariums.
textos.2826242873c6ff1b: **Notes**: Another dwarf corydoras that swims in schools in the middle of the tank. It has a black spot at the base of its tail with a light-colored border. Perfect for small, peaceful aquariums.
textos.2477b06996276c06: **Notes**: Long-snouted, with the same black dorsal stripe and orange frontal spot as Adolfo’s corydoras, which it mimics in the wild.
textos.c358c460b8e7dfbd: **Notes**: Speckled with fine black dots rather than lines. Much rarer in stores than Corydoras trilineatus, with which it is almost always confused.
textos.ae8109b5a9780c3a: **Notes**: Speckled body with a dark spot on the dorsal fin. Belongs to the Agassiz corydoras group.
textos.b51a43104b451474: **Notes**: Elongated body covered in black spots, with a dark band along the back and face. One of the most striking long-snouted corydoras.
textos.5ffa5fff3fd0b0f6: **Notes**: Black spot on the dorsal fin and a dark band on the face. Small and colorful.
textos.714de631d0f27dec: **Notes**: A dark, oblique band runs across the body from the back to the tail, against a golden background. Active and hardy.
textos.938901399bfe47a7: **Notes**: Light-colored body with large, rounded dark spots. Elegant and rare.
textos.4ed36fd6924a63c1: **Notes**: Known as the golden-green corydoras: metallic green body with a black lateral stripe. Hardy and large for its genus.
textos.1cba50ca82e117b4: **Notes**: A diagonal black stripe running from the back to the lower lobe of the tail, on a light-colored body. It is often confused with Corydoras metae.
textos.0740f2adafc7ecb3: **Notes**: Known as the “bandit corydoras” due to the black stripe across the eye and the dark band along the back. Light-colored body with golden highlights.
textos.bcfbd7a05d5b2769: **Notes**: Dark horizontal lines alternating with dots on a silvery background. Small and very active; prefers a slight current.
textos.d474632b9ef46ce6: **Notes**: Light-colored body with a dark spot below the dorsal fin and another at the base of the tail. Peaceful and easy to care for.
textos.b5cecf65503ef26a: **Notes**: It has a very long snout with an arched black band against a light background. It needs fine sand because it digs a lot with its snout.
textos.4b663a079fe27063: **Notes**: Known as the blue corydoras because of the bluish sheen on its body, which features a dark band. It prefers slightly cooler water.
textos.7f12ed1e13063d1d: **Notes**: A small corydoras with a black lateral stripe. Requires soft, acidic water.
textos.1d728d6fafd39234: **Notes**: Dark spots on a light background and a band along the back. Rarely found in stores.
textos.c322cbe11f11a0ea: **Notes**: Dark horizontal lines and a spot on the dorsal fin. Resembles the trilineatus.
textos.f9d1b10db5f79776: **Notes**: Silvery body with a black spot below the dorsal fin. Peaceful and unassuming.
textos.f8b8656bffa973ed: **Notes**: The Corydoras species most tolerant of low temperatures. Compatible with goldfish in moderate temperature ranges (18–22°C). Use fine sand to avoid damaging their barbels.
textos.0f84ae60b0d3440a: **Notes**: Black spots on the eye, dorsal fin, and caudal fin against a white background. One of the most striking Corydoras species for planted aquariums.
textos.3749d3dda9701beb: **Notes**: A large Corydoras with golden highlights and a faint dark band. Sturdy.
textos.260b884fbb37b666: **Notes**: Dark parallel lines on a light background with bluish highlights. Highly sought-after and demanding in terms of water quality.
textos.8fc4d0155d3f3c92: **Notes**: Light-colored Corydoras with a dark dorsal stripe and a masked face. Peaceful.
textos.6ffb07b9cf7a6d08: **Notes**: Its name means “many spots”: its body is covered with small dark spots with greenish sheen.
textos.e000a5cefff43d9a: **Notes**: Stocky body with dark spots and a patch on the dorsal fin. Very calm.
textos.25fec4893cced2bd: **Notes**: The type species of the genus Corydoras, covered in dark spots. Rarely found in pet stores.
textos.f35d58fd08cb93b1: **Notes**: Unlike other corydoras, it swims a lot in the middle of the tank in groups, like a small school. Ideal for nano tanks with shrimp. Use a fine, smooth substrate.
textos.1138c00d30044a63: **Notes**: Orange-copper body with a black, arched band across the back. Juveniles have a different, more speckled pattern.
textos.c249af24433da2d4: **Notes**: Dark net-like pattern on a light background and a large spot on the dorsal fin. Its pattern changes significantly with age.
textos.342ad602a3998958: **Notes**: Known as the "flagtail corydoras" because of the black horizontal stripes on its tail. Light-colored body with a pattern of dark lines.
textos.0f6b20487635c746: **Notes**: Black spots on a light background and a dark band running from the eye to the back. Hardy and easy to care for, a good Corydoras for community aquariums.
textos.f6569a8066d5b1c4: **Notes**: Long-snouted, with a dark dorsal band and greenish iridescence. Requires fine sand.
textos.851dd95966e58464: **Notes**: Metallic green body with light-colored fins. Related to the bronze corydoras and just as hardy.
textos.806ceca69212c73a: **Notes**: Copper-colored body with a large black spot on the side below the dorsal fin. One of the large, stocky corydoras species.
textos.8174b18050e0280a: **Notes**: Speckled body with a large dark spot on the dorsal fin. One of the most elegant and peaceful corydoras.
textos.d82456ec02e59600: **Notes**: Long-snouted, it resembles Corydoras metae with a dark band along its back.
textos.2171d4b14d116ce5: **Notes**: Net-like pattern and a black band on the back. It mimics other species with which it lives in mixed groups in the wild.
textos.6679210777aabadc: **Notes**: Previously classified in the genus Brochis. Metallic emerald green, larger and sturdier than a typical corydoras. Very hardy.
textos.24294f3b339073bb: **Notes**: **The only Corydoras that tolerates discus aquarium temperatures (28–30°C).** A pattern of white spots on a dark background with orange fins. Essential as a bottom cleaner in a discus tank.
textos.8b740dd628b6d268: **Notes**: Silvery body with black spots and a band running from the back to the caudal peduncle. Hardy and fairly active.
textos.2ce7719022c9d521: **Notes**: Pattern of lines and black spots on a light background. It is often sold as Corydoras julii, which is a similar and much rarer species. Hardy and sociable.
textos.2e3aace2a7efddb5: **Notes**: Light-colored body with thick black spots and an orange forehead. Highly prized by collectors; requires soft, very clean water.
textos.454f441dbe9b8dc1: **Notes**: Dark, wavy lines on a light background. Tolerates cool water well.
textos.5dbb96d892d95e92: **Notes**: A golden-orange Corydoras with a greenish head. Hardy, similar to the bronze Corydoras.
textos.fc232d58e790d4b4: **Notes**: Light-colored body with a gray head and a dark spot on the dorsal fin. Unobtrusive, ideal for mixed groups of corydoras.
textos.d423a657084138bb: **Notes**: Vertical black stripes on an orange-gold background. It prefers slightly cooler water than other corydoras, as befits its Andean origin.
textos.78e9fa30da488425: **Notes**: Copper-colored body with a black stripe along the side. Very hardy, similar to the rabauti.
textos.562707f51945c438: **Notes**: Small, brightly colored polyps (pink, green, orange) with tentacles that have rounded tips. Cold water and fine foods.
textos.e6cf7ff793a495b2: **Notes**: A small, translucent goby with a dark mask. It lives in groups that hover beneath rock ledges.
textos.3a66166902f49152: **Notes**: Checkered pattern and fins with red spots. Females can turn into males, which is rare among cichlids.
textos.d9a78a6cc47f644e: **Notes**: A dwarf cichlid resembling a pike, elongated in shape, with females having a pink belly. Requires water flow, caves, and live or frozen food.
textos.1260c9f6c9d27d5b: **Notes**: A small pike cichlid with an ocellus on its tail. The female has a dorsal fin with a striking ocellus.
textos.e6dd5b368bb25571: **Notes**: A pike cichlid with an ocellus on its tail and a dark lateral line. An ambush predator.
textos.fb9d38e3ab7ec7eb: **Notes**: Known as the silk-tailed tetra: males have large reddish fins and a black spot on the tail. They exhibit interesting parental care.
textos.c04bc10868a42873: **Notes**: Body with bluish sheen and dark spots. It burrows into the substrate in search of food.
textos.e0281d7ec5cfe75f: **Notes**: Long, thin, curly leaves that grow from a bulb. Very hardy: cichlids and herbivorous fish leave it alone. Tolerates hard water and slightly brackish water.
textos.d169026f26ceee50: **Notes**: A bulb with very long, ribbon-like leaves that float on the surface; suitable only for tall or large aquariums. Very hardy: can withstand herbivorous fish. Endangered in its natural habitat.
textos.48cf3b8edbeb45fc: **Notes**: White with black spots; very striking when young. Grows up to 70 cm and will eat any fish that fits in its mouth.
textos.05145d563af5e029: **Notes**: One of the few fish that eats black beard algae. The black stripe extends all the way to the tip of its tail, which distinguishes it from the false algae-eater. As an adult, it eats less algae if it is fed plenty of food.
textos.e740b16b0daae3e5: **Notes**: Obligate symbiosis with Alpheus pistol shrimp: the shrimp digs the burrow, and the goby acts as a lookout. Requires a deep, sandy substrate for the burrow.
textos.6f4286b12cb30bd7: **Notes**: Dark bands on a yellowish background with blue spots. Shares a burrow with pistol shrimp.
textos.184222967f1831e5: **Notes**: Known as the spotted goby: greenish with blue and pink spots. Shares a burrow with pistol shrimp.
textos.70bd6949328c6f58: **Notes**: Dark green, crinkled leaves with a wine-red underside. Forms dense stands easily.
textos.ddaad863f06f8374: **Notes**: Narrow, wavy leaves with brown spots. Tolerates current and hard water.
textos.b18cc701d0f48b9a: **Notes**: The largest Cryptocoryne, with long, cupped leaves. Ideal for tall aquariums with hard water.
textos.6b4446c65faf78fa: **Notes**: Olive-green leaves with a coppery underside. Like all Cryptocorynes, it may “die back” after a sudden change but will sprout again in a few weeks.
textos.df3aa4bfba805b63: **Notes**: Heart-shaped leaves with a reddish or purplish underside. Prefers soft water; some varieties are highly sought after.
textos.d562e3b476081c26: **Notes**: Long, narrow, wavy leaves, resembling crumpled Vallisneria. Tolerates hard water well and is ideal for the background of aquariums without CO2.
textos.5c37bf92a02e25f6: **Notes**: Narrow, light green leaves that form dense clumps. Very easy to care for and hardy.
textos.323f3662730938d6: **Notes**: Large leaves with wavy edges and a dimpled texture. Sturdy.
textos.4f1c24778fefedec: **Notes**: Leaves with spots and a pitted texture; highly sought after. Prefers soft, acidic water.
textos.042b18d0cdfe4f05: **Notes**: The smallest Cryptocoryne. Ideal for the foreground without demanding groundcover plants.
textos.c9820999513c91ed: **Notes**: Heart-shaped, light green leaves. Sturdy and eye-catching when planted in groups.
textos.c688d911f58421c7: **Notes**: Narrow, spiral-twisted leaves. Tolerates hard water; an alternative to Vallisneria.
textos.55f897cdd54496d9: **Notes**: Long, narrow leaves, straight or wavy. Tolerates hard water well.
textos.ceb81b30300fc73a: **Notes**: Elongated leaves with wavy edges, green or coppery in color. Very hardy and tolerant of low light.
textos.b3fe5e5086294cca: **Notes**: Green, lanceolate leaves with a reddish underside; includes the former C. lutea. One of the easiest Cryptocorynes to care for.
textos.fe184a014faf4c2b: **Notes**: Excellent for the background of a shrimp aquarium. The broad leaves provide a surface for biofilm. The stolons and roots create hiding spots among the gravel. Compatible with Neocaridina; for Caridina, it is essential to ensure the correct pH.
textos.973ca615e64e4fe3: **Notes**: A small, narrow-leaved Cryptocoryne that forms clumps in the foreground.
textos.103515cb91f6f514: **Notes**: An anemone that forms a carpet of tiny tentacles with colored edges. Very sticky; clownfish do not typically inhabit it.
textos.70537fc3d5a552e9: **Notes**: A small, yellow Central American cichlid with a dark band. One of the most easygoing.
textos.6bdc6af9d1c7ca7d: **Notes**: Body with blue or golden iridescence and a yellowish throat. Calmer than the common convict.
textos.4df32eae9dbbe8b5: **Notes**: An elongated, free-living coral shaped like a slipper. It settles on the sand and can move slowly.
textos.6b6706bdcc7dedf3: **Notes**: Juveniles have an orange-and-black wavy stripe pattern (“chevron tang”); adults are dark brown.
textos.32991380f85833cc: **Notes**: Brown with thin blue stripes and a yellow ring around the eye. Its comb-shaped teeth clean rocks and glass without damaging the corals.
textos.c4da372c534c889c: **Notes**: Brown body with orange-edged dorsal and anal fins and a white tail. One of the smallest and most peaceful surgeonfish, suitable for medium-sized reef tanks.
textos.112cadc551438189: **Notes**: Light-colored body with golden spots. Shares a burrow with pistol shrimp.
textos.58729eeafd8797bc: **Notes**: Elongated body like a pike with a pointed snout. Hunts at the surface; a leaper.
textos.439c21d3d5303cdb: **Notes**: It aggressively eats aquatic vegetation. Useful for controlling algae and invasive plants. However, it can eliminate all ornamental vegetation from the pond.
textos.c983a58b9567325f: **Notes**: Covered in spots like a leopard. Hunts by lying in wait among the roots. Peaceful toward fish of its own size.
textos.c89af0ead3833997: **Notes**: Grayish body with an ocellus on the tail. An African labyrinth fish that breathes air.
textos.2f769a9c330a41e9: **Notes**: Belongs to the Ophthalmotilapia tribe, with long ventral fins tipped with yellow spots. Scrapes biofilm off rocks; offer plant-based food frequently.
textos.20a03c1cdd0ca0fd: **Notes**: Males have green and blue metallic iridescence and very long pelvic fins. Requires a spacious aquarium with sand.
textos.b1c96f95e14cf7c0: **Notes**: A Mediterranean seagrass with ribbon-like leaves. Natural meadows are protected: use only cultivated plants.
textos.03e40da83d1b33c2: **Notes**: A solitary coral with translucent tissue that swells like glass bubbles. It lives freely on the sand.
textos.36f7a7c7a02da6e9: **Notes**: Blue and black stripes with a yellow or white dorsal fin, depending on the location. Feeds on plankton in the middle of the water column among the rocks.
textos.a191781485c5f68e: **Notes**: A small mbuna with electric blue and black stripes. Unlike other mbuna, it swims in the middle of the tank and feeds on plankton; it is available in several local varieties.
textos.b1daacb2d69657c1: **Notes**: An encrusting coral with small, round corallites. Very hardy; it usually arrives on live rock.
textos.7ddc26d9d1e33ab1: **Notes**: Black stripes on a white or bluish background and a huge hump on adult males. Grows slowly and lives for more than 20 years. Very majestic when kept in a group.
textos.9a2b96b0aea3efb0: **Notes**: A close relative of the northern frontosa, with six bands and bluer hues (“Blue Zaire,” “Mpimbwe”). Highly sought after.
textos.dfc38b594261ddfc: **Notes**: Shiny shell with tiger-like markings, covered by the mantle when active. Large and voracious.
textos.1c7bf22847a0c17a: **Notes**: An open-water cichlid that forms schools, which is somewhat rare among cichlids. Males have yellow or blue tails. Ideal for the upper section of a Tanganyika aquarium.
textos.01e5b106a7920ad8: **Notes**: Males are blue with dark bands and a yellow tail. An open-water schooling fish.
textos.3740128c6c70e78c: **Notes**: The only hawkfish that swims in midwater feeding on plankton. It has a forked tail and is orange in color.
textos.ecf43de720b9494a: **Notes**: Males are steel blue with an orange throat during the breeding season. They can tolerate water ranging from freshwater to water saltier than seawater.
textos.030fbf988b0282c3: **Notes**: The ancestor of the koi. Golden-brown with large scales. Extremely hardy. It digs through the substrate in search of food—it destroys pond plants. Suitable only for plant-free ponds.
textos.4f0923c6a07a9637: **Notes**: Koi belong to the Asian carp species Cyprinus rubrofuscus. The “butterfly” variety has very long fins. A large pond with good filtration is required.
textos.df848a528aa1325e: **Notes**: Pale blue with a large hump on the forehead of adults. Peaceful; should not be kept with aggressive mbuna, which will harass it.
textos.b199d4c32fb01210: **Notes**: A close relative of the zebrafish, with green and orange spots and stripes. Ideal for nano tanks with some water flow.
textos.0e57e30dc60cfccf: **Notes**: Pink and blue pearlescent iridescence that changes with the light. Very hardy and a tireless swimmer; needs open space near the top and a lid.
textos.f76dda71232afe83: **Notes**: A small danio with orange, blue, and gold stripes. It tolerates somewhat cool water and likes a current. It is fast and a good jumper.
textos.d84530486ab5d302: **Notes**: A large danio with a ringed pattern and long barbels. Cool, well-oxygenated water.
textos.92155c6dfa151d01: **Notes**: Violet-blue bands on an orange background. Prefers hard, cool water, like that of its natural lake. With plenty of vegetation and calm tankmates, it stops hiding.
textos.04e55dbbb2bfd172: **Notes**: Known as the Yoma danio: rows of dark spots and yellow highlights. Active and a good jumper.
textos.8ed262893b60c129: **Notes**: Two blue lines on a gold background. A tireless swimmer that thrives in a current.
textos.508cfec2a78da774: **Notes**: The hardiest fish in the hobby. Tolerates an extraordinary range of conditions. Ideal for cycling new aquariums. Jumps: use a lid.
textos.f5d273f0840f3fe8: **Notes**: Known as the gold ring danio: golden body with rows of dark spots. Small and lively.
textos.bbeacb02df2b38b4: **Notes**: Large red hermit crab with white spots edged in black. For large FOWLR tanks only.
textos.87eb60450a1d8a32: **Notes**: Males are scarlet red with blue bands; females are inconspicuous. Tiny and shy: ideal in a planted nano tank on its own or with shrimp.
textos.1c9103678eec8bd1: **Notes**: Black and white stripes. Very hardy, which is why it was used to cycle aquariums—a practice that is no longer recommended. Very territorial.
textos.456e0c8c3e518d36: **Notes**: Gray body with a white tail and blue spots. Less aggressive than other Dascyllus species.
textos.7f9747f0fd98f22b: **Notes**: Similar to the three-banded species, but with a black tail. Just as hardy and territorial.
textos.4a3c4027ac63a563: **Notes**: Gray with reticulated scales and faint dark bands. Hardy and territorial.
textos.20b97ad26301f6dd: **Notes**: Black with three white spots, like a domino tile. It becomes aggressive as it ages.
textos.9a5fb2a18ce4c98b: **Notes**: Known as the Siamese tiger fish: vertical black stripes on a golden background. Large and predatory.
textos.38a977ef90c301f9: **Notes**: Adult males have filaments on their dorsal fin and a black spot on their caudal peduncle. Requires a long aquarium.
textos.2b709f04d62ff6d5: **Notes**: Known as the “butterfly pleco”: dark and light bands and broad fins. Very flattened body.
textos.e10406d05caceccb: **Notes**: Poison dart frogs are the focal point of a tropical paludarium. In captivity, they are not toxic (their toxicity comes from the specific insects they eat in the wild). They require Drosophila melanogaster or hydei as their main live food. Tadpoles need small pools of water. Many species are protected: only purchase specimens from legal breeders.
textos.6b34efb8be59ca14: **Notes**: A small lionfish with two ocelli on its dorsal fin and cirri on its face. Shy and nocturnal.
textos.96d189af8bb025ba: **Notes**: A small, stocky lionfish with fan-shaped fins. It spends a lot of time resting on the bottom.
textos.11e4621cf4b6943b: **Notes**: A small version of the lionfish with fan-shaped pectoral fins. Its spines are venomous. Suitable for FOWLR tanks with fish of the same size or larger.
textos.9e42389560e94d67: **Reef Safe**: ⚠️ Use caution (leaves corals alone, but eats shrimp and small fish)
textos.584bce0e052c47e8: **Notes**: The lower jaw is much longer than the upper jaw. It lives at the surface, hunting insects. It is easily startled and may bump into the glass; avoid sudden movements.
textos.44c8c4b08389d900: **Notes**: Known as the Johor striped barb: several dark longitudinal stripes. Soft water.
textos.033bb9ef4dd9df06: **Notes**: Calmer than the tiger barb, with five dark bands on a coppery background. Requires soft, acidic water and a heavily planted aquarium.
textos.6caadef8d89b600c: **Notes**: Steel blue with golden stripes. Its speed makes it a good “distraction fish” for medium-sized cichlids. It jumps a lot.
textos.40950b9ff17c17bd: **Notes**: Very similar to the giant danio, with blue and yellow stripes. Requires a long aquarium and a lid.
textos.94afdbdaa3da977b: **Notes**: Extremely long, venomous black spines. A great algae eater, crucial to the health of Caribbean reefs.
textos.d914a98a46288c7b: **Notes**: Extremely long, venomous black spines that cause very painful punctures: be careful during maintenance. An excellent algae eater in large aquariums.
textos.96996b04a5299dd9: **Notes**: Brown body with dark spots and long barbels. Peaceful and suitable for communities of medium-sized fish.
textos.864f8e6da8029127: **Notes**: Known as the “flagtail porthole” because of the black and white stripes on its tail. Swims in midwater more than corydoras do. Peaceful and best kept in groups.
textos.0d2e252f8d9cef1d: **Notes**: Green with black spots. It is sold as a freshwater fish, but as an adult it requires brackish water.
textos.ecb7a7efb5ef356c: **Notes**: The most interesting brackish-water fish, but also the most difficult to keep with other species. Its teeth (which fuse into a beak) grow continuously: they must be worn down by eating snails, mussels, or squid. Keep in a species-only aquarium or with fish that are too fast to be bitten (mollies in large groups). It has a very distinct personality and recognizes its caretaker.
