textos.b971d4231a5f6b25: **Notes**: Checkerboard pattern and lyre-shaped tail in males. Requires very soft, acidic blackwater; highly sensitive to nitrates.
textos.138be773fd4e06f9: **Notes**: Checkered pattern and sword-shaped tail in males. Very soft blackwater.
textos.3aff45d14c958a95: **Notes**: Related to Dicrossus filamentosus, with larger spots and fins with red edges. Requires blackwater.
textos.8b4a3a2e0b7f062b: **Notes**: A Y-shaped, branched brown algae that can become a pest in marine aquariums. Few herbivores eat it.
textos.8435c00c3068e321: **Notes**: Thin, needle-like leaves with reddish tips. Sensitive to low potassium levels.
textos.90b16fe6725e9b50: **Notes**: Body is very laterally compressed, allowing it to hunt among vegetation. Known as the “Malawi eye-biter” because of its reputation for attacking the eyes of its prey.
textos.80e28564f1ac65fb: **Notes**: Elongated predator, related to compressiceps. Males are blue-green with a red dorsal fin. Keep only with fish that do not fit in its mouth.
textos.dcc74bcdd5e16a98: **Notes**: Orange or red branches with white polyps. Does not photosynthesize: requires daily feeding.
textos.dc1f209c40163893: **Notes**: It puffs itself up and raises its spines when frightened; it’s best not to provoke it. Very expressive and curious. It produces a lot of waste: it needs a powerful filter.
textos.7f31624f745ce7c6: **Reef Safe**: ❌ No (eats shrimp, snails, and crabs)
textos.881fb6efeb1ec724: **Notes**: Massive coral with dome-shaped corallites. Very slow growth.
textos.3db9382421ee41d4: **Notes**: Silvery with two black bands, one on the back of the head and another near the tail. Grows quite large; suitable only for large Mediterranean aquariums.
textos.c4dd06f78d57ebb2: **Notes**: Separate, round corallites, formerly classified in the genus Favia. Wide variety of colors.
textos.410f423edaa78a89: **Notes**: Tiny, with enormous pectoral fins and a tall dorsal fin. It moves by hopping across the sand. Ideal for nano reefs.
textos.dc19194a44415c47: **Notes**: Mushroom with radial stripes and spots. Easy to grow and fast-growing.
textos.bf7e55b13ae0db2e: **Notes**: The easiest corals for hobbyists. They tolerate fluctuations in water parameters that would kill other corals. They reproduce by fission. Wide variety of colors and textures. Metallic Discosoma are highly prized. In low light, they expand to capture more photons.
textos.b2e391234ee84ce4: **Notes**: A small, silvery Distichodus with reddish fins. It eats all soft plants.
textos.70947304c13583ed: **Notes**: Juveniles are orange with six black bands and are very striking, but as adults they grow to a large size and lose their color. They eat all plants.
textos.2773873d835bb9a7: **Notes**: Very slender body with red and white bands. Slow feeder; best kept without voracious competitors.
textos.ac416c167eb4fd9c: **Notes**: Large polyps with a green disc and short tentacles. One of the easiest and most rewarding LPS corals for beginners.
textos.3e0d4d29ec83b2b6: **Notes**: Yellow and black stripes with a red tail. Removes parasites from other fish; slow eater.
textos.da4059f26d142a2d: **Notes**: A yellow chain pattern on a dark background. It feeds mainly on crustaceans.
textos.0d9921452265971a: **Notes**: Black and yellow snowflake-like markings on a white background. One of the calmest moray eels. An escape artist: use a lid without gaps.
textos.af6da9828080dc68: **Notes**: Five-armed red starfish, an icon of the Mediterranean. Difficult to feed over the long term.
textos.1d476ec2894b78e3: **Notes**: Very vigorous roots: deep substrate (5–8 cm). Produces runners with plantlets.
textos.5f3e458bb762fe47: **Notes**: Large, heart-shaped leaves. It tends to grow out of the water with aerial leaves; trim it to keep it submerged.
textos.b048cc616754ff94: **Notes**: Large sword plant with heart-shaped leaves and prominent veins. It tends to grow leaves above the water.
textos.7cb412842b31c45a: **Notes**: Leaves that grow at an angle, almost horizontal. A compact and unusual sword plant.
textos.f053bb8a555983d7: **Notes**: Long leaves with wavy edges. A large sword plant suitable for the background of tall aquariums.
textos.5fcdf4cea43311c3: **Notes**: Young leaves are reddish at first and turn green as they mature. A striking, solitary plant.
textos.b22b0d2ff2bf13a9: **Notes**: A compact sword plant with prominently veined leaves. Ideal for medium-sized aquariums.
textos.d10a24726544b887: **Notes**: A small sword plant that spreads into lawns through runners. A good carpeting plant without CO2.
textos.9ce8e697a16d5fd8: **Notes**: Green leaves with reddish spots, like an ocelot’s fur. More compact than the Amazon sword plant and very hardy.
textos.518190190b672b22: **Notes**: One of the few carpet plants that grows without pressurized CO2. A good alternative to HC Cuba for beginners.
textos.cff4555767bf8bde: **Notes**: Long, narrow leaves, dark green or reddish. Tolerates cooler water than other sword plants.
textos.46f1ee09cd32c27c: **Notes**: A sea urchin with short, pink spines that burrows into rocks. A good algae eater.
textos.9161e735bd55cc69: **Notes**: It grows in sheets with “eyes” of contrasting colors. There is a wide variety of colors with commercial names. It prefers moderate light.
textos.480450d54d5b37e5: **Notes**: Thin, overlapping plates in shades of green or brown with small corallites. Tolerant and fast-growing.
textos.23a9d555db1f3b2e: **Notes**: Dark blue front half and orange back half. It peeks out from holes in the rock and nibbles on algae. It has a lot of personality.
textos.139cc8bb5d927b27: **Notes**: The front half is blue and the rear half is yellow with a black line. It mimics the venomous fangblenny.
textos.bc5288001b47adf5: **Notes**: Golden yellow and full of personality. Unlike other blennies, it swims in the middle of the water column among schools of anthias, which it mimics.
textos.90d71604c19db8bf: **Notes**: Black body with a yellow tail. A curious blenny that peeks out from holes in the rock.
textos.3ab102048ab86fe6: **Notes**: Light-colored body with dark dotted lines. A small, interesting blenny for reef tanks.
textos.d94c4de2aa9f397a: **Notes**: A small blenny with a spotted tail and lines on its head. Curious and peaceful.
textos.ddb6a0a713693557: **Notes**: Tolerates the low temperatures goldfish need. Goldfish eat it, but it grows so quickly that it keeps up. Excellent nitrate absorber. Invasive species: never release into the wild.
textos.f2845210e6a9dc9a: **Notes**: Translucent body that moves by undulating its anal fin. Communicates using weak electrical signals. Best kept in groups.
textos.f71ec017d4b54a37: **Notes**: Yellow or white stripes on a black background. A captive-bred cleaner fish that is hardy and effective against parasites.
textos.e954e0359cfa5a95: **Notes**: Yellow stripes on a black background. It removes parasites from other fish, which allow it to approach them. It is bred in captivity and is very hardy.
textos.fce4fc6305326af0: **Notes**: A neon blue line runs from head to tail. It is a very efficient parasite cleaner. One of the few gobies that breeds in captivity.
textos.0d164b82c89fb6b5: **Notes**: A cleaner goby with a yellow stripe on a dark background. Bred in captivity and very hardy.
textos.ff96ec8bff4d6254: **Notes**: Black males with bright blue iridescence during the breeding season. Ideal for heavily planted nano tanks without a heater.
textos.f6e4831f2785973f: **Notes**: Males are bluish-black with iridescent fins. Softwater nano tank without a heater.
textos.7d01ffee3ebc7972: **Notes**: A tiny relative of the sunfish, with dark spots on its sides. Ideal for planted nano aquariums without a heater, using only live food.
textos.59c09dc78634dda2: **Notes**: A tiny groundcover plant with round leaves, even smaller than HC Cuba. For nano-aquarium aquascaping with CO2.
textos.c269c0d14262d198: **Notes**: Easier to establish than HC Cuba. With CO₂, it grows laterally, forming a carpet.
textos.cdb3604b5840632e: **Notes**: Long, thin, hair-like stems. A larger version of hairgrass for the background.
textos.5d6952f72d52f3db: **Notes**: A very popular grass-like groundcover in nano aquascapes. With CO2 and high light levels, it forms a dense carpet. Without CO2, it grows more slowly and is less compact but still viable. It requires a nutrient-rich substrate and regular trimming to keep it short.
textos.5518dafff2e5857f: **Notes**: Very thin stems that form cascades when new shoots emerge from the tips. Ideal for adding movement to the background of a planted tank.
textos.97909d1b6172f00e: **Notes**: A cold-water oxygenating plant for ponds and aquariums without a heater. Introduced to Europe: Do not release it into rivers.
textos.050d82c36f2acafd: **Notes**: Its wavy, lettuce-like body stores the chloroplasts from the algae it eats. It helps control Bryopsis algae.
textos.ad41ce2ce8dd1a40: **Notes**: Males in breeding season display vivid blue and yellow hues. A very shy sand-dwelling cichlid that lives in large groups.
textos.776c86aae306a640: **Notes**: Tall body with vertical black bands. Cold, soft, acidic water; requires a drop in temperature during the winter.
textos.d6f6d34fb03328af: **Notes**: A small sunfish with golden and green spots and dark bars. Requires dense plants and a drop in temperature during the winter.
textos.e9995835efd178d3: **Notes**: Small pink lobster with purple spots. Nocturnal; requires caves.
textos.841ad62e42fb9af5: **Notes**: Tentacles with bubble-shaped tips. The most commonly used anemone with clownfish. It moves around until it finds its spot: protect flow pumps with a mesh guard.
textos.163424b6ac983740: **Notes**: Reddish body with thin dark vertical stripes. Peaceful African barb.
textos.39f1ccf3c198eb05: **Notes**: Black spots with yellow edges and orange fins. A very colorful dwarf barb.
textos.a6e6e5697d04ede3: **Notes**: Small reddish African barb with dark bands. Soft, acidic, and cool water.
textos.8b5e6bd8e0383b1c: **Notes**: Velvety black body with a red tail. Keep only one specimen per aquarium, with caves and driftwood to help it establish its territory. Extinct in the wild: the entire current population consists of captive-bred individuals.
textos.c33c7717a8c4903e: **Notes**: Bluish-gray body with all fins red; a pinkish albino form exists. Slightly less aggressive than the red-tailed black shark, but it’s still best to keep only one.
textos.a3c7598139947b51: **Notes**: Black lateral stripe with a gold border and fins with black and white edges. It is often confused with the Siamese algae eater, but it eats less algae.
textos.b7f0aa41566b0212: **Notes**: Black and yellow stripes and a red and blue flame-shaped tail. Lives just below the surface: floating plants and no current.
textos.9cfd1e89713ef3d6: **Notes**: Dark vertical stripes and a spear-shaped extension on the tail in males. Easy to care for.
textos.cf5ef29ddad1f63e: **Notes**: Known as the red-throated killifish. Males have faint dark vertical stripes and a red throat.
textos.fb056b084b41d15f: **Notes**: Dark vertical stripes and red spots. A robust surface killifish.
textos.e9ad9118f03d0afb: **Notes**: A surface killifish with dark bands and reddish fins. Peaceful.
textos.819dfc8861f76f74: **Notes**: Six dark vertical bands and a reddish throat in males. A robust, jumping surface killifish.
textos.10207f3d9275f349: **Notes**: Known as the cichlid goby, it lives in wave-swept areas near the shore. It requires highly oxygenated water and plant-based food.
textos.31bfbbd0e2cf0689: **Notes**: Elongated, snake-like body. Breathes air and escapes through any crack: lid must be completely closed.
textos.8e8161c677ad9d5d: **Notes**: Known as an “encrusting gorgonian”: a brown mat from which hairy polyps emerge. It grows rapidly on rock.
textos.35df54125c6561bc: **Notes**: Very long barbels and a dark lateral line. Swims at the surface and jumps easily.
textos.2e81406b9dea71fd: **Notes**: Males display bright blue and orange bands during the breeding season. A fish found in cold, flowing streams; rarely seen in stores.
textos.47188d444c818165: **Notes**: The only cichlid native to Asia. In brackish water, its health and coloration are optimal. Bright orange with black spots. They form stable pairs and actively care for their eggs. Smaller and easier to care for than the Green Chromide (E. suratensis).
textos.636d1c3175d9192a: **Notes**: One of the few Asian cichlids, green with dark bands and light spots. Requires brackish water.
textos.fdf707cde1a9b44f: **Notes**: Thick, blunt spines like pencils. Nocturnal; effective against algae, but may nibble on corals.
textos.aeddfd7b47f95e72: **Notes**: Photosynthetic gorgonian with brown branches and large polyps. Easy to keep in a tank with good water flow.
textos.5ff2e73bb8d23d9d: **Notes**: A Mediterranean gorgonian with whitish branches. It is protected in the wild: only legal, farmed specimens.
textos.8f86bf7abcf416dd: **Notes**: Tentacles with hammer- or mace-shaped tips. Clownfish sometimes use it as a substitute anemone. The tentacles have long-range nematocysts: leave at least 10 cm of space around it. They reproduce by lateral budding.
textos.070fcc4913499b7e: **Notes**: Known as “grape coral”: short tentacles with round tips resembling grapes. Related to the torch coral.
textos.623509a6fa6d8ab1: **Notes**: Known as “frogspawn”: tentacles with tips that resemble frogspawn. Leave space between this coral and others.
textos.929d6863f94681a9: **Notes**: Elongated tentacles with a translucent, torch-like tip. Some clownfish (A. clarkii) use them as an anemone. The tip can sting humans. Good fluorescence under blue light. Do not place next to hammer coral: they will “fight” with their tentacles.
textos.b55a0742a14da40a: **Notes**: Branched tentacles with rounded tips, fluorescent green or blue. Euphyllia are susceptible to “rapid tissue death” if water parameters change suddenly.
textos.87edc9f3a2d9b1dc: **Notes**: Euphyllia with short, thick tentacles. Same care requirements as the torch coral.
textos.694ca0f6e901247c: **Notes**: The most common pest in marine aquariums: it multiplies very quickly when there is an excess of nutrients. It can be controlled with mint shrimp, butterflyfish, or specific products.
textos.7525c51bbae3e001: **Notes**: Covered in red or brown spots. It feeds on coral polyps, making it difficult to keep.
textos.1b176ba0c5803db7: **Notes**: Elongated snout; males are dark blue with a light-colored dorsal fin. Rarely found in stores.
textos.de350e1159930b02: **Notes**: Two black spots on a golden body. Very beautiful, but it tears off the scales of any tankmate: requires a species-specific tank and a large group.
textos.3e476ffaa2b560af: **Notes**: A relative of Farlowella vittata, just as slender as a twig. A threatened species in its natural habitat.
textos.5180ba197c9620a9: **Notes**: Slender, elongated body that resembles a twig. It goes unnoticed among the driftwood. Requires abundant algae and biofilm: thrives best in established aquariums without voracious competitors.
textos.e79a331a1d947e54: **Notes**: Elongated, black, shiny shell. Buries itself partially in the sand; good cleaner.
textos.b21d5f084a2893e4: **Notes**: Massive colonies with a hexagonal cell pattern. The mesenteries can damage nearby corals within a range of 5–10 cm. They require open space. Very slow growth.
textos.137b02a76c2f4bda: **Notes**: A honeycomb-shaped colony with corallites that share walls and come in a wide variety of colors. At night, it extends sweeping tentacles that harm its neighbors.
textos.ed94fe1ba24f328f: **Notes**: The most popular climbing plant for the terrestrial zone of a paludarium. It attaches to any surface with adhesive roots. It quickly covers the false bottom and the wooden/cork back walls, creating a jungle-like texture. It requires high humidity in the terrestrial zone.
textos.84b31685cf982519: **Notes**: Forms very dense, compact cushions of tiny leaves. Widely used in nano tanks and detailed aquascaping.
textos.6e650b200abb712b: **Notes**: A Fissidens species with larger, feather-shaped leaves. Striking in rock landscapes.
textos.b217603eb1228dfd: **Notes**: A native moss found in cold rivers with long, dark green stems. Ideal for cold-water aquariums and ponds; it deteriorates in warm water.
textos.aea72c3afa68d0dc: **Notes**: Its elongated snout allows it to extract polychaetes and crustaceans from crevices. It feeds on LPS coral polyps and tubeworms. It is very striking due to its bright yellow color and black mask.
textos.a11ad4ad81a22db4: **Notes**: Its snout is even longer than that of its relative, the long-snouted butterflyfish. It is more delicate.
textos.06142944d41e8cc6: **Notes**: A fish found on sandy bottoms that buries itself when startled. Males in breeding season turn blue with black markings. Requires a large area of fine sand.
textos.a28d2475bfdc8e9c: **Notes**: Small red starfish with dark spots. Suitable for reef tanks; requires slow acclimation and a mature aquarium.
textos.ac7ad85f75ef9920: **Notes**: Males are red with blue bands and filamentous fins. This species is threatened in its natural habitat.
textos.171015262a62c4bc: **Notes**: Males are reddish with blue scales and fins with yellow edges. A semi-annual killifish from seasonal pools.
textos.10b02f346a6f2a46: **Notes**: Males have long filaments on the anal and caudal fins. Red spots on a bluish body.
textos.cf3b312747e2dc3d: **Notes**: One of the easiest killifish to keep. Blue-green body with red spots and fins with yellow edges. It jumps a lot.
textos.b21547ac72e35731: **Notes**: Males are bluish-green with red and yellow fins. Related to the blue gularis, but slightly smaller.
textos.49839c4d181bb36c: **Notes**: Bluish males with red spots and a red-and-yellow lyre-shaped tail.
textos.ffd0e00c50b94341: **Notes**: Bluish-green body with red spots. One of the easiest killifish to keep and breed.
textos.62ea1090acd5f3a5: **Notes**: The largest of the common killifish, with a blue body and red and yellow lyre-shaped fins. Very colorful.
textos.6d5394aa493a56c1: **Notes**: Bluish males with red spots. Related to Scheel's killifish.
textos.ab39773a53e5704f: **Notes**: Males have blue scales with red spots and a yellow tail with bands. Prefers cool water.
textos.cca1c3889dfd0db0: **Notes**: Greenish body with golden and red spots. Tolerates cool and slightly brackish water.
textos.aa04dfa9c8a6618a: **Notes**: Very hardy and adaptable. Excellent for paludariums with temperate or cold water areas. Feeds on insects that fall into the water from the land area. Tolerates a wide range of conditions.
textos.d74b684bf309a140: **Notes**: A solitary, free-living coral that is not attached and lives on the sand. It can move slowly and even flip itself over. Always place it on sand, never on rock.
textos.32730fca0151c046: **Notes**: Tubular corallites with white, star-shaped tips. One of the most aggressive corals: give it plenty of space around it.
textos.53e3ca566644284e: **Notes**: Feeds on mosquito larvae. Very useful for ponds without an active filter that have problems with mosquitoes. ⚠️ Invasive species in Europe—check legal status.
textos.c08571f5d7843b59: **Notes**: Dark body with a black spot behind the operculum and orange fin edges. A stream fish.
textos.63a61edd1e77ed01: **Notes**: Black and yellow stripes. A small biofilm feeder that thrives in a current and on smooth rocks.
textos.0c5eccebfb186dd4: **Notes**: Known as the “doctor fish” in spas, a practice not recommended for health reasons. In the aquarium, it is a very curious stream-dwelling fish that constantly scrapes at rocks.
textos.61a904eda2ac9ca4: **Notes**: Silver hatchetfish with a dark lateral line. Leaps out of the tank; a lid is essential.
textos.b3bebb97094bb42c: **Notes**: Silvery, with a keel-shaped belly. It can leap out of the water and glide short distances, so the aquarium must be securely covered.
textos.d300c3904ff06744: **Notes**: The male in breeding season has a red throat and blue eyes. Its breeding behavior is among the most studied in the animal kingdom. It requires cold water and live food. Protected in some areas of Spain: do not capture it from the wild.
textos.f0c91266026840db: **Notes**: Flattened body with light spots. Requires strong water flow, cool water, and rocks with biofilm.
textos.6068de478cc80b2b: **Notes**: Females are white with black and orange lines; males are silvery gray with yellow stripes. This angelfish is suitable for reef tanks.
textos.ea748d160c4fc489: **Notes**: Silvery white with black horizontal stripes. Angelfish of the genus Genicanthus feed on plankton and do not harm corals.
textos.cdfcd601a4b98bf5: **Notes**: Males have thin vertical stripes and a black spot on their chest; females are plain with a black-edged tail.
textos.9582b673aa045244: **Notes**: Males are yellow with black stripes; females are solid-colored. A plankton-feeding angelfish suitable for reef tanks.
textos.ca88b5724e7b5755: **Notes**: Males are bluish with black stripes; females are plain with a black-edged tail. Elegant and suitable for reef tanks.
textos.aa27743224962277: **Notes**: Specializes in biting off pieces of fins and scales from other fish. A curiosity only for dedicated aquariums.
textos.ce27c39e753310d2: **Notes**: High forehead and scales with blue and gold iridescence. Very similar to the sveni; requires fine sand and warm water.
textos.fa8bb88a4adbd307: **Notes**: Known as the pearl cichlid: covered in bright blue spots. Very hardy and tolerant of cool water.
textos.a33759a2552ef4b7: **Notes**: Known as the “yellow hump”: males develop a yellow hump. Body with blue iridescence.
textos.6d433ef4a0f64b7b: **Notes**: Males develop a red hump on their foreheads. Tolerates harder water than other Geophagus species.
textos.5451ba25eb75164f: **Notes**: Scales with blue and yellow iridescence and a black spot on the side. Spends the day sifting through sand: requires fine sand. Very elegant when kept in groups in large aquariums.
textos.7e07549ae623e59d: **Notes**: One of the few crab species that does not require saltwater to reproduce. The young are born on land as miniature versions of the adults. They are bright red-orange with violet eyes. They need as much or more land area than water area. A secure lid is essential: they escape easily. They feed mainly on land but drink water regularly.
textos.42a83f97279ac69e: **Notes**: Same care requirements as the Red Crab. Very striking dark violet-purple coloration. The two can be kept together if there is enough space and hiding places. The advantage of Geosesarma crabs over other crabs is that they do not require saltwater to breed.
textos.fd9b683637195b09: **Notes**: An unassuming Mbuna, bluish-gray with yellow fins. It lives where rock mixes with sand; it is more peaceful than most members of its group.
textos.a815ffd1f897982e: **Notes**: Silvery body with metallic sheen; some males have a black throat. Very peaceful and easy to care for.
textos.f5b01f0005232cd7: **Notes**: Adult males are bright red and have a high back. Females are silvery-green. Threatened in its native lake by introduced species.
textos.5507a9a691f55ee0: **Notes**: REQUIRES strictly overhead light: if light comes from the sides, it grows vertically instead of spreading out.
textos.c6ad5f19668be6d9: **Notes**: Yellowish body with faint bands and a prominent mouth. Peaceful for a Tanganyika species.
textos.713cab61d14b9074: **Notes**: It uses a “proboscis” on its chin and weak electrical pulses to search for food in the sand at night. It has a proportionally enormous brain. It needs fine sand and hiding places.
textos.3151ce99c18e85b6: **Notes**: Black and yellow stripes like a bumblebee. It feeds on the tubular feet of sea urchins; it also accepts frozen food.
textos.bc9b88be14daaa1d: **Notes**: A spotted bottom-dwelling fish with two barbels. Requires cold, clean, and well-oxygenated water; a good indicator of water quality.
textos.fa8cb9e7ba92149d: **Notes**: Yellow with thin blue lines on the head. It lives perched among the branches of corals.
textos.44a73dfd336b4a27: **Notes**: Green with red stripes on the head. Tiny and perfect for nano reefs with branching corals.
textos.f729346f00908d0c: **Notes**: Lemon-yellow and tiny. It lives perched among the branches of Acropora corals. Its toxic mucus protects it from predators.
textos.08887bdb5a0df02e: **Notes**: Greenish coral goby with reddish lines on its head. It lives among the branches of Acropora.
textos.c82386ff963c178d: **Notes**: Eel-like in appearance with visible teeth, but very peaceful and nearly blind. Burrows into the sand. Requires brackish water and food that sinks to the bottom.
textos.4bef05e671675988: **Notes**: A large goby with red lips and spots. Common on rocky bottoms in the Mediterranean.
textos.10394171e71b0dd3: **Notes**: Long, beak-like snout; males are bluish-green and females are brown. A tireless swimmer.
textos.dd7caf313c0afb34: **Notes**: Massive coral with polygonal corallites and short valleys. Hardy.
textos.6294e5b0aac00977: **Notes**: The extended polyps resemble 12-petaled flowers. Historically difficult to keep (“6-month coral”). The key is active feeding with phytoplankton and rotifers. Captive-bred frags are much hardier than wild ones.
textos.21fb32accc7f6fe9: **Notes**: A free-living coral with very long polyps, often green. Delicate over the long term; requires fine foods.
textos.36b5a748ce296430: **Notes**: A large, silvery Goodeid with dark fins. Tolerates cool water; a good choice for summer patio ponds.
textos.f825f4fb06ec11be: **Notes**: A purple, net-like fan that extends perpendicular to the current. Requires a strong current and vertical space.
textos.fbffc8ac2334b16c: **Notes**: Edible red macroalgae for surgeonfish and other herbivores, known as “ogo.” It is grown in the refugium to feed the fish naturally.
textos.4e5fe8228b0cba64: **Notes**: The front half is purple and the back half is yellow. It lives near caves and often swims on its back under overhangs. Very hardy and suitable for reef tanks.
textos.bd06667d35472918: **Notes**: Deep purple with a black line on the dorsal fin. A relative of the royal basslet, but less common.
textos.701a0792df9eba5b: **Notes**: Dark vertical stripe below the eye and a yellowish forehead. An attractive, medium-sized cichlid.
textos.268359106b4496d7: **Notes**: Also called the black widow tetra. It has a tall body with a black rear half, which fades with age. Very hardy; when kept in a group, it behaves much better toward other fish.
textos.9474df9ae2798edf: **Notes**: Males have a large frontal hump and blue lines on their faces. They benefit from a drop in temperature during the winter.
textos.5cf1943f100092e9: **Notes**: Males have blue and red stripes on their faces. Requires a cool winter.
textos.4561ab0128dd5d1b: **Notes**: Blue stripes on the body and face. Requires a cooler winter to stay healthy.
textos.0dc769f4d4945bc5: **Notes**: White rings on a dark brown background. Flat teeth for crushing shells; very peaceful around fish.
textos.ba3679c75be2fdf4: **Notes**: Known as the golden-tailed moray eel: dark with yellow spots. Requires caves and a cover without holes.
textos.fb8fb7946a1b250e: **Notes**: Sold as a “freshwater moray eel,” but it requires fairly salty brackish water. Prone to escaping: use a lid without holes.
textos.b9b7a4df439c3855: **Notes**: It is sold as an algae eater, but as an adult it stops eating algae and becomes territorial. It is not a good choice for community aquariums with angelfish or discus.
textos.35b1657f2144333b: **Notes**: Red with green stripes and two black spots on the dorsal fin. It burrows at night.
textos.8aa46483bd1f8529: **Notes**: Bright green with dark spots on the head. Buries itself in the sand at night.
textos.49b71af5bd36df2d: **Notes**: Uniform bright yellow color. Sleeps buried in the sand: requires at least 5–8 cm of fine sand. Eats parasites from the substrate. If stressed, buries itself within seconds.
textos.55f91b462c06c1ad: **Notes**: Black-and-white checkered pattern with a yellow spot on the back. Large for a Halichoeres.
textos.9ac1d1b3acb89d5e: **Notes**: Orange head with green stripes and a brown body. Effective against pest worms; needs sand to sleep in.
textos.3832bd2b6d6c3e35: **Notes**: Upper half yellow and belly white. Similar to the yellow wrasse, just as useful and peaceful.
textos.5454822fa8114fa7: **Notes**: Orange and blue stripes. Very effective against flatworms and zoanthid-eating nudibranchs. Buries itself in the sand at night: requires a bed of fine sand.
textos.e1b284f10c66ba16: **Notes**: Red body with green stripes and an ocellus on the dorsal fin. It burrows into the sand at night.
textos.30ad13dda9f7f6cc: **Notes**: Calcified segments shaped like coins or plaques. It consumes calcium from the water to grow (like corals). Very ornamental in the main reef tank. The calcified segments that fall off form natural aragonite sand over time. It requires a calcium supplement if it grows significantly.
textos.be410895b7ce49af: **Notes**: An abalone with an elongated shell and a very large foot. A great algae eater; do not forcefully pull it off the rock.
textos.7118aaa33a8d5675: **Notes**: Reddish body with irregular dark vertical bands. Active and peaceful.
textos.dcdaf54e14cb97eb: **Notes**: Males have a fiery red back and a blue belly. A Lake Victoria species preserved by hobbyists.
textos.1b0662b50f5343a2: **Notes**: Tiny, arrow-shaped catfish with leaf litter camouflage. Suitable for nano tanks with small tankmates.
textos.471d89f32f425e77: **Notes**: Copper-colored body with white tips on all fins. It lacks an adipose fin, unlike almost all tetras.
textos.7cc933b42c88e623: **Notes**: Thin, spiral-twisted leaves; very decorative. Forms dense clumps.
textos.0d12541597af8aa5: **Notes**: A solitary coral with long tentacles that resembles an anemone. It lives freely on the sand; gentle current.
textos.332411d8d9ff1a14: **Notes**: Thick lips that it uses to scrape off algae. It is sold as a small, pink fish, but grows to 30 cm. It eats soft plants.
textos.036209485bf1e593: **Notes**: Known as L200. Yellowish-green with light spots. Requires strong water flow and plenty of oxygen, as well as plant matter in its diet.
textos.49f68c3e7c39d567: **Notes**: The smallest and most sought-after groundcover plant. Without pressurized CO2 and under very intense lighting, the stems grow vertically. The DSM (Dry Start Method) makes it much easier to establish the groundcover.
textos.59cc26bd74471e46: **Notes**: The smallest and most demanding groundcover plant in the hobby. In well-equipped nano aquariums (with CO2 injection, strong lighting, and active substrate), it creates an incomparable emerald-green carpet. Only for advanced hobbyists with a fully equipped setup. It will not thrive without CO2 and strong lighting.
textos.fb395688d9a0a3ca: **Notes**: Known as “grass pearl” or Hemianthus micranthemoides. Thin stems with tiny leaves that form clumps.
textos.9bfffbdd6105ba4f: **Notes**: Deep red speckled with bright blue spots during the breeding season. Beautiful but aggressive: best kept as a single pair or with hardy fish.
textos.a8300b1fe99aa69c: **Notes**: Deep red with blue spots, very similar to the jewel cichlid. Same aggressive behavior during the breeding season.
textos.02c9b306a9a9f6c8: **Notes**: Known as the red jewel cichlid: deep red with blue spots. Slightly less aggressive than the common jewel cichlid.
textos.41433d6810aafc55: **Notes**: A small, silvery tetra with a dark stripe and golden highlights. Ideal for nano tanks.
textos.9fe59fcb31bfa485: **Notes**: The red nose is an indicator of water quality. It forms very compact, synchronized schools—one of the most beautiful sights in the hobby.
textos.9175070c556c06ed: **Notes**: A glowing orange line runs along its translucent body. Calm and very hardy, it’s an excellent alternative to neon tetras for beginners.
textos.f5bd7ff157af3960: **Notes**: Translucent greenish body with a golden stripe and a black spot on the tail. Unobtrusive and very hardy.
textos.f0aef0255f611cf5: **Notes**: Silver with a dark band at the base of the tail. Hardy and active.
textos.e249157ec7d56745: **Notes**: Known as “lighthouses” because of the golden reflections in their eyes and at the base of their tails. A classic in community aquariums—active and undemanding.
textos.96c60ad08efdaa37: **Notes**: Slightly tall, silvery body with a black wedge-shaped patch on the rear and coppery iridescence. Peaceful and a good tankmate for corydoras and dwarf cichlids.
textos.03d30b3e0df708de: **Notes**: The red on the head extends only as far as the nape of the neck, unlike the Bleheri tetra. Its color fades when water quality deteriorates: a good indicator.
textos.b8f2087d31633188: **Notes**: Its golden sheen is caused by a harmless skin parasite in wild specimens; those bred in captivity are silvery.
textos.392d9329bb9e2562: **Notes**: Silver with red fin bases. Peaceful and suitable for Amazonian community tanks.
textos.7e8fcb0decf021ec: **Notes**: Very elongated silvery body with a black band extending to the red tail. Very fast and a good jumper.
textos.17174853f3c2c0fe: **Notes**: White triangle on its side against a yellow background and a dark head. It feeds on plankton and is one of the few butterflyfish suitable for reef tanks.
textos.92c38e01cc88614a: **Notes**: A tall-bodied Haplochromis with a pointed snout; males shimmer with a metallic blue sheen and green highlights. Peaceful and somewhat shy; compatible with peacock cichlids and utakas.
textos.3c202daaab83d6f4: **Notes**: Very similar to Heniochus diphreutes, with a long dorsal filament. More solitary and somewhat more prone to picking at invertebrates.
textos.703b11894640cad9: **Notes**: Known as the “false Moorish idol.” It has black and white bands and a long filament on its dorsal fin. It is much hardier than the true Moorish idol.
textos.72e5aac1846411fd: **Notes**: Elongated predator with sharp teeth. For dedicated aquariums only.
textos.474cdc65c878cbeb: **Notes**: Covered in turquoise-blue spots. Sturdy and tolerant of cool water. Sometimes sold as “Green Texas,” although the Texas cichlid is a different species.
textos.ed36933b3d2ada54: **Notes**: The only cichlid native to the United States. Covered in white and blue spots. Digs and moves the decorations.
textos.c923caa57ca8806b: **Notes**: Tall, rounded body, resembling a small discus. There are “gold” and “red spotted” captive-bred forms. A good tankmate for large angelfish and plecos.
textos.172414b1a7bbe72f: **Notes**: A relative of the Severum with red spots on its face (“rotkeil”). Prefers soft, acidic water.
textos.441151974e2e8395: **Notes**: Elongated free-living coral with a central groove, resembling a tongue. Found on sand.
textos.de3a69ea77b5237f: **Notes**: Known as the banded anemone: tentacles with white rings. It buries itself in the sand.
textos.9566faa75dafe9ed: **Notes**: Long, pointed tentacles. They are often sold bleached or dyed different colors: choose specimens with their natural brown color.
textos.afac741604aee756: **Notes**: A large anemone with a brightly colored base. It hosts many clownfish, but it is very difficult to keep and often dies in home aquariums.
textos.3ea923beb8bd9803: **Notes**: A sand anemone with short tentacles that have magenta tips. Less commonly used by clownfish in aquariums.
textos.e1a6441f66ce2c4a: **Notes**: One of the smallest vertebrates in the world; males measure just 2 cm. Ideal for nano-aquariums without a heater. It will disappear if kept with larger tankmates.
textos.47229b0036686432: **Notes**: Grass-like, narrow leaves. It can grow upright or spread out as a ground cover.
textos.7fb3b74d646ebd33: **Notes**: It lives with half its body buried in the sand, swaying like plants. It requires a very deep layer of sand and peaceful tankmates.
textos.85a1f2acd99ee612: **Notes**: Very distinct black and yellow stripes. It was sold as Tilapia buttikoferi. Very aggressive as an adult; keep only with large fish.
textos.584a87160e2dd2e0: **Notes**: Polyps that open and close rhythmically, like Xenia. Grows quickly in aquariums with some nutrients.
textos.10532a39d8f1d86a: **Notes**: Transitions between ponds and indoor aquariums. Tolerates winter in deep ponds.
textos.50cd88171dd36d58: **Notes**: The European frogbit, with round leaves and white flowers. It spends the winter as buds at the bottom of the pond.
textos.b34a1c7fd9aeaa30: **Notes**: Widely bred in captivity and accustomed to eating frozen food. Slightly cool water, gentle current, and structures to cling to.
textos.56faf211d3fdb601: **Notes**: Requires a dedicated aquarium with little current, places to cling to, and slow-moving tankmates. Purchase only captive-bred specimens that are already accustomed to eating frozen food. This species is listed under CITES.
textos.83a6ce4b94013cd7: **Notes**: May be yellow, orange, or red with spots. Captive-bred; dedicated aquarium.
textos.0238700b39789160: **Notes**: One of the smallest seahorses in the world. It needs live brine shrimp every day and should not be kept with any tank mates that might bother it.
textos.2bfab37f8867d718: **Notes**: Similar to the otocinclus, with a light band on its snout. Cool, oxygenated water.
textos.066037f2697414d8: **Notes**: Greenish-blue with yellow-edged fins. Related to the queen angelfish, but without the crown.
textos.cfe69aa701025fc2: **Notes**: Electric blue and yellow with a blue and black “crown” on the forehead. One of the most spectacular fish in the Caribbean. Very large and feeds on coral.
textos.4d25c41b81f280d0: **Notes**: Yellow with a black rear half. Requires sponges in its diet; difficult to keep long-term.
textos.b18175a9440d84c8: **Notes**: Black on top and pink underneath. Cleans the sand bed; protect the pumps.
textos.0e144194e14325a0: **Notes**: It does an excellent job of cleaning the sand substrate. When stressed or dying, it may release toxins that affect the entire aquarium. Protect the pump inlets.
textos.9259155cc00b2dc6: **Notes**: A river loach with broad, angled pectoral fins for anchoring itself in the current. A spotted pattern that mimics rocks. Cool, highly oxygenated water.
textos.2d55ce6c2b573716: **Notes**: A fleshy, rounded solitary coral with spectacular colors. It was sold as Scolymia australis. Place it on the substrate with moderate lighting.
textos.8ccd70735393464e: **Notes**: Known as traíra. Sharp teeth and a painful bite. Only for dedicated aquariums; be careful during maintenance.
textos.6f75a930d8b41b49: **Notes**: Purple with a yellow tail. Very skittish and prone to jumping: use a mesh lid and keep with calm tankmates.
textos.e299236ee4e3f32f: **Notes**: Very hardy, capable of breathing air through its intestines. Grows quite large and stirs up the substrate. A good tankmate for medium-sized cichlids.
textos.fa80cdee73ab74d4: **Notes**: Small, translucent, with a bright green stripe and orange fins. Suitable for peaceful nano tanks.
textos.c8957ca831671c22: **Notes**: Known as water violet because of its lilac flowers held above the surface. A cold-water pond plant.
textos.e081f2427e1eebe8: **Notes**: Branches covered with small, conical protrusions, fluorescent green in color. It grows quickly and is aggressive: leave plenty of space around it.
textos.3b462871f396dae5: **Notes**: Round, floating leaves and yellow, three-petaled flowers in the summer.
textos.e9bcc129a8d2d69d: **Notes**: Round leaves on stems that grow in a zigzag pattern. Very easy to care for; it can also be left floating, where it provides shade and shelter for fry.
textos.39df8221a75d4640: **Notes**: Small, clover-shaped leaves that form a soft, carpet-like cover. It climbs over rocks and wood if not pruned.
textos.1cb66c019fb2ce1a: **Notes**: Round leaves resembling small umbrellas on slender stems. Very decorative in natural landscapes.
textos.58182ef836d2588a: **Notes**: Finely divided, aromatic leaves. It may release substances that bother delicate shrimp.
textos.dc76055811135b73: **Notes**: Sturdy stems with large, lanceolate leaves. It absorbs a lot of nutrients and helps control algae. Varieties include “Siamensis” and “Kompakt.”
textos.c3b955f6c1dfd137: **Notes**: Leaves are deeply lobed, resembling a fern when submerged. Very decorative when planted in groups.
textos.735e9b7bb7279f48: **Notes**: Narrow leaves that turn reddish in bright light. The “Araguaia” variety is very popular.
textos.a1ed7eba3face1b1: **Notes**: Olive-green, lobed leaves with a reddish underside. It can be grown as an epiphyte, attached to wood—which is somewhat unusual for a stem plant.
textos.dccfc88b3b4a79aa: **Notes**: One of the hardiest stem plants. Excellent for beginners and for absorbing nitrates.
textos.00cf95c63d0b0283: **Notes**: One of the most beautiful shrimp, white with purple spots. It feeds exclusively on starfish, so it requires a constant supply. Effective against Asterina starfish infestations.
textos.2b6d79e1792bf4fd: **Notes**: Black with small light spots and fins with white edges. A modestly sized pleco for warm-water aquariums.
textos.c3f22250a113db35: **Notes**: Known as L129. Irregular black and white stripes; cheaper and easier to keep than the zebra L046. Warm water with a current.
textos.2fbd79c941ead3a6: **Notes**: Dark body speckled with light spots. Nocturnal and cave-dwelling.
textos.630354c84e66eb63: **Notes**: Known as L102. Black with large white spots. Nocturnal; requires caves, oxygenated water, and food that sinks to the bottom after the lights are turned off.
textos.af9d9fb7ba238e7a: **Notes**: Dark gray with light spots and white fin edges. Related to the Orinoco angel pleco.
textos.5555a32064ccbc87: **Notes**: Known as L046, with black and white stripes. Requires well-oxygenated water with a current, warmth, and narrow caves. Export from Brazil is prohibited: purchase only captive-bred specimens.
textos.41652098df4ad80b: **Notes**: A tiny, fiery-orange tetra, ideal for planted nano-aquariums. Compatible with adult shrimp. It needs to be kept in a large group with similarly small tankmates to come into its own.
textos.4a2d65b44105c697: **Notes**: Pink body with a white and black dorsal fin, which is very long in males. Looks elegant in planted soft-water aquariums.
textos.c070deb2ccddd15c: **Notes**: Yellowish body with two dark bars behind the head. Tolerates cool water.
textos.f9bf282743ae8900: **Notes**: Metallic blue upper half and red fins. Sturdy and very active; best kept with fast-swimming, short-finned fish.
textos.d52846e16c0327e6: **Notes**: Translucent pink body with a black spot on the shoulder and a dorsal fin with a white edge.
textos.3a5da6cb77ecae1d: **Notes**: A tiny, translucent tetra with a spot at the base of its tail. Suitable for nano tanks.
textos.b7c90bede4714ac0: **Notes**: Translucent pink body with a black spot behind the head. A blackwater fish.
textos.ca81bbe8f94d1250: **Notes**: Bright red with a black spot behind the head. Very hardy, but does not mix well with angelfish, bettas, or long-finned guppies. In groups of ten or more, it spreads out the chasing within the school.
textos.3f5ee17dc7e61ba2: **Notes**: Tall, pink body with a red spot on its side, shaped like a heart. Males develop a long, sail-shaped dorsal fin. It fits well in Amazonian aquariums with angelfish and discus.
textos.89f43a70cf2ba6e7: **Notes**: One of the hardiest tetras. The rear part of the body is reddish-orange. Ideal for beginners.
textos.0fc12b8c8016dc17: **Notes**: A small orange tetra with a dark spot behind its head and fins with white tips. Easy to care for and peaceful.
textos.eb16c433b4df3d75: **Notes**: A small, reddish tetra with a dark spot on its tail. Uncommon.
textos.902aee48ab424ff3: **Notes**: A bright white stripe on top of a wide black band. More tolerant of hard water than the common neon tetra and a very good schooling fish for community aquariums.
textos.1962d33f46e85a6a: **Notes**: Golden body with a dark lateral line and reddish fins. Small and inconspicuous.
textos.1ae31dbe233f0b9c: **Notes**: Silvery with reddish fins and a spot on the shoulder. Suitable for cool water.
textos.acf27b7abda55e36: **Notes**: Dark gray color with metallic sheen. Adult males develop long fins. Stands out beautifully in planted aquariums.
textos.34ff216f1e6fb934: **Notes**: Translucent yellow body with a bright yellow and black edge on the anal fin. The color stands out much better against a dark background, among plants, and in a large group, where the males show off to one another.
textos.24a95cbfe4b702b0: **Notes**: Known as the red-backed bleeding heart tetra. Pink with a red back and red fins. More demanding than the erythrostigma.
textos.9ab7b9ee314c7584: **Notes**: Translucent pink body with a black-and-white dorsal fin, which is elongated in males. Elegant and peaceful in planted, soft-water aquariums.
textos.31344da6a3adf5ca: **Notes**: Small yellow-orange tetra with a dark spot near its head. Peaceful and suitable for nano tanks.
textos.63d7a7fca985df24: **Notes**: Known as the shoulder-spotted tetra: pink body with a dark spot. Related to the bleeding heart tetra.
textos.e19a4077dc8123ef: **Notes**: Orange-red with a black spot on the dorsal fin. Prefers slightly cooler water than other tetras and low light, with roots and dry leaves on the bottom.
textos.85d2971ec54b4fa5: **Notes**: Known as the copper tetra: bright copper-colored body with a black spot. Very striking when kept in a group.
textos.b5b5c2334095c43e: **Notes**: A black lateral stripe with a silvery border and reddish fins. Similar to the black neon tetra.
textos.4d1ced7dd8085ef9: **Notes**: A small, golden-yellow tetra with a dark spot on its dorsal fin. Very striking when kept in a group.
textos.e1849e3b20cf0ef8: **Notes**: A larger relative of the otocinclus that swims in the middle of the tank. It feeds on biofilm and fine algae.
textos.dfaafb3f43b53d7f: **Notes**: The classic pleco found in stores. It’s bought as an algae eater when it’s 5 cm long, but it grows to half a meter and makes a big mess. For medium-sized aquariums, an ancistrus is a better choice.
textos.563d3c9b42d35962: **Notes**: Known as the “chocolate cichlid”: its color changes from green to red or chocolate depending on its mood. Calm for its size.
textos.ec8d7393fc4cef5c: **Notes**: Males are reddish with fins edged in black and white. Swims in the middle of the water column, which is unusual for a goby.
textos.695e0aac081e5e80: **Notes**: Males have enormous fins and blue and black bands. A highly endangered Brazilian annual killifish.
textos.f16ca56769ab0454: **Notes**: During the breeding season, it turns black with a light vertical stripe, similar to Tropheus species. It scrapes algae off rocks.
textos.0783dc4b2f129328: **Notes**: Golden body with blue and green iridescence and a yellow belly. One of the most beautiful and easy-to-care-for Central American species.
textos.7b4b3a63988b68dd: **Notes**: Feeds on detritus from the bottom. Active at night. Large koi ponds benefit from having them as “bottom cleaners.” ⚠️ Invasive species in Europe.
textos.734deb2c29d23cf1: **Notes**: Males have golden highlights and yellow fins. A robust goodeid that thrives in a current.
textos.1f0fd98738a448c1: **Notes**: Males are a deep purplish blue; females are more brownish. Peaceful and suitable for planted aquariums with moderate lighting.
textos.33cbc6918ac0d7d4: **Notes**: Known as “rusty”: reddish-brown with violet highlights. A good choice for peaceful mbuna, along with the Labidochromis yellow.
textos.73b0140c1a28ba64: **Notes**: Males have fins with very long, feather-like filaments. Keep only with calm, small tankmates. Slow feeder.
textos.eb4389b7d6cc7f52: **Notes**: A shore plant with yellow flowers in the spring. It purifies the water and provides shelter for aquatic life. The entire plant is toxic.
textos.d8ce74675ee79616: **Notes**: Tuberculate polyps that resemble greenish fingers; they open only at night.
textos.babbc9b83d37113c: **Notes**: Known as the “zebra acara”: black stripes on a bluish background and a tail with a red edge. Calm and elegant.
textos.e662c543d876679a: **Notes**: Horizontal red stripes on a greenish background, like a flag. An excellent eater of hair algae.
textos.6d7ed2e3c82fe1cd: **Notes**: Brown body with dark stripes and fins edged in electric blue. Calm for a Julidochromis.
textos.717549ff0afca639: **Notes**: Black-and-cream checkered pattern. The female is larger than the male and dominates the pair.
textos.f7567c29214d857f: **Notes**: Yellow with three horizontal black stripes. Small and a good first species of cichlid from Lake Tanganyika.
textos.e43c13cc3c8a66da: **Notes**: Elongated body with four horizontal black lines. Swims close to the rocks, often upside down. Requires a rock wall with many crevices.
textos.c2174e943ae48488: **Notes**: The smallest Julidochromis, black with white spots. Ideal for medium-sized Tanganyika aquariums.
textos.49f1216dac96eafd: **Notes**: Green, cylindrical stems in dense clumps. A decorative, twisted variety (“Spiralis”) is available.
textos.26996931d495620e: **Notes**: Orange and green stripes on a light background. Requires a well-established aquarium with algae for the fish to nibble on.
textos.81c4bb8685c3cd69: **Notes**: Brown body with shiny scales and filamentous fins. Peaceful outside of breeding season.
textos.d32dfafc99d2c7eb: **Notes**: One of the few vertebrates that can self-fertilize. It can survive for weeks out of water on damp logs.
textos.59644ffb58de7a1e: **Notes**: Completely transparent: its skeleton and organs are visible. When kept alone, it becomes stressed and stops eating. It likes to float motionlessly against the current near plants.
textos.5a80d6497bdd3d7a: **Notes**: Velvety black; sold as a juvenile, but grows to 80 cm. Suitable only for very large aquariums.
textos.bd3a40211f9b0188: **Notes**: Mouth positioned on the underside beneath a fleshy snout, adapted for scraping algae. Males are blue, and females have a mottled “OB” pattern.
textos.9599ceca8703bce8: **Notes**: More slender than the fuelleborni. Males from many localities are blue with a red dorsal fin.
textos.318035a6a43dc9e9: **Notes**: Lemon yellow with a black-edged dorsal fin. The best mbuna to start with Lake Malawi: stacked rocks with plenty of caves and hard water.
textos.79cf187892e75eed: **Notes**: Light blue with faint stripes and fins with black edges. A peaceful relative of the Labidochromis yellow.
textos.1f8956c13e7884c0: **Notes**: Known as “red top hongi”: males are blue with orange upper bodies, and females are orange. This species has not yet been formally described.
textos.aaa1c16d910266d4: **Notes**: A small, light-colored mbuna with faint banding. Peaceful for a Malawi cichlid.
textos.0b363dd17c53c3e4: **Notes**: A small Mbuna that uses its fine teeth to nibble on invertebrates among the rocks. Bluish males with dark bars; a good choice for peaceful Malawi aquariums.
textos.c914a2d7578f555f: **Notes**: Known as the “red dottyback”: red with an ocellus on the operculum. Large and aggressive.
textos.4d89fc331e6d16a5: **Notes**: It removes parasites from fish in the wild, but in an aquarium it almost always starves to death. Purchasing this species is not recommended; captive-bred cleaner gobies are the alternative.
textos.0310457f64085ad3: **Notes**: Yellow, box-shaped body with two “horns” above the eyes. Like the boxfish, it releases dangerous toxins if it becomes stressed or dies. Keep only with peaceful tankmates.
textos.74171519b4ddebd6: **Notes**: A small, bluish lampeye from the African Great Lakes. Tolerates hard water.
textos.e46ee636be5d281d: **Notes**: Small, translucent African tetra with golden highlights and red-edged fins. Jumps; requires a lid.
textos.e248ed3ceb919fce: **Notes**: Greenish body with blue lines on the face. Peaceful, a good tankmate for tetras.
textos.4176ee32caaba241: **Notes**: A dwarf cichlid with a greenish face and blue highlights, known as the “smiling acara” because of the shape of its mouth. Very peaceful, suitable for Amazonian community tanks.
textos.472ffbcea03f35a1: **Notes**: Known as the red-bellied acara: during the breeding season, it turns red and black. Peaceful and easy to care for.
textos.00cdd9991ab0c861: **Notes**: A relative of the Cryptocoryne genus with reddish or pinkish leaves (“Red”). Very slow-growing but eye-catching.
textos.c42894b67f51aadd: **Notes**: Blue males with red bands and white-edged fins. A jumper; use a tight-fitting lid.
textos.5d550f331ded2774: **Notes**: The largest killifish, with silvery-blue scales. An ideal schooling fish for the upper zone of a Tanganyika aquarium.
textos.29f6ddc1cc3480bd: **Notes**: Elongated, dark body with a hump on males. A riverine relative of the Lake Tanganyika Lamprologus.
textos.1dbf8cc6312f2860: **Notes**: A shell cichlid covered with light-colored spots resembling pearls. It lives in colonies on beds of shells.
textos.877bf023792822c0: **Notes**: A small shell-dwelling cichlid with large eyes, also available in a gold form. Each pair needs several shells and sand to bury them as they like.
textos.888cb55787ef16fc: **Notes**: A shell-dwelling species with fins that are finely striped with yellow and brown. The male usually has several females, each in its own shell.
textos.c9012fa6b9966a9e: **Notes**: A shell-dwelling cichlid with dark bands on the males. Requires shells and fine sand.
textos.5b489ea158e633b0: **Notes**: Brown pleco with bristles on its cheeks. A good algae eater of moderate size.
textos.2cd6981e9b004079: **Notes**: Green freshwater pufferfish with a lateral ocellus. Very territorial; requires its own tank.
textos.8546e4e873b9a30a: **Notes**: Tiny floating leaves that cover the surface within days. It absorbs a lot of nitrates, but it’s almost impossible to remove once established, and it blocks light from reaching other plants.
textos.b3d169c5a0d55342: **Notes**: An elongated lamprologus with a pattern of dark spots. It preys on small fish and fiercely defends its spawn; requires robust tankmates.
textos.a4db5208383b6c73: **Notes**: Elongated body covered with golden spots. A predator; keep only with fish of its own size.
textos.e75337b455ebab75: **Notes**: A brown-speckled sand loach, unobtrusive and very useful as a bottom-dwelling cleaner. It needs a fine substrate in which to burrow.
textos.8228364acfd18718: **Notes**: A spotted loach that burrows into the sand. Very hardy.
textos.4f57bf352afb7592: **Notes**: A prehistoric fish with hard scales and a long, toothed snout. Suitable only for very large aquariums.
textos.72a7539a512e1fea: **Notes**: Known as L007 and L029. Black with white spots and long teeth that it uses to eat snails. It does not eat algae.
textos.0ee7affb48a3e0cf: **Notes**: Known as L172. Pale yellow with dark spots. Smaller than other vampire plecos and prized by collectors.
textos.b35907b46c580a56: **Notes**: Known as L264. Gray with light spots and elongated teeth. Eats snails and meat, but not algae.
textos.b65c968bf85db0a7: **Notes**: Vertical black stripes on a yellow background. Grows very large and destroys plants. Jumps.
textos.f5cb885c0daa6ac0: **Notes**: Compact colonies of polygonal corallites in a wide variety of colors. Easy to care for and eye-catching.
textos.add8974be33c5b37: **Notes**: Known as “stringy moss”: thin, light green stems that sway with the current. Grows quickly.
textos.b1561cbb9bdb297a: **Notes**: Narrow, sinuous grooves resembling a brain. Slow-growing and hardy.
textos.96ff1e24607e3df4: **Notes**: Low-light SPS—unusual for this category. Forms thin, laminar plates or cup-shaped structures. Lives in deep areas of the reef. Does not require the intense lighting needed by Acropora corals. More tolerant of variations in water parameters. Ideal for lower areas of a home reef.
textos.63a2348f90b32889: **Notes**: Known as “sunbleak”: a silvery schooling fish for cold-water ponds.
textos.6a225afadcab6653: **Notes**: Known as the golden orfe. An orange pond fish that swims in fast-moving schools near the surface. It requires plenty of oxygen, especially in the summer.
textos.fa5d68d22605e7d7: **Notes**: Pointed head; males are bluish-green with reddish fins.
textos.99ef4fe4578e08b4: **Notes**: Small, spatula-shaped leaves that form a dense carpet. Slower-growing than other groundcover plants but very decorative.
textos.7334ef2288b93db9: **Notes**: A ground-covering plant with spatula-shaped leaves, lighter in color than Lilaeopsis brasiliensis.
textos.ef50960aff80ae9b: **Notes**: Red mantle with tentacles and electric flashes. Very striking, but it usually starves without an abundance of phytoplankton.
textos.d27f0cfdb852e08b: **Notes**: Males have blue and yellow iridescence with black bands. They are voracious algae eaters. Endemic to Jamaica and rarely found in stores.
textos.86105b744cd009a2: **Notes**: Known as the black-banded limia: males have a high back and dark vertical bands. It feeds on algae.
textos.ec7be517318b91a9: **Notes**: Males have golden and blue iridescence and yellow fins with black edges. Good algae eater.
textos.d161db5577ebc752: **Notes**: Known as Amazon frogbit. It has round, floating leaves and long roots where fry can take shelter. It dislikes condensation on its leaves, so leave some ventilation under the lid. In some countries, it is regulated as an invasive species: never release it into the wild.
textos.76c718206e9efbce: **Notes**: Pink or violet leaves in good light, with a citrusy scent; also used as an herb in Vietnamese cuisine.
textos.495a4ee09c3bf92a: **Notes**: Very easy to care for, with thin, light green leaves. A good plant for the background of community aquariums without CO2.
textos.639522f2dfe9a694: **Notes**: Leaves arranged in whorls with purple hues on the upper surface. Elegant and less common.
textos.58a51be4886e91ab: **Notes**: Thin leaves arranged in whorls with reddish hues. Grows leaning toward the light.
textos.3e65b45e4c406e08: **Notes**: Very thin leaves arranged in whorls, similar to Cabomba but much easier to care for. It absorbs nutrients quickly and helps control algae in new aquariums.
textos.66c26da3a5648732: **Notes**: A tiny, entirely aquatic crab that lives among the roots of floating plants. Suitable for nano tanks with shrimp and very small fish.
textos.0253c56738e2f1ee: **Notes**: Deep blue and very striking, but delicate: it requires very slow acclimation using the drip method and a large, established aquarium with plenty of rock.
textos.7057822b26db88f0: **Notes**: Small, round leaves; the “Variegata” variety has a white center. Very easy to care for.
textos.c67cdec1e5ebeaab: **Notes**: Similar to the Ranchu but with a more prominent hood covering the cheeks. The Chinese equivalent of the Japanese Ranchu.
textos.4b1be1e764c062fb: **Notes**: Known as the “Swissguard basslet”: red and yellow stripes. Lives hidden among crevices.
textos.674d9144835b5e1e: **Notes**: Jaguar-like spots. Nocturnal and peaceful with medium-sized fish.
textos.201cc423d0a2490e: **Notes**: Conical shell with star-shaped tips. Effective at removing algae from glass and rocks.
textos.d645f932e1a19469: **Notes**: A soft coral with a tree-like branching structure, in shades of gray or brown. It grows quite large.
textos.b74c97a33a11056e: **Notes**: Oval leaves on long petioles and small white or pink flowers. Very hardy.
textos.91aa71a902ec3c3a: **Notes**: Green leaves with reddish undersides. Out of water, it produces red flowers; the “Mini” variety is ideal for the foreground.
textos.2a0e669b5ed73245: **Notes**: It is recognized by its enormous lips, which it uses to pull snails and shrimp off rocks. Suitable only for public or large aquariums.
textos.b055ba0b1f507719: **Notes**: Fleshy, cup-shaped corallites on stalks. Wide variety of colors.
textos.b8831edfaaafb8cb: **Notes**: Massive coral with large, fleshy polyps: green, red, brown, blue. Very hardy. Can be placed on the substrate in low-light conditions. Responds very well to nighttime feeding with mysis. Very suitable for reef beginners.
textos.bac3f13da4e46733: **Notes**: Leathery with thick, finger-like lobes. Very hardy; releases substances that affect other corals.
textos.32bd8287f54ae402: **Notes**: Similar to Sarcophyton but lobed or finger-like. It also releases terpenoids. Very fine, feathery polyps when extended.
textos.5de279e1b7abb37b: **Notes**: Juvenile form of a fern that resembles a moss with lobed leaves. Very hardy; perfect for shrimp and low-light nano tanks.
textos.d0c7f0d6ab87f906: **Notes**: An elongated, sand-colored Loricaria that partially buries itself. The male carries the eggs attached to his lower lip.
textos.24cc694b29a5769a: **Notes**: A small black goby with a large white spot on its head. It lives alongside the pistol shrimp Alpheus rubromaculatus.
textos.8ad8409142561434: **Notes**: Males have blue and red fins and a dark lateral line. Suitable for aquariums without a heater.
textos.78cafc559e20b342: **Notes**: Needle-like leaves that turn a coppery red in bright light. Adds subtle texture and color to CO2-enriched planted tanks.
textos.dd10989e904e3e13: **Notes**: Small, rounded leaves with coppery hues. A compact Ludwigia.
textos.64dd0d280caf60b1: **Notes**: Narrow, wine-red leaves. Easier than the 'Inclinata' variety to achieve intense red hues.
textos.dc716bfd96b08895: **Notes**: Deep red or orange leaves; highly sought after in its “Cuba” and “Pantanal” varieties. Demanding in terms of CO2 and lighting.
textos.b069979d86f1ae3d: **Notes**: Oval leaves in shades of pink or copper. Grows upright or creeping, depending on the light.
textos.85d4069537cb1e02: **Notes**: Rounded leaves with a deep red color when provided with good light and iron. The “Super Red” variety is one of the easiest red varieties to grow. It also thrives in ponds.
textos.e327bcda1a5c0279: **Notes**: Leaves are green on top and reddish on the underside. Under intense light, the upper leaves turn reddish-orange.
textos.8e0844200bf9293c: **Notes**: Forms mosaic-like rosettes of red and green leaves on the surface. Looks spectacular in open aquariums or patio ponds in the summer.
textos.b08022ee08327574: **Notes**: Rounded leaves with a network of reddish veins. A rare and highly decorative stemmed plant.
textos.9a4288678951d355: **Notes**: It has a small anemone on each claw, like a cheerleader's pom-poms, and uses them to defend itself and catch food.
textos.b21a1bac2127a63f: **Notes**: A large snail with a pointed shell found in European ponds. Useful in ponds, but it devours tender aquarium plants.
textos.c7d630b2f042d4b4: **Notes**: The best parasite cleaner for marine aquariums. The fish assume “submissive postures” (fins spread, gills open) to be cleaned. The white dorsal stripe with red spots is characteristic. A must-have for any reef tank.
textos.a3176503fa9eb329: **Notes**: Very similar to the mint shrimp, with red stripes. Effective against Aiptasia; often sold under that name.
textos.b2562c8bc0b02af5: **Notes**: Bright red with white spots. Strictly nocturnal: rarely seen during the day. Requires caves and deep hiding places. Becomes somewhat less shy when kept in pairs.
textos.03a7f4fe5d9f3ba5: **Notes**: Very similar to the Indo-Pacific cleaner shrimp, with a white line along the back that does not extend all the way to the tail.
textos.bbb440ee8a25d3ec: **Notes**: Thin red stripes on a translucent body. Mediterranean cleaner shrimp, ideal for cold-water aquariums.
textos.73f008e54a8af125: **Notes**: Translucent with red stripes. Widely used to control Aiptasia infestations. When well-fed, it loses interest in them.
textos.e19b9cedfdc3e655: **Notes**: Short spines of various colors (green, white, purple). It covers itself with shells and debris.
textos.e8e9c8f19437e46a: **Notes**: Magenta flower spikes in summer that attract pollinators. Native to Europe (invasive in the Americas).
textos.baff66e133be92d5: **Notes**: Bright red with electric blue stripes. Cold-water fish: it does not survive long in a tropical reef tank.
textos.0cee87f6ff532855: **Notes**: A translucent shrimp with short claws; very hardy and easy to breed.
textos.3af7850244749c5b: **Notes**: A large prawn with very long blue claws in males. Nocturnal predator: only in a dedicated aquarium or with large, fast-swimming fish.
textos.c9a7ddc1d4fb1221: **Notes**: A sand anemone with a reddish base and long tentacles. It buries itself in the substrate; somewhat easier to care for than other clownfish anemones.
textos.a6ac2762c0fdf69c: **Notes**: Ocellations at the base of the dorsal fin and a brown body with stripes. It burrows into fine sand.
textos.b75b1a1b36f7afc7: **Notes**: It burrows into the sand, leaving only its eyes and snout exposed, with striking ocelli near its tail. It requires fine sand—never gravel—and a tightly fitting lid.
textos.fbf6c67df63ad5a2: **Notes**: Orange with blue spots. Like all leopard wrasse, it requires a well-established aquarium with microfauna.
textos.bb49f2e82b43e84a: **Notes**: Covered in spots like a leopard. Delicate upon arrival: requires a well-established aquarium with plenty of live rock and sand for it to burrow into at night.
textos.3636271b3968f324: **Notes**: One of the first ornamental fish brought to Europe (17th century). Extremely hardy. Tolerates cold water (down to 15°C), poor water quality, and paludarium conditions. Breathes atmospheric air. A good fish for paludariums in temperate climates. Aggressive toward other labyrinth fish and long-finned fish.
textos.246cb7c2de82eb02: **Notes**: A relative of the common paradise fish, bluish-black in color with red-edged fins. It tolerates cool water and is very hardy.
textos.6f0ba67e7c70f1d2: **Notes**: It produces electric shocks of several hundred volts. It must be kept alone and requires great caution during maintenance.
textos.02ef1e8c98af5cef: **Notes**: Small labyrinth fish with long fins edged in blue. Endangered in its natural habitat; requires a calm, dimly lit aquarium.
textos.ce69eefb12daeb34: **Notes**: Translucent yellow body with a blue line and fins with black and yellow filaments. Hard water and a slight current.
textos.e6d0e7f2ed82e432: **Notes**: An aquatic fern that, when submerged, produces loose leaves that form a carpet-like mat; when growing above water, it forms four-leaf clovers. A tolerant groundcover suitable for beginners.
textos.495123a327ce6f6d: **Notes**: An aquatic fern with leaves resembling clovers, ranging from one to four leaflets. A groundcover plant tolerant of low light, though it grows slowly at first.
textos.aad19ddefa1ae68e: **Notes**: Aquatic fern with leaves composed of four leaflets. When submerged, it forms a carpet; in a pond, the leaves float.
textos.9bc5c45130f7e8fe: **Notes**: Black with bright red lines and spots. Burrows into fine sand; grows quite large and requires a lid without holes.
textos.a625d04a039d60c7: **Notes**: Very thin leaves on delicate stems, yellowish-green. Requires soft water.
textos.c1cbbc2b1a436e1e: **Notes**: Dark vertical stripes and an ocellus on the tail. Highly adaptable, even to brackish water.
textos.21d70e41c9e5887f: **Notes**: Males are light blue with a bright yellow throat and belly; females are orange-brown. Slightly less aggressive than other Maylandia species.
textos.46995ec0c811cc93: **Notes**: Uniform cobalt blue, without bands, in both males and females. A white form also exists. Hardy and very showy.
textos.5e14942a480d6db8: **Notes**: Females are orange and males are sky blue. Like all mbuna, they should be kept in heavily stocked aquariums with plenty of rocks to help diffuse aggression. Avoid meat-rich foods.
textos.780731e40631cc27: **Notes**: Males are ice blue with a reddish-orange dorsal fin; females are brown. One of the most striking mbuna.
textos.2d281e8eb8881d98: **Notes**: A pale blue mbuna with faint stripes and striking eyes. Care is the same as for the blue zebra; keep in an aquarium with plenty of crevices among the rocks.
textos.cc9b96c1c4dd0425: **Notes**: Interesting sexual dimorphism: females are blue with stripes, and males are yellow-orange. Very territorial; should only be kept with robust mbuna.
textos.0e688d77d3d87767: **Notes**: The classic mbuna: light blue with vertical black stripes. There are many local variants. Keep the aquarium heavily stocked and provide plenty of rocks to help diffuse aggression.
textos.dde3a4753242a987: **Notes**: Dark brown with black spots. Hardy and calm; occasionally comes to the surface to breathe air.
textos.3def4aadabf0e7a0: **Notes**: The front half is grayish-blue and the rear half is yellow, with a dark line across the eye. It swims in the middle of the water column.
textos.8f65b560b5e4ee9a: **Notes**: Black lines on a yellow and white background. It has venomous fangs that deter predators; harmless to humans.
textos.5384a7d6ae58a7f1: **Notes**: Uniform canary yellow. Bred in captivity and very hardy.
textos.feac7c2907114fc8: **Notes**: Bluish-gray with a black line across the eye and a blue-edged dorsal fin. A docile fanged blenny.
textos.2dee71028bd6033c: **Notes**: Females are golden with black bands; males are almost black with light lines. Very aggressive toward others of its own species: only one male per aquarium.
textos.95404ddd1c3d58ce: **Notes**: Males are dark blue with light blue stripes; females are brown. Very territorial.
textos.43c0de4d6c3857b6: **Notes**: Electric blue and black horizontal stripes on both males and females. Small and less aggressive than other Melanochromis species.
textos.aba3b24799646df4: **Notes**: A light-colored mbuna with dark lines that break up into spots, hence the name. Rare; keep it with mbunas of similar size.
textos.2647dceef73ea0b3: **Notes**: Females are orange and males are dark blue with light horizontal stripes. They have the same strong temperament as the auratus.
textos.54484bb3949ea214: **Notes**: White with two parallel horizontal black lines, very high contrast. Slightly calmer than the auratus but just as territorial toward fish with a similar pattern.
textos.d1488fa6ef66cde5: **Notes**: It spends the day buried in the substrate and stirring it up, which prevents oxygen-depleted areas. A rapidly growing population indicates an excess of food.
textos.78efbc82969fe10d: **Notes**: The front half is blue and the back half is orange. Males become more colorful at dawn. Requires a long aquarium for swimming and moderately hard water.
textos.a41328578f64c56e: **Notes**: A temperate-climate rainbowfish with reddish fins and blue iridescence. Tolerates cool water.
textos.f1b4fb5bb2b0b084: **Notes**: Greenish body with a dark line and fins with red edges. Active in groups.
textos.2a422514945a49a9: **Notes**: Yellow body with a dark lateral stripe. Active and hardy, a beautiful contrast with blue rainbowfish.
textos.850463154dd731ae: **Notes**: A small, tall-bodied rainbowfish, blue with yellow fins. Endemic to a single lake.
textos.3e529e01d052199b: **Notes**: Deep turquoise blue. Requires space to swim in a group and somewhat hard water.
textos.4ecaaad45142673e: **Notes**: Dwarf rainbowfish with dark horizontal stripes and red fins. Hardy and suitable for medium-sized aquariums.
textos.d2bddffe17639b2e: **Notes**: Dark lateral line and fins with red edges. The first rainbowfish to be scientifically described.
textos.e0dec3985445afe6: **Notes**: Bluish-silver body with an orange rear half in males. Very elegant in large groups.
textos.26aca45b1c508f8b: **Notes**: Males have metallic blue scales and red fins (females have yellow fins). The best rainbowfish for medium-sized planted aquariums.
textos.776a1dc91859506e: **Notes**: Small rainbowfish with fine lines and reddish fins. Suitable for medium-sized aquariums.
textos.af2518f63c70dc09: **Notes**: A rainbowfish with thin dark stripes and yellow fins. Known as the six-lined rainbowfish.
textos.45f2e1e93bbd120a: **Notes**: Body with blue and green iridescence and fins with red edges. One of the hardiest rainbowfish.
textos.8b0ef9bf44a6fd56: **Notes**: Each locality has different colors (blue, red, yellow). It’s best not to mix forms to keep them pure.
textos.53ae95f2a4013bf6: **Notes**: Dark body with a pink tail and white fins. It also eats algae; it is calmer than other triggerfish.
textos.85df949f623ab9fe: **Notes**: Fragrant, with lilac-colored flowers that attract pollinators. Absorbs nutrients and helps control algae in the pond.
textos.38a08de6e4c9e9f0: **Notes**: Plates with fan-shaped grooves, in shades of cream or pink. Grows quickly in shelf-like tiers.
textos.a1a6d5bd99e80b08: **Notes**: A dark diagonal stripe runs from the snout to the dorsal fin. Peaceful and a good tankmate for angelfish.
textos.57bdc2adfa433d74: **Notes**: Related to the blackwater flag cichlid, with a more pronounced diagonal stripe.
textos.ea819830d23951b7: **Notes**: Short spines and blue bands. It covers itself with small pieces of shell or rock for camouflage. It cleans algae without harming the corals.
textos.833a2162f1a25600: **Notes**: A herbivorous relative of piranhas, with a round, silvery body. It eats almost any plant, so the aquarium should be decorated with roots, rocks, or hardy plants such as Anubias.
textos.1de2effc5803fe20: **Notes**: Silvery with bluish iridescence and reddish fins. An active swimmer that travels in schools.
textos.6510c66b0e82b3e4: **Notes**: A more forgiving alternative to HC Cuba. With CO2, it forms a dense, low carpet. Without CO2, it grows somewhat taller.
textos.b0088365b58cbc82: **Notes**: Tiny, round leaves on slender stems that form compact clumps. With frequent pruning, it remains a low-growing shrub; without CO2, it becomes leggy and loses its lower leaves.
textos.f25b0764e96b6cd1: **Notes**: Males have orange and green bands and white-edged fins. A small, very colorful African labyrinth fish.
textos.543e68d086d28bb8: **Notes**: Translucent lime green that glows under side lighting. Prefers a slight current and well-oxygenated water. Great choice for planted nano tanks.
textos.29f1c6b6e92781ff: **Notes**: Tiny, translucent danio with an iridescent stripe. Ideal for cool-water nano tanks.
textos.925368ea3987c8ea: **Notes**: Yellow and brown stripes like a bumblebee. Nocturnal and secretive: needs caves and food when the lights go out.
textos.839d959dea4998ca: **Notes**: Known as “Acan.” Fleshy polyps in an almost infinite variety of color combinations. Grows faster when fed mysis or coral pellets. It was sold as Acanthastrea lordhowensis.
textos.ed83121ff57c0a1e: **Notes**: Known as the “swamp guppy”: males have red, black, and yellow spots. Requires slightly brackish water.
textos.0de89a418b7b0208: **Notes**: Males are reddish with a dark lateral stripe. It shares the lake with the emerald danio and prefers hard, cool water.
textos.c3c7bf91196849e8: **Notes**: Tolerates temperatures up to 30°C. One of the few medium-sized plants suitable for discus tanks.
textos.942b17e8e1d381ec: **For a plantless Discus tank**: Many professional breeders keep Discus in plantless (bare-bottom) tanks to facilitate cleaning and frequent water changes. This is a completely valid and common option.
textos.ac114e1da6132138: **Notes**: Less striking than the Ramirezi, but much hardier and more tolerant of normal temperatures. An excellent first cichlid for community aquariums.
textos.56c97fb491e0c2c6: **Notes**: One of the most colorful dwarf cichlids, with electric blue iridescence. It requires warm, soft, and very clean water. Many captive-bred varieties (golden, balloon) are more delicate than the wild form.
textos.fa191b2a7ed74f31: **Notes**: Compatible with goldfish in terms of temperature. Becomes restless before storms (detects changes in atmospheric pressure). Needs fine sand for burrowing. Can breathe atmospheric air.
textos.7128486b1c3f706c: **Notes**: A red relative of the emerald crab. It eats algae and detritus.
textos.96382ec927bcd436: **Notes**: The only invertebrate effective against bubble algae (Valonia ventricosa), the “green plague” of marine aquariums. It also eats filamentous algae and Bryopsis. It may occasionally prey on small invertebrates if hungry. Add just a few individuals so they always have algae available.
textos.6dc8d9f3fc9ac8b1: **Notes**: A small African catfish with a mottled brown pattern. Nocturnal and shy; requires hiding places and soft water.
textos.795c9863bcd7f147: **Notes**: Shiny silvery scales and a dark band on the tail. Active and hardy.
textos.869c22b53e79217f: **Notes**: Large scales with dark, net-like edges and a red area above the eye. A larger relative of the red-eyed tetra.
textos.fb50b674dddb6a53: **Notes**: Scales that shimmer like glitter in the light. Adult males develop long, purplish fins. Hardy and very showy when kept in a group.
textos.f56f7ad08f84aa10: **Notes**: Silver in color with a red upper eye and a black band on the tail. Hardy and adaptable to almost any water condition. May eat plants with very tender leaves.
textos.38bceeb85693e25f: **Notes**: Related to the purple-spotted gudgeon, with red spots and striped fins. Tolerates cool water.
textos.ee0f69eef316241a: **Notes**: Covered in red, purple, and blue spots. Hardy and easy to breed.
textos.e13e56c3939512d9: **Notes**: It mimics a floating dry leaf to approach its prey. Highly specialized: it eats only live prey.
textos.110c15a012a2dade: **Notes**: Silver with a diamond-shaped body and yellow fins. As juveniles, they tolerate nearly freshwater conditions, but as adults, they require heavily brackish or saltwater. Always kept in groups.
textos.9057dd6248cb74ad: **Notes**: Very tall body, taller than it is long, with vertical black stripes. Always found in groups and in brackish water.
textos.e6c417df4246ec10: **Notes**: Known as “pellia”: a broad-lobed liverwort that sinks on its own, unlike riccia. An ideal hiding place for shrimp.
textos.9c7a45dbfd6f20cc: **Notes**: Large, rounded coral polyps in fluorescent green, orange, or red. Massive Caribbean coral.
textos.cddad08e27d42227: **Notes**: Grows in plates or branches depending on light conditions, often reddish in color. Easy for an SPS.
textos.dfe89c2864444f92: **Notes**: It grows in spiraling sheets or plates, in shades of orange, purple, or green. The best SPS for beginners looking to start with small-polyp stony corals.
textos.14143ba5f0be5c69: **Notes**: An encrusting coral with brightly colored bumps and polyps. Easy to care for and fast-growing.
textos.184b510cc22945d1: **Notes**: An encrusting species with a ridged pattern that glows under blue light. Highly prized in cultured varieties.
textos.868297b0956a757e: **Notes**: Branched (digitate) form. Grows faster than most SPS corals. Very sensitive to temperature: bleaches above 28°C. The most recommended “starter” SPS: if you can grow M. digitata well, you’re ready for Acropora.
textos.97899a78998693d8: **Notes**: Overlapping, leaf-shaped plates. Related to capricornis, just as easy.
textos.861e2215b30929a4: **Notes**: Branches covered with small bumps. Grows quickly and is tolerant.
textos.8f01e28f292a45a8: **Notes**: Short, thick branches, often pink or orange. More tolerant than Acropora.
textos.9164e56f9d2f0344: **Notes**: The most tolerant SPS and the one most recommended for beginners. Comes in a wide variety of forms: encrusting (M. capricornis), branching (M. digitata), and foliate. Stunning colors under blue light (green, orange, purple, red). Much more tolerant of KH fluctuations than Acropora. M. digitata is the most recommended entry-level SPS species.
textos.9d8f7f3a113f2d19: **Notes**: Encrusting, with small tubercles and colorful polyps. Easy to care for and hardy.
textos.d4afe7eadd088f60: **Notes**: It grows in plates with wavy ridges, in shades of green or orange with contrasting-colored polyps.
