textos.8277b33cea097a9b: **Notes**: A goby from the lakes of Sulawesi with yellow fins. Ideal for alkaline-water aquariums with large shrimp.
textos.9c8c075a74b99e0a: **Notes**: Plates with corallites tilted like tiny noses, in contrasting colors. Resembles the chalice.
textos.e8b647c283e7fcd6: **Notes**: A diagonal black stripe runs across its body. It has teeth in its throat for crushing snails.
textos.312d1a38d6b0a005: **Notes**: Silver in color, with a hook-shaped red anal fin in males. Always kept in groups and in large aquariums without soft plants.
textos.724b0eb884ab1e6c: **Notes**: Small sky-blue flowers for months. Covers the edges of the pond.
textos.d5106f38be66c805: **Notes**: Blue-green, feathery leaves. Invasive alien species; trade is prohibited in the EU: check the regulations before growing it.
textos.f3f369416c5a8368: **Notes**: Light green, feathery leaves that turn red at the tips. Sediment on the leaves bothers this plant.
textos.e7be62852285c692: **Notes**: A native oxygenating plant with feathery leaves. Excellent for cold-water ponds.
textos.ebc58590db30d9e2: **Notes**: Deep red, feathery leaves. Very demanding in terms of light and nutrients, but spectacular.
textos.02f3151b7d19e6e3: **Notes**: Bright red with large eyes. Nocturnal; requires shaded caves.
textos.a77d1c7354b9a52f: **Notes**: Dark horizontal stripes and long barbels. Similar to the striped catfish, but somewhat more tolerant of cool water.
textos.7e951052277aab9b: **Notes**: Dark horizontal stripes and long barbels. Active and somewhat restless; best kept with fish of similar size.
textos.3e9f20a8505f57c6: **Notes**: Juveniles have a very tall dorsal fin with brown bands, but as adults they lose that shape and grow to over one meter in length. Suitable only for large ponds.
textos.ce20634a359c48e4: **Notes**: Known as “guppy grass”: a mass of thin stems ideal as a shelter for fry.
textos.4178e6ddeff986bb: **Notes**: It mimics a dry leaf to get close to its prey. Keep only with fish too large to fit in its mouth.
textos.c3902d935ea3e5d5: **Notes**: Males have metallic green scales. Hardy and easy to breed: a good introduction to cichlid breeding.
textos.eea61ad4c43b770b: **Notes**: Males have golden heads and bodies with blue iridescence. An easy and good alternative to the Ramirezi.
textos.4f24c0226655fc00: **Notes**: A small Nannacara with a checkered pattern. Very peaceful and suitable for nano tanks.
textos.20fe2e954b6e2a2f: **Notes**: Pencil-shaped body with a dark stripe and fins with red accents. At night, its pattern changes to stripes. Ideal for peaceful planted aquariums.
textos.cb4e7b6bdbe91985: **Notes**: Swims with its head tilted upward, near floating plants. Needs peaceful tankmates that won’t steal its food at the surface.
textos.0526f7b01ce3f3b8: **Notes**: Instead of lines, it has a row of comma-shaped black spots. Small and peaceful.
textos.1698c1f2f9bc25d1: **Notes**: Wide black stripe with a gold border and red accents on the tail. Rare.
textos.110515a3da78891b: **Notes**: The smallest pencilfish, with black and gold stripes and red spots on its fins. Perfect for planted nano tanks.
textos.f86bbae0e7f62e96: **Notes**: Males are a deep coral red with black lines. One of the most spectacular pencilfish.
textos.8e7a30bd3aba38d8: **Notes**: Tiny pencilfish with a red tail and a dark stripe. Ideal for planted nano tanks.
textos.5efb4d16f8d3f2f1: **Notes**: Three dark bands with a golden line and red spots on the fins. One of the most beautiful pencilfish for calm Amazonian aquariums.
textos.b5d981a0cfa4635d: **Notes**: A single black band with a gold border. It swims at an angle with its head pointing upward, like Nannostomus eques.
textos.aaae018956b3ecee: **Notes**: Bluish body with greenish iridescence and white-edged fins. A rapids-dwelling cichlid.
textos.d3bb0343a2b4de07: **Notes**: It gets its name because the female is more colorful than the male, with red fins and black stripes. Very soft blackwater.
textos.8a16ec7b47a61827: **Notes**: An Indian Ocean relative of the naso tang, with a yellow dorsal fin. It grows quite large.
textos.8b60f0eee7ef5db4: **Notes**: Orange lips and a yellow line running from the eye to the mouth. It has spines at the base of its tail. It grows very large: suitable only for very large aquariums.
textos.7bc114cc57e96bdd: **Notes**: Spends most of its time buried in the sand. Emerges rapidly when it detects food. An essential part of the cleanup crew: they remove food scraps before they decompose. They stir up the sand, preventing anoxic zones. Almost indispensable in any saltwater tank with sand.
textos.5c09f24a9cdcf503: **Notes**: A small snail that lives buried in the substrate and emerges as soon as it smells food. It stirs up the sand.
textos.be398ad700691535: **Notes**: Orange with a purple line extending from the eye. It lives in large schools on the reef.
textos.74b013ec0b1636a9: **Notes**: Very tall dorsal fin with shades of purple and yellow. It takes refuge in a hole in the rock when startled. Jumps: the aquarium needs a mesh cover.
textos.6eb96a9893b99def: **Notes**: Yellow head with violet highlights and a lavender body. It lives at greater depths than other dartfish and is expensive.
textos.e8759402f35c591f: **Notes**: Red-orange tail and white body with a greatly elongated first dorsal fin. Jumps when startled: a lid is essential. Gets intimidated by active or aggressive fish.
textos.0a0c0254a5449838: **Notes**: Black lateral stripe, violet iridescence, and a trident-shaped tail in males. Less gregarious than other tetras: a small group with a majority of females is sufficient.
textos.539ed6df50110d9f: **Notes**: Care requirements are exactly the same as for the Cherry Red. The deep blue color is harder to achieve than the red. High-quality “Blue Dream” specimens are more expensive. Do not mix with other Neocaridina varieties to maintain the color line (crossbreeding produces transparent or brown shrimp).
textos.c3b4be27ffa358f2: **Notes**: The most popular and easiest shrimp to keep in the hobby. Breeds without human intervention. The red color is more intense in healthy adult females. Quality grades: Sakura < Cherry < Fire Red < Painted Fire Red (based on color density). The male is smaller, transparent, or slightly pinkish. Inert substrate recommended. The shrimp constantly forage on moss and plants in search of biofilm.
textos.ae2b8112ee8b5475: **Notes**: Bright lemon yellow, especially striking against dark substrates. Same care requirements as Cherry Red. The highest-quality specimens have a solid yellow color without any transparency. Do not mix with other Neocaridina varieties.
textos.5ac532aafc6c6fb4: **Notes**: Bright red with a black stripe along its back. It perches on corals, keeping watch over its territory.
textos.d071a995aeedd2ea: **Notes**: Juveniles are black with neon blue lines and a yellow bar; as adults, they lose their coloration and become very territorial.
textos.9d8fe823a831d9a9: **Notes**: A shell cichlid in which the male and female live together in the same shell, which is somewhat unusual. It requires fine sand and several snail shells.
textos.4b3c01e70f399b03: **Notes**: Elongated body with thin bands and fins edged in blue. Lives in deep rock crevices.
textos.c5f541044be79521: **Notes**: Gray body with a yellow dorsal fin and a speckled tail. Small, peaceful, and easy to breed.
textos.6f547f80bbde91d3: **Notes**: Elongated body with dark vertical bands and fins with blue edges. It fiercely defends its cave.
textos.9ac09f6d7f0106a8: **Notes**: Lyre-shaped tail with filaments and a beige body. Belongs to the princess group.
textos.0840dd1814bd22f7: **Notes**: Slender, with blue-edged fins and a lyre-shaped tail. Elegant when seen in family groups.
textos.9f8b5b6c8ef16fda: **Notes**: A relative of the Burundi princess, with a yellow face. Forms family colonies among the rocks.
textos.8d07130b8f695767: **Notes**: Uniform, deep orange. Lives among stacked rocks with crevices. Its color is best maintained with a diet rich in carotenoids.
textos.8a16fc2ab8e6bf2b: **Notes**: Yellowish-orange and elongated, very similar to the leleupi. It lives in crevices.
textos.073b18beb4324254: **Notes**: The world’s smallest cichlid. It lives in colonies on a bed of shells, which it buries and unearths by stirring up the sand. Fascinating in a dedicated aquarium.
textos.065a7773e12a3dca: **Notes**: Dark body with a yellow or orange face and fins. Related to the leleupi.
textos.7272f377ce49b684: **Notes**: Olive-colored body with fins edged in blue and yellow. From the Burundi Princess complex.
textos.8345b7bdbd96b893: **Notes**: It was sold as Neolamprologus brichardi. Elegant, with lyre-shaped fins edged in white. Forms family clans that eventually occupy the entire aquarium.
textos.d685390906f09801: **Notes**: Small, with vertical bands and blue lines on its face. Lives in family groups.
textos.828a08b66d979663: **Notes**: Six dark bands on a blue or gold background, depending on the location. Feeds on snails in the wild.
textos.3bfcff6e0421e06b: **Notes**: Similar to multifasciatus, with vertical bands extending up to the head. It lives in colonies on beds of shells.
textos.2bfd706b86c01b68: **Notes**: A large bottom-dwelling lamprologine, gray with light spots and a dorsal fin edged in white and red. It stirs up the sand in search of invertebrates.
textos.7ea7dfe2e328d0e8: **Notes**: Five vertical black stripes on a bluish background. It resembles a small frontosa, but is much more aggressive.
textos.cfb5541cb1547493: **Notes**: A small red and green African characin with a dark stripe. Requires soft water, dense plants, and a calm environment.
textos.4d516608047ab9cc: **Notes**: White with red spots. Lives inside an anemone, like clownfish. Prefers phytoplankton and powdered food.
textos.4ba9e2e09d377846: **Notes**: A tree-like coral with fleshy branches in shades of green or brown. It sways with the current.
textos.8252ea3b8c76681b: **Notes**: Marine nerite snail with a smooth shell in various shades. It cleans algae from the glass and can climb out of the water.
textos.f0f77ea0787ce9de: **Notes**: Yellow shell with black zigzag stripes. An excellent algae eater that does not reproduce in the aquarium.
textos.0d85ad788b5ba3a1: **Notes**: Shiny black shell with a yellow opening. Excellent at removing film-like algae.
textos.c6416529dc67e100: **Notes**: The hard operculum protects the Nerite from goldfish, although round-bodied goldfish with large mouths sometimes bother them. It effectively cleans algae from the glass. The temperature is a bit low for this snail—it thrives best at 22–25°C.
textos.9c286abec4b89977: **Notes**: The best glass cleaner for brackish aquariums. Salinity-tolerant Nerite species include N. virginea and N. turrita. Ideal for controlling algae in brackish aquariums. They will not survive with pufferfish; do not keep them together.
textos.af129e65f1441c2b: **Notes**: Elongated, band-like markings; males have bluish-green heads. Large and voracious.
textos.9e07e98c2cb9cea4: **Notes**: It has irregular markings that mimic a decaying fish: it lies on its side at the bottom and preys on curious fish that approach.
textos.7faf6486aa98aaf9: **Notes**: Covered in brown spots; males turn blue and green. A stalking predator.
textos.5ebd6fc2e8247a43: **Notes**: Spots like those of a giraffe; males have blue and yellow heads. In the wild, it buries itself and plays dead to hunt.
textos.b602ed863c7a4c42: **Notes**: Short, hook-shaped lower jaw that is black, and red and black fins. Clean, flowing water.
textos.0f81698ad63a7fc0: **Notes**: Known as “bullrout”: rock-like camouflage and highly venomous spines. Handle with extreme care.
textos.df3da11097f200c6: **Notes**: It comes in red and blue varieties. Like all Nothobranchius, it requires live food and has a short lifespan.
textos.cd46592056cc15c6: **Notes**: Males have blue scales edged with red and a red tail with a dark border. Like all Nothobranchius, it has a short lifespan.
textos.d6fa50f5d14bed62: **Notes**: One of the shortest-lived vertebrates (a few months), widely used in studies on aging. Males have red or yellow tails.
textos.72fb12b6d4f1c3ab: **Notes**: Males are red with blue-green scales and a red tail edged in black. Short lifespan, about one year.
textos.40eac977451a7633: **Notes**: Males are reddish-orange with edged scales and a yellow tail. Short lifespan; requires live food.
textos.ea286d8cba622903: **Notes**: Males have a reddish body with pale blue scales. Annual Malawi killifish.
textos.5fcded0ff324ce29: **Notes**: Males have red-edged scales and a yellow or red tail. One of the easiest Nothobranchius species to care for.
textos.0e70c94ba249d4b6: **Notes**: Males have bluish scales with a red net-like pattern and dark spots on the dorsal fin.
textos.15d3c3a0bbf0d456: **Notes**: Bluish males with red-edged scales and a red tail. A short-lived annual killifish.
textos.fa4a788b2f1b537b: **Notes**: Males are blue with red-edged scales and black fins with light-colored edges. Small and colorful.
textos.c98f526fdef45cba: **Notes**: One of the most colorful fish in existence, with blue scales edged in red. It has a very short lifespan—about one year—because in the wild, its pond dries up.
textos.b797ee9e5b17435a: **Notes**: Bluish males with red tails and fins. Annual killifish found in coastal ponds.
textos.b31ab01c53c71075: **Notes**: Silvery-bronze, knife-shaped body. Nocturnal; smaller than the clown knifefish.
textos.670e691b8bbe4467: **Notes**: Known as the “rainbow shiner”: males in breeding season display pink, blue, and violet colors. A cold-water, fast-flowing stream fish.
textos.a14e72d441f21bc6: **Notes**: Juveniles mimic drifting algae with filamentous fins. As adults, they turn over rocks in search of food.
textos.fb98fcfbe31c6549: **Notes**: Round, yellow flowers. Tolerates some shade and current; suitable for large ponds.
textos.7f644724f17cdaa5: **Notes**: The native white-flowered water lily. It requires sunlight and deep water; it provides shade and shelter for the fish in the pond.
textos.8bc77b3536f09c47: **Notes**: Red leaves with dark spots that grow from a bulb. If allowed to reach the surface, they shade everything else: trim them so the plant stays submerged.
textos.022060590458ff79: **Notes**: Its storage roots look like small bananas. If left to grow, it produces round floating leaves.
textos.888513a8561e51e7: **Notes**: Round, floating leaves and yellow flowers with fringed petals. Invasive in small ponds: control it.
textos.47e5fbae63a51214: **Notes**: Spectacular colors and a strike so powerful it can shatter glass. Only in a dedicated aquarium.
textos.ac045f775c46e619: **Notes**: Violet-blue with visible red teeth. Hides in holes in the rocks. Eats invertebrates, so it is not suitable for reef tanks.
textos.7fbcced8f114e92a: **Note**: Very popular for their visual impact and because they are easy to appreciate.
textos.7402a41ff14fe066: **Notes**: Large scales with dark edges that form a checkerboard pattern. Males have red fins with black edges. Small, hardy, and peaceful.
textos.fed7db46fa064565: **Notes**: A translucent catfish with dark spots that lives in groups in the middle of the water column. Shy.
textos.f2ca6727da735b23: **Notes**: A large green brittle star. Very effective at scavenging, but as an adult it catches small, sleeping fish. Best kept with medium-sized or large fish.
textos.2bdf0967c26b0189: **Notes**: Dark body with red lips and fins. It vigorously defends its rock.
textos.26b5fa82a762588e: **Notes**: Arms with dark and light bands. Scavenges under rocks; peaceful with fish.
textos.57895a06af8d2465: **Notes**: A brittle star with ringed arms. It picks up debris under rocks at night.
textos.e1e8ea5f3f0eb3b5: **Notes**: Males are black with fins edged in blue and yellow. Related to the ventralis.
textos.4688d451f213e55c: **Notes**: Males have a prominent fleshy snout and very long ventral fins. Requires plenty of space.
textos.bb4a692787c3478d: **Notes**: Males are electric blue with very long ventral fins that have yellow tips. They build nests on rocks.
textos.26653cb545607fba: **Notes**: Yellow head and pale blue body. It digs a vertical burrow in the substrate and pokes its head out. It needs at least 10 cm of sand mixed with gravel and a cover, because it jumps.
textos.2e63faeaae666d9a: **Notes**: Golden yellow with electric blue spots. Prefers water that is slightly cooler than that of a typical reef tank.
textos.69b034e3e4ed2fff: **Notes**: The cap grows as the fish ages. Do not mix with elongated goldfish (which are slower eaters). The cap can become infected if the water quality is not optimal. The “Red Cap Oranda” (white body, red cap) is iconic.
textos.52b6f3fc15546802: **Notes**: A very popular rice paddy fish in Japan, bred in hundreds of color varieties. It lives without a heater and in patio ponds during the summer.
textos.208a8420eb1bfb58: **Notes**: Electric blue body with red fins. Very easy to care for and prolific. Perfect for planted tropical nano-aquariums.
textos.d45c86bf5386c23c: **Notes**: It is sold when it is only a few centimeters long but can grow to over half a meter and live for 20 years. Suitable only for public or very large aquariums. Very intelligent and sociable with people.
textos.bf83ee52c7604d59: **Notes**: A relative of the giant gourami with a red tail and fins. Just as huge: only suitable for very large aquariums.
textos.7119ae942716a5b6: **Notes**: It is sold as a juvenile measuring just a few centimeters, but it grows to nearly one meter and is a great jumper. Only suitable for very large, securely covered aquariums.
textos.1602000f40f75b35: **Notes**: Juveniles are black with a yellow stripe; adults are bluish-silver. It grows very large.
textos.3ff6f247cd0796c4: **Notes**: Known as the blue-eyed cardinalfish: brown stripes and large bluish eyes. It lives among branching corals.
textos.e15a8f795618bebd: **Notes**: Silvery-blue body with horizontal orange stripes. Shy during the day and more active at dusk.
textos.a7056729d6f1436a: **Notes**: Juveniles are yellow cubes with black spots. When stressed or dying, they release ostracitoxin, which can kill the entire aquarium. For experienced aquarists only.
textos.424b9648c1894c6d: **Notes**: Males are blue with white spots and yellow sides; females are black with white spots. Delicate and toxic if it dies.
textos.34bfb94bb5676450: **Notes**: An excellent eater of green algae on glass and plants. Requires a mature aquarium with an established biofilm. Very fragile in new aquariums. Coexists perfectly with shrimp.
textos.f5f5415b4771f4c5: **Notes**: Otocinclus with very distinct black bands on a white background. Delicate at first: introduce into established aquariums with abundant biofilm and acclimate slowly.
textos.4b97b7ee450151c2: **Notes**: A temperate-climate Otocinclus with a dark lateral stripe. Tolerates cooler water.
textos.bea0c7ed078eb969: **Notes**: Dwarf Otocinclus with a speckled pattern. Ideal for mature nano tanks with fine algae.
textos.82e83bd0643a463e: **Notes**: Otocinclus with a large black spot at the base of its tail. Requires established aquariums with fine algae.
textos.2979bbe816ae4f44: **Notes**: Small Otocinclus with a black spot on its tail. Removes fine algae in mature nano tanks.
textos.9aff776136a4ce66: **Notes**: Very similar to Otocinclus affinis, with a dark lateral stripe extending to the tail. Requires a mature aquarium with abundant biofilm.
textos.33352ff8c4b606a8: **Notes**: Males are dark blue with a yellow stripe on the forehead and a light-colored dorsal fin. Very striking and relatively calm.
textos.a88cf08c99fb1985: **Notes**: Four dark spots on the side; males have blue and green hues. Medium-sized haplo.
textos.46b827cbe7d5a555: **Notes**: A small, otocinclus-like loricarid with a reddish tail. It eats fine algae in planted nano tanks.
textos.5126f0862d7602d1: **Notes**: Large, translucent, wavy leaves. A spectacular solitary plant in large aquariums.
textos.7d92bcedb67a09d2: **Notes**: Wide, winding valleys with thin walls. Green and brown brain coral.
textos.8c08d7139082bf92: **Notes**: Red pattern on a white background and a long snout. It perches on gorgonians and corals, observing everything. It is not safe around small cleaner shrimp.
textos.db05a06dd6457f4c: **Notes**: Known as the marble goby: a massive predator that spends the day motionless. Suitable only for very large aquariums.
textos.e9841daf631557e7: **Notes**: Green with orange spots and an elongated snout. Feeds exclusively on Acropora polyps: very difficult to keep in an aquarium.
textos.edc8503fda18d35e: **Notes**: Thin, lace-like perforated sheets with contrasting colors. Resembles the chalice.
textos.6968d61ed269ea9b: **Notes**: Known as GSP. A purple mat from which fluorescent green polyps emerge and sway with the current. It grows very quickly: best placed on an isolated rock.
textos.a7760ce84ab13dba: **Notes**: Males have red scales with golden highlights. This species is endangered in its natural habitat; those sold in stores are bred in captivity.
textos.828602c8dd4a27a3: **Notes**: Red spots on a gold background. Robust and a jumper; best kept with fish of similar size.
textos.78422edcce949a4b: **Notes**: Plates with concentric ridges resembling fingerprints. Tolerates low light.
textos.7118f81cd086f541: **Notes**: Fan-shaped brown algae with white calcified bands. Typical of Mediterranean rocks.
textos.84e9fc04d06b883c: **Notes**: Bright red with yellow eyes. One of the most peaceful hermit crabs; feeds on algae and detritus.
textos.d13c7d8ebca2de62: **Notes**: A translucent shrimp with dark lines and yellow and blue spots on its legs. Very common in tidal pools.
textos.fe1717099e452b94: **Notes**: Lives in marshes and salt flats; tolerates extreme changes in salinity. Very hardy.
textos.9da44fda0a7f86c9: **Notes**: Completely transparent. Very inexpensive and hardy. In aquariums with small shrimp, it can act as a predator. Frequently used as live food for large fish. Less ornamental than Neocaridina and Caridina. Tolerant of a wide range of water parameters.
textos.7f67db5417cf7287: **Notes**: Forms greenish-yellow mats. Grows quickly and can take over the rock. Same precautions regarding palytoxin.
textos.c6ab50097be555da: **Notes**: Known as the “sun polyp”: large yellow or green polyps. Contains palytoxin, which is very dangerous: wear gloves and goggles when handling.
textos.58250323b1e3559c: **Notes**: ⚠️ **PALYTOXIN**: Contains palytoxin, one of the most potent natural toxins. It is released when the coral is cut, crushed, or heated. Symptoms: nausea, difficulty breathing, seizures. ALWAYS wear nitrile gloves and goggles when handling. NEVER pour water containing Palythoa onto a wound.
textos.fd1199b7219c009f: **Notes**: Brown colonies of polyps with embedded sand. Contains palytoxin: wear gloves when handling.
textos.4d10a62d5472c5e7: **Notes**: Known as L204. Black with white, worm-like lines and a tail with orange edges. Small and suitable for medium-sized aquariums with driftwood.
textos.e99e9efa818ea3a6: **Notes**: Known as L206: dark and light bands and a tail with an orange edge. Requires driftwood.
textos.3b5d1c08d70dfa51: **Notes**: Known as L104. Black and gold stripes and a moderate size. It needs wood in the aquarium, because it scrapes at it and the wood is part of its diet.
textos.65e9fffad2dd1cb8: **Notes**: Known as L027. Olive gray with light-colored fin edges. Like the royal pleco, it requires driftwood and very powerful filtration.
textos.695e68fa56974ecc: **Notes**: Dark gray with turquoise-blue eyes. Highly prized and delicate; requires driftwood and crystal-clear water.
textos.26f896f0ee38a21d: **Notes**: Known as L190. Dark stripes on a gray background and red eyes. It gnaws on wood, so it needs driftwood in the aquarium, and it produces a lot of waste.
textos.2994395880b2f388: **Notes**: A uniformly brown Pangio with a very elongated body. Nocturnal; requires fine sand and hiding places.
textos.7de16e6fdb46cca0: **Notes**: It looks like a small eel with orange and black stripes. It needs fine sand to burrow into and hiding places. It squeezes through any crack—be sure to protect the filter inlet.
textos.d6b002ba644ac17d: **Notes**: Wide black stripes on an orange background, thicker than those of the kuhli loach. Nocturnal and social.
textos.e68ed63201afc982: **Notes**: A relative of the kuhli loach with a uniform chocolate-brown color. Just as elusive: fine sand and a protected filter.
textos.9856b9816a494f4a: **Notes**: Very similar to the kuhli loach, but its dark bands do not quite close the ring on its belly, which is light orange. Same care requirements: fine sand and hiding places.
textos.c67245375d1b9881: **Notes**: Its pectoral fins resemble butterfly wings. It stays close to the surface and leaps to catch insects. It requires still water, floating plants, and a cover.
textos.3628891f683135ad: **Notes**: Blue-green body with white stripes and white antennae. Nocturnal; grows quite large and needs spacious caves.
textos.5369d7a6a6e6abf7: **Notes**: Known as the pig-headed pufferfish: rock camouflage and skin with cirri. Hunts by lying in wait.
textos.220364c0c8dcef9a: **Notes**: The largest Mediterranean blenny, with branched filaments above its eyes. It lives in crevices and has a lot of personality.
textos.b0e9f48faa0cd4d5: **Notes**: The "Dory" from the movie. Very susceptible to marine ich. Needs large aquariums to swim in. Eats mainly filamentous algae and nori. NOT suitable for small aquariums.
textos.e0091bd6dca78742: **Notes**: The common Mediterranean sea urchin, violet or brown in color. A voracious algae eater in cold-water aquariums. Its harvest is regulated.
textos.7a4de01f649c6c75: **Notes**: Males “flash” by unfurling their electric-colored fins to court females. A small wrasse that is fully suitable for reef tanks. A mesh cover is essential.
textos.39ea2c1b0c0280c4: **Notes**: Males have filaments on their dorsal fin and blue lines. They spread their fins to court females.
textos.0ee57f6b2adbb21e: **Notes**: Males are orange with blue stripes and red fins. Small and suitable for medium-sized reef tanks.
textos.685c5c77e2b9fed0: **Notes**: Males are red with eight blue lines and fan-shaped fins.
textos.dc34fc0bdf19d25a: **Notes**: The only tetra that is truly compatible with discus in very soft, acidic water. Discus usually do not eat them once they are adults (>2 cm). Spectacular when kept in a dense school under the “shade” of the discus.
textos.ee2e5d5b3bd3c3f7: **Notes**: The iridescent blue band and the red stripe only shine under good lighting and against a dark background. Very susceptible to neon disease (microsporidiosis). The red stripe extends only halfway down the body (unlike the Cardinal).
textos.bb7d6c5183be579b: **Notes**: Smaller than the common neon tetra and featuring a blue-green stripe that runs along almost the entire length of its side. Requires very soft, acidic water; ideal for blackwater aquariums with dried leaves.
textos.495ee27e7f046d34: **Notes**: Known as the “wolf cichlid.” One of the largest American cichlids, voracious and highly territorial.
textos.e9cb231c332bcce3: **Notes**: Black spots like a jaguar on a silvery background. Very large, voracious, and territorial. Only suitable for enormous aquariums.
textos.94840e65033ca6d3: **Notes**: Similar to the jaguar cichlid, with red spots on its face. A territorial predator.
textos.dfb70076e26f7535: **Notes**: A band of color behind the eye and a white lateral stripe. Sturdy; keeps watch from atop the rocks.
textos.682f3e40b008edd1: **Notes**: Neon blue stripes on a dark background. Lives in groups along rocky walls, often upside down under overhangs.
textos.ecd3223636b5b40f: **Notes**: Transparent body with bluish fin edges. For years, specimens injected with colored dyes were sold—a cruel practice that should be rejected.
textos.73624697e134bbe1: **Notes**: Known as L056. It can be dark gray, orange, or mottled. It lives in rapids: it needs a strong current and plenty of oxygen.
textos.373eed6bd66a59fd: **Notes**: A fully aquatic crab with leopard-like spots. Keep only in a dedicated aquarium.
textos.ae9c4d2a0d79a958: **Notes**: A schooling catfish with three dark lines and a banded tail. Active in the middle of the water column.
textos.ab1fb8706f95b136: **Notes**: A catfish that swims in midwater in schools, with dark stripes and a semi-transparent body. Active and sociable.

textos.e456e707a584b31d: **Notes**: Encrusting or columnar coral with small corallites. Easy to care for and comes in a variety of colors.

textos.d2a249ada336183d: **Notes**: Long-legged flat crab with golden stripes. Eats algae. Invasive species in the Spanish Mediterranean: never release it.

textos.8766b63f76555851: **Notes**: Dark body with an orange tail and a black spot behind the head.
textos.91a329c61072c978: **Notes**: Males turn a deep pink during the breeding season. Hardy and suitable for cool water. One of the best barbs for beginners.
textos.c5d21e503616b2ca: **Notes**: Golden with two dark bands and red or yellow fins, depending on the form. Peaceful and pretty.

textos.656dfd09d8ddd47d: **Notes**: Tiny golden barb with dark spots. Very peaceful; prefers slightly cooler water.
textos.51aa129769c2a6f7: **Notes**: During the breeding season, the males turn ruby red on the head and velvety black on the body. One of the most peaceful barbs.
textos.2f27f068655b18ba: **Notes**: Males have a bright red stripe running along their bodies and scales with black edges. Calm for a barb.

textos.6134466ec1ef2d49: **Notes**: The male in breeding condition is a bright cherry red. Much calmer than the tiger barb. This species is endangered in its natural habitat.

textos.837c22cd6525bd20: **Notes**: Covered with white or yellow spots on a dark background, with a crescent-shaped tail. Very aggressive and demanding.
textos.ced43c7aeb5bd2b7: **Notes**: A large mbuna with dark blue males and fins featuring yellow spots. Very territorial; requires plenty of space and rocks.

textos.dac347d51bd12bca: **Notes**: Small viviparous fish with a black spot on its side. Tolerates cool water; suitable for tanks without a heater.
textos.b875e93817e13055: **Notes**: A relative of the Congo tetra with orange hues and fringed fins. Needs space to swim.
textos.a2d6a8b82aa71ccb: **Notes**: Large scales with iridescent sheen and fins with white fringes in males. Needs space to swim and peaceful tankmates; becomes stressed around very fast-swimming fish.
textos.a050fe1cb35fb122: **Notes**: As a juvenile, it has stripes like a striped eel catfish. It digs tunnels under rocks, moving large amounts of sand: make sure the rock rests securely on the glass bottom.
textos.2064f918b5c4ee4e: **Reef Safe**: ⚠️ Use with caution (may destabilize the rock)
textos.8d9d014cd42ac179: **Notes**: A fish found in highly oxygenated mountain streams. Males in breeding season develop a red coloration on their bellies. Requires cold, clean water with a current.
textos.ba6f13b30e0f78c9: **Notes**: Sold at 5 cm and grows to over one meter: unsuitable for any home aquarium. Public aquariums no longer accept specimens. Do not buy it.
textos.400ed318170e81d0: **Notes**: Small floating leaves that turn red in bright light and reddish roots. Very decorative in open aquariums.
textos.b7568dac93805b7b: **Notes**: A small, brightly colored anemone that attaches itself to the substrate among rocks and does not usually move. Much safer in a reef tank than other anemones.
textos.0222bf4c3f907c31: **Notes**: The “pest” snail that comes with plants. Harmless, but its population explodes when there is an excess of food.
textos.b73dfdf843bb3b0b: **Notes**: Related to bubble coral, with smaller, pearl-like vesicles. Prefers low light and gentle currents.
textos.0f0e1aef8b986d2c: **Notes**: It is sold as a “vegetarian piranha” measuring just a few centimeters, but it can grow to over 80 cm and weigh more than 20 kg. Unsuitable for a home aquarium; it should never be released into rivers.

textos.318682c1c3277913: **Notes**: Very intense, uniform magenta color. Small but assertive around similar fish.
textos.c8726a39e5e2e899: **Notes**: Silver with black spots and very long barbels. Very active at night. Its spines get caught in nets: it’s best to catch it with a container.
textos.dfd5616ce323bd4c: **Notes**: The “rosy red” variety is common in ponds. Very hardy; should not be released into the wild.
textos.461f4f870a52ef6d: **Notes**: Photosynthetic gorgonian with yellowish branches and brown polyps. Easy to care for within its group.
textos.c5b36af291e543d9: **Notes**: Very long, dense roots; excellent hiding place. Requires a humid air space above the water.
textos.db9f2180ef9715f7: **Notes**: Sky blue with dark stripes on the head. One of the calmest haplochromines, ideal for keeping with peacock cichlids.
textos.048b0d3f3685b26d: **Notes**: A tall-bodied Haplochromis with black spots on a bluish background. Requires a large aquarium and tankmates of similar size.
textos.b600df5d16406299: **Notes**: Known as the “super VC-10.” It has enormous, fleshy lips that it uses to seal cracks and suck up invertebrates.
textos.be91b4a5ebbe2976: **Notes**: Males are blue with white lips and foreheads and dark spots. Very colorful and relatively calm.
textos.dd5bea98147e9d49: **Notes**: It mimics the cleaner wrasse to get close to fish and bite them. Not suitable for community aquariums.
textos.01906099df693ee0: **Notes**: The large European Planorbis snail, with a flat spiral shell. Very useful in cold-water ponds and aquariums.
textos.02107b0ecb69c971: **Notes**: Flat spiral shell with a red body. Breeds prolifically if there is excess food. Requires moderately hard water to form a well-developed shell.
textos.397052fe28c70099: **Notes**: Juveniles resemble a dry leaf. It grows very tall and large: suitable only for enormous aquariums.
textos.38a19db4984783c8: **Notes**: Juveniles are black with orange edging and very long fins. Very delicate; suitable only for public aquariums.

textos.b6ab8c8d120d7769: **Notes**: Juveniles are brown with white spots and swim in a manner resembling a flatworm. Adults grow to over 70 cm.
textos.9dd3071547125d2b: **Notes**: During the day, the tentacles expand like translucent bubbles. At night, it retracts the bubbles and extends stinging tentacles to hunt zooplankton. Do not mix with high-current corals. Leave 15 cm of free space around it.
textos.db1a59b972a165bf: **Notes**: A translucent goby that lives perched on corals, sponges, or algae. Almost invisible.
textos.d7e395445188da8f: **Notes**: Dark, flexible branches with light-colored polyps. A photosynthetic gorgonian, easy with good water flow.
textos.38eb366dd1503093: **Notes**: Juveniles form compact clusters with black and white stripes. Their spines are highly venomous. They grow quite large.
textos.e7ff5996e261d1f5: **Notes**: Dense, bulbous branches. P. damicornis can reproduce asexually by releasing “planulae” that settle in the aquarium. A good SPS for beginners after Montipora. Responds quickly to changes in water parameters (useful indicator).

textos.a85e10e236bae979: **Notes**: Branches with warts in shades of pink or green. It grows quickly and is a fairly hardy SPS.
textos.350f73fd81b6977f: **Notes**: The most salt-tolerant livebearer. In low-density brackish water (1.003–1.010), they thrive and are healthier than in freshwater. Highly resistant to disease in brackish water. Male Sailfin Mollies have a large, showy dorsal fin. The “Balloon Molly” variety (with a rounded body) is more delicate.
textos.d80018e4c3274a63: **Notes**: A wild molly with populations living in caves with sulfurous water. In the aquarium, it is hardy and eats algae.
textos.f8ade96c04a2c864: **Notes**: The most commonly bred fish in the world. They reproduce without human intervention. A ratio of 1 male to 2–3 females is recommended to prevent bullying. The fry are independent at birth.
textos.7277affb18401716: **Notes**: Known as the “Liberty molly”: males have orange and blue dorsal fins. Somewhat aggressive.
textos.cf437967e701db80: **Notes**: The black variety (black molly) is the best known. It requires hard, alkaline water; it becomes ill easily in soft water. It eats algae from the glass and from plants.
textos.78611a336cb7aee0: **Notes**: Males have a huge, sail-shaped dorsal fin with blue and orange spots. This species requires hard water and plenty of space.
textos.14f4431d8c20c227: **Notes**: A very colorful viviparous nano fish. Males have exceptional colors (orange, metallic green, black). Breeds easily: in a nano tank without predators, the aquarium will quickly become overpopulated. Very tolerant of water parameters. Hybridizes with guppies: do not mix them if you want purebred lines.
textos.c961da592096da8c: **Notes**: A modest viviparous species with dark lateral spots. It may carry several litters at different stages of development at the same time.
textos.9ba8616c899f04dd: **Notes**: Known as the “black morpho tetra”: black males with enormous fins edged in red and white. Very demanding.
textos.bac9149dc3ccac7f: **Notes**: Light green, needle-like leaves in dense whorls. Fine texture, suitable for the background.
textos.6c0fbb98f4eb30ef: **Notes**: Upright stems with needle-like leaves, resembling a small fir tree. It grows straight without requiring much pruning.
textos.8d430acb69edd4df: **Notes**: Wavy, star-shaped leaves. Very decorative among rocks. Tolerates heat well. Endangered in the wild: almost all of the plant sold commercially is grown in vitro.
textos.05debc86a1eb4df9: **Notes**: Known as Eusteralis: thin, star-shaped leaves in shades of lilac. Demanding but very showy.
textos.5f5208b4fd957e13: **Notes**: Needle-like leaves in dense whorls. A plant with a fine texture, suitable for aquascaping.
textos.81f20435ab294178: **Notes**: A yellow and purple, vase-shaped tunicate. Very striking, but it usually starves without an abundance of phytoplankton.
textos.0fba352689e007cf: **Notes**: Dark body speckled with light spots. Nocturnal and an ambush hunter.
textos.b10d7d54dc5cd204: **Notes**: An elongated, free-living coral covered with short tentacles. It lives on the sand.
textos.67cc5e71112d3b43: **Notes**: Dark vertical stripes on a greenish background. Sturdy and slow-growing.
textos.518ee7baf54ab312: **Notes**: A large bichir with dark bands and a prominent lower jaw. It grows quite large.
textos.5c3e75ddc7e9d85d: **Notes**: The most striking bichir, with a black-and-white net-like pattern. Grows quite large; make sure the lid fits snugly.
textos.e9196892f603d601: **Notes**: Moderately sized bichir with dark spots. Tight-fitting lid.
textos.fd1911fd79520b4b: **Notes**: A prehistoric fish with primitive lungs that comes to the surface to breathe. An escape artist: the lid must be tightly closed with no gaps.
textos.421c4b614ea976ce: **Notes**: Orange-brown with curved blue lines and a blue ring above the operculum. Large and long-lived.
textos.b8940121bf7e4bce: **Notes**: Known as the gray angelfish: juveniles are black with yellow bands. Very long-lived and large.
textos.7852147ddc8bcedd: **Notes**: Dark blue with a crescent-shaped yellow stripe and a yellow tail. Hardy.
textos.fbcf9e2b8d2602d6: **Notes**: The color change from juvenile (white and blue rings on a black background) to adult (horizontal yellow and blue stripes) is one of the most spectacular phenomena in the marine hobby. Suitable only for very large aquariums. Hard to wean onto flake food without experience.
textos.eca009916e0a9bd1: **Notes**: Violet-blue with a crescent-shaped yellow spot. Very hardy and long-lived.

textos.59efbcc4015f4a00: **Notes**: Juveniles are dark blue with white semicircles; as adults, they turn greenish with blue spots. One of the hardiest large angelfish.
textos.fc7e8d16f3949490: **Notes**: Blue face with a yellow mask and yellow scales edged with blue. Spectacular as an adult.

textos.7b4c0faaa98b9b09: **Notes**: Electric blue with yellowish rear fins. A good choice for a reef tank with small fish.
textos.50964804fbaad996: **Notes**: Electric blue with a yellow belly and tail. Hardy.

textos.018e8fa730126c0a: **Notes**: Heart-shaped leaves and spikes of blue flowers in summer. Very decorative along the water’s edge.
textos.459325a764b793aa: **Notes**: Smooth, finger-like branches in yellow, green, or blue. One of the hardiest SPS corals.
textos.8f1504398379cc93: **Notes**: Irregular brown or cream-colored plates and columns. Hardy.
textos.16d3da8e9ec9271f: **Notes**: Its eyes shimmer with a neon blue sheen. A small, peaceful schooling fish for planted aquariums.
textos.98c8318a83cc3980: **Notes**: Wavy leaves with serrated edges. A native cold-water plant that grows in winter and spring.
textos.ed1212d2b212c620: **Notes**: Black with white spots; one of the most sought-after stingrays. Venomous stinger; pristine water and a large sandy bottom.

textos.9895750f0c3f7470: **Notes**: Males are silvery blue with large fins. A fish found in fast-flowing streams with well-oxygenated water.

textos.d17b25431b706daf: **Notes**: Cream-colored body with chocolate-brown bumps. Hardy, but feeds on corals and clams.

textos.e038f9a4e5fb3595: **Notes**: Flattened branches with a velvety surface, green or brown. Easy to care for and fast-growing.

textos.699999855fb77279: **Notes**: Body covered with short spines and fins with reddish edges in some localities. Large and territorial.
textos.40835940da112679: **Notes**: Violet front half and yellow rear half. One of the hardiest anthias for a reef tank.
textos.1962f755ca176cfc: **Notes**: Upper half orange and belly lilac; males have two filaments on the dorsal fin.
textos.c20738fe478c64bd: **Notes**: Males are golden orange with a red dorsal fin and violet lips. Delicate during shipping.
textos.5d8afffc7e2115f4: **Notes**: Violet body with a yellow back and tail. Lives in large schools.

textos.9b40c665d57f95e8: **Notes**: Related to the six-line wrasse, with eight dark lines on a pink background. Slightly more aggressive.

textos.de42c9c6b653fc8a: **Notes**: Known as the “neon dottyback”: orange with a neon blue stripe. Very territorial; add last.
textos.2c5f7bc1ce482041: **Notes**: Yellow with a purple stripe along the back. Small but very territorial.
textos.f63d70efc5e708a5: **Notes**: Blue body with a yellow back. More docile than other Pseudochromis species.
textos.4bf568166d8de4fd: **Notes**: Deep purple with a dark line across the eye. Captive-bred specimens are easy to find. Very hardy.

textos.517e88cb6cbf8784: **Notes**: Known as the spotted “hillstream loach.” Easy to breed; cool water with a current.
textos.d24680c0b91114b7: **Notes**: Very flattened body with sand-colored camouflage. It burrows into the substrate and is difficult to spot.
textos.5fd9150a149bd713: **Notes**: Elongated body; males are green with a blue stripe, and females are cherry pink. Requires sand for sleeping.
textos.6c5b2c12b817942d: **Notes**: Males have a bright blue back. It lives in freshwater and brackish water in mangrove swamps.

textos.f8add00a9bded5c8: **Notes**: Large fins with black spots that males spread out during courtship. Tiny and delicate during transport, but easy to care for once acclimated.
textos.4929169a6de98488: **Notes**: Males are orange with black and yellow fins. Tiny and very colorful.
textos.804747c02ccb49a1: **Notes**: Males are orange-red with yellow fins and blue eyes. Tiny and very striking in nano tanks.
textos.7ee753a4619a076d: **Notes**: Males are reddish with yellow fins and blue eyes. Small and suitable for nano tanks.
textos.12a1f28c7de91034: **Notes**: Light blue eyes and yellow fins with black edges. Highly adaptable; lives in both freshwater and brackish water.

textos.dc5f9f0d2e1c5ccb: **Notes**: A small relative of the paradise fish, with a reddish belly during the breeding season. Easy to care for and peaceful.
textos.ec72798f22762958: **Notes**: Brown body with two dark lines and fins edged in blue and red, with an elongated tail.

textos.8e84f1f7a3694b76: **Notes**: Vertical dark blue and light blue bands. Small but very aggressive: keep only in large groups and with plenty of rock.
