textos.3d738c50bd91ed0e: **Notes**: Long fins with black bands and white spots. Endangered species: Buy only captive-bred specimens, which are easy to find. Slow and calm.
textos.5849967229b80ba1: **Notes**: Bluish body with a black rear section. Fast and a jumper; swims in midwater above the rocks.
textos.e642cc9f5792928d: **Notes**: Pale blue body with a dark spot on the tail. Jumper; mesh lid.
textos.e63b938f1589e9cd: **Notes**: Greenish body with thin pink vertical stripes. Lives in groups and jumps: mesh lid.
textos.79a08a0cc96fc41c: **Notes**: Spotted pectoral fins and antennae above the eyes. Venomous, like all lionfish.
textos.edd7020e50101125: **Notes**: Very similar to the common lionfish. An invasive species spreading throughout the Mediterranean: it should never be released into the wild.
textos.1cc8e82360028385: **Notes**: Wide reddish bands and long, thin white pectoral spines. Venomous spines: handle with care.
textos.5695478f8c7cb0f7: **Notes**: ⚠️ The dorsal, pelvic, and anal spines are VENOMOUS: severe pain, nausea. Handle with long nets and gloves. It can be trained to eat frozen fish moved on a stick. Very calm and slow-moving: it stalks its prey and waits. A devastating invasive species if released into the wild.
textos.ef022a8030d100ff: **Notes**: The tallest and most majestic angelfish. It requires very soft, acidic, and warm water, as well as a tall aquarium with vertical roots. It is very sensitive to sudden changes.
textos.6e5777ffe8b2f865: **Notes**: The smallest angelfish, with a dark spot at the base of the dorsal fin. More shy than the common angelfish.
textos.f0b7b47761bae6fb: **Notes**: Eats small fish that fit in its mouth (Neon tetras are not compatible). A tall aquarium is essential due to its dorsal fin. Forms stable, monogamous pairs.
textos.d6f5c9bdba43c6a1: **Notes**: Enormous, sail-shaped dorsal fin and leopard-like markings. Produces a great deal of waste: requires powerful filtration. Sold as a juvenile but grows quickly; not suitable as a glass cleaner for medium-sized aquariums.
textos.f25cb555199b35e8: **Notes**: Known as L001. Black with gold spots. Smaller than the sailfin pleco, but still requires a large aquarium.
textos.75d56e5d128c8934: **Notes**: Related to the sailfin pleco, with a spotted pattern. Grows very large; considered invasive in many tropical countries.
textos.05244bc12bfed879: **Notes**: Very similar to the sailfin pleco, with a striped pattern. An invasive species in many tropical countries: it should never be released into the wild.
textos.d196488abbf4cf1f: **Notes**: Males are red with dark bands and a yellow belly. Many species from Lake Victoria have become extinct; aquarists help conserve them.
textos.c5e2be873adcc498: **Notes**: A relative of the three-spined stickleback, with nine small spines along its back. Males turn black during the breeding season.
textos.dd302a900613df35: **Notes**: Similar to the tiger barb but with an additional, incomplete stripe. Slightly less aggressive.
textos.68008bc28c8d816e: **Notes**: Four vertical black stripes on a gold background. Very active and hardy. Never keep with angelfish, bettas, or gouramis; best kept with fast-swimming, short-finned fish.
textos.de0bb7ef8118d249: **Notes**: Small greenish barb with dark spots and orange fins. Peaceful.
textos.7e4c1aa22b17daff: **Notes**: More skittish than its reputation suggests: it becomes stressed with little cover. Be very careful with your hands during maintenance. In Spain, keeping this species is not prohibited, but check the regulations in your region.
textos.b87c6d6305f7d435: **Notes**: Orange, white, and blue stripes. One of the most beautiful reef fish and one of the most difficult to keep; those from the Red Sea adapt better.
textos.a9b5f8722b642f4f: **Notes**: Elongated body with red spots and a dark line across the eye. Peaceful, surface-dwelling.
textos.61358cb0616ebfbd: **Notes**: The “king of goldfish” in Japan—highly prized in competitions. No dorsal fin = reduced stability. Swims with a characteristic swaying motion. For experts.
textos.9883b6397f0631b5: **Notes**: Thin submerged leaves and white flowers above the water in spring. A plant native to cold ponds.
textos.abc08296523b7381: **Notes**: Black line with a gold border and a red tail base. Unfussy, hardy, and very active in groups.
textos.4970acff6cae1840: **Notes**: Known as the giant scissortail rasbora: tail lobes with red and black edges. A strong swimmer.
textos.b90f18df58e0c501: **Notes**: Known as the dotted rasbora: a line of dark dots runs along its silvery body.
textos.e49091c40c9cf47b: **Notes**: Silvery with a thin black lateral line. Very hardy and active.
textos.4be30c01893294e5: **Notes**: Known as the “hi-spot rasbora” because of the black spot with a white border on its dorsal fin. Calm and elegant.
textos.3fdcfbec90589eb2: **Notes**: Silver with a black line running from the snout to the tail, set against a golden sheen. Calm and elegant in large groups.
textos.ff6df9b2690b677f: **Notes**: Silvery with a black spot on its side and another at the base of its tail. Large and calm.
textos.9f51d1c744c34675: **Notes**: Orange-pink body with two large dark spots. A peat swamp fish that requires very soft, acidic water.
textos.7feaf3cdff4bd7ec: **Notes**: A bright coppery-red line on a dark band. Shy; shows its best color in dark, planted aquariums.
textos.727af62b1d2f21c9: **Notes**: Silvery with a dark lateral line and reddish fins. Active and hardy.
textos.1c858a58f9ab87db: **Notes**: Scissor-shaped tail with black and white spots that appears to open and close as it swims. It grows larger than it appears in the store: it needs a long aquarium.
textos.7ce77618d02cedf7: **Notes**: A rasbora with a bright red rear section, like lava. Recently described and very striking.
textos.cb270599dc168240: **Notes**: Males are bright orange with reddish fins. An endangered species found in rainforest streams; prefers a gentle current and shade.
textos.657d7de11fc7306a: **Notes**: A small rainbowfish with iridescent scales and red or blue fins, depending on the location. Soft water.
textos.f7cda4288456774b: **Notes**: Color pattern like a Picasso painting. Very intelligent and curious; interacts with its owner. May bite thermometers, hoses, cables, and fingers. The dorsal fin has a “trigger” mechanism that allows it to lock itself into crevices. Never keep in a reef tank.
textos.9ccafc5d8e324734: **Notes**: Related to the Picasso triggerfish, with a dark diagonal stripe and a black, arrow-shaped spot near the tail.
textos.3c4d948d2ee66f86: **Notes**: Males have two spots on the dorsal fin and lines on their cheeks. Cool water with a current.
textos.b4f785f709356c94: **Notes**: Males have red cheeks and fins with blue edges. A cool-water stream goby, suitable for tanks without a heater.
textos.d4ae4e0276758ff2: **Notes**: A blue and yellow ribbon with leaf-shaped nostrils. It almost always starves to death in an aquarium: not recommended.
textos.d1ba028b265cb04c: **Notes**: Mangroves are the symbol of the brackish water biotope. They are planted with their roots submerged in brackish water and their stems above the water. They grow very slowly (taking years to reach 30 cm). They require plenty of light to prevent etiolation. Propagules can be purchased at specialty stores: these are seedlings with already-formed roots. Over time, they create a spectacular mangrove aquarium-terrarium.
textos.a7302825e3c2de82: **Notes**: Mushrooms with a fuzzy surface and small bumps. Very easy and prolific: it reproduces on its own by division.
textos.c99dcb60635836ed: **Notes**: Males in breeding season turn violet and red. Their reproduction depends on a freshwater bivalve—a fascinating relationship. Suitable for cold-water aquariums or ponds.
textos.9bb3ed90e9362d92: **Notes**: Red and white stripes and a hump on the back. Lives in groups; best suited for FOWLR or reef tanks without delicate soft corals.
textos.dfd9266760a1ce05: **Notes**: A liverwort that forms dense, compact cushions, perfect for adding detail to nano tanks and rock landscapes.
textos.449b1361a7fb658b: **Notes**: A liverwort that forms light green clumps. When tied with netting to a rock, it creates mats with sparkling oxygen bubbles. When floating, it serves as a refuge for fry.
textos.60b568149c1396e8: **Notes**: A liverwort similar to the common Riccia, with slightly thinner branches. It forms mats with oxygen bubbles.
textos.fb26248a287dba6e: **Notes**: Heart-shaped floating liverwort with purple roots. Decorative and provides shelter for fry.
textos.ff7b66e088405f95: **Notes**: Surface covered with rounded tentacles that give it a plush or flower-like appearance. Very striking colors (green, orange, blue, purple). Slightly more demanding than Discosoma but very manageable. Responds well to direct feeding with mysis to grow faster. Highly sought after for its unique colors.
textos.837f37183916e430: **Notes**: Indo-Pacific version of R. florida. Longer tentacles. Very striking colors that fluoresce under blue light. Slightly more sensitive to water parameters than R. florida. High-quality specimens are highly sought after.
textos.85d12616d961a8a9: **Notes**: A marbled-patterned whip-tailed Loricaria. It breeds easily in tubes. There is a very striking red variant bred in captivity.
textos.1d5a68100bee3c23: **Notes**: Known as the whip-tailed Loricaria because of its long, slender tail. It goes unnoticed on the sand thanks to its camouflage. Peaceful and easy to breed.
textos.d0728ab3c43b4de6: **Notes**: Dark with turquoise-blue and gold spots. It is named after a boxer because of its temperament. There is a bred variety called “Electric Blue,” which is more delicate and somewhat less aggressive.
textos.216a4ab3771d12af: **Notes**: Needle-like leaves that turn a deep pink. Demanding; prized in aquascaping.
textos.4fa79f735e473347: **Notes**: Small leaves that turn pink at the tips in bright light. Stores usually sell it under the name Rotala rotundifolia, which is very similar. Prune by trimming the tips to encourage branching.
textos.3ce6c3da665a9dd3: **Notes**: The most spectacular red stem plant. Without stable CO2 and very strong lighting, the leaves turn green. For advanced aquarists only.
textos.0002a37640c2d16b: **Notes**: Thin leaves arranged in whorls that turn yellow or orange in bright light. Delicate with fragile stems.
textos.b0fe56cd8cc2f90a: **Notes**: Broad, pink leaves when provided with good light and iron; commonly known in stores as “Florida.” Adds color to planted tanks.
textos.f1d60f116b9b3da3: **Notes**: With CO2 and high light, the leaves turn coral/reddish-orange. The most popular pink stem plant.
textos.9fe5adc2bb41fa54: **Notes**: Needle-like leaves that form rosy-red tufts. Very demanding: it wilts if there isn’t enough CO2 or iron. Spectacular in Dutch-style planted tanks.
textos.8f3f8a0593603c7b: **Notes**: The hardiest fancy. Distinctive hump. Active and vigorous. Suitable for indoor aquariums or temperate ponds without harsh winters.
textos.6f51a26390d728f3: **Notes**: A tubeworm with a large, spiral-shaped crown of tentacles. It requires powdered food or phytoplankton.
textos.06de4ab73deaea7b: **Notes**: It lives in a tube and unfurls a crown of feathery tentacles, which it retracts instantly if anything approaches. Some angelfish and butterflyfish eat them.
textos.8165ec0eecabecd8: **Notes**: Thin, ribbon-like leaves that form clumps. Very hardy and also suitable for ponds.
textos.096961f66c48e3fc: **Notes**: Wide, ribbon-like leaves that form clumps. Very hardy; also thrives in ponds.
textos.adc7e7e8b32f5b79: **Notes**: Short, ribbon-like leaves that carpet the substrate without requiring CO2. An easy alternative to hairgrass in community aquariums.
textos.1806edc85826020e: **Notes**: Arrowhead-shaped leaves and white flowers. Native to still waters.
textos.55255201f85e7fb8: **Notes**: Very similar to Vallisneria but more compact. Tolerates hard, alkaline water.
textos.db48788b27846f01: **Notes**: A relative of the Denison barb with a shorter red stripe and a black spot on the dorsal fin. Endangered species.
textos.494350c923b1c977: **Notes**: A red stripe running from the snout to the midline, and a tail with yellow and black spots. Requires well-oxygenated water with a current and a long aquarium. Endangered in the wild: please purchase captive-bred specimens.
textos.0a517b54cb5c8312: **Notes**: Known as the “lawnmower” because of the way it scrapes away filamentous algae. It needs a well-established aquarium with algae; without it, it goes hungry. It has an expressive face with cirri above its eyes.
textos.3e53cb756255077a: **Notes**: A relative of the lawnmower blenny with light spots. It eats filamentous algae.
textos.059e0263b746dad9: **Notes**: Reduces light in the aquarium. Provides shelter for fry and shrimp. Make sure it doesn’t cover the entire surface.
textos.f1f8f173b7f9b9ab: **Notes**: A floating plant that filters nitrates, reduces light (useful for shrimp that prefer low light), and creates refuge areas at the surface. Shrimp rise to the surface to forage among the roots. Make sure it doesn’t cover the entire surface and prevent gas exchange.
textos.4d38cc343cf7cfbb: **Notes**: Free-living coral with an oval, dome-shaped form. It lives on the sand.
textos.d07dd7061a4d9b02: **Notes**: Leather mushroom coral with long polyps. Very hardy; periodically sheds a layer of skin.
textos.50ed686cc1e9c447: **Notes**: Shaped like a giant mushroom. Releases terpenoids that may inhibit the growth of nearby corals. Use activated carbon to counteract this. Periodically, the coral “closes up” and becomes covered in mucus, which it later sheds: this is normal behavior.
textos.0fbc68124efdef8c: **Notes**: Red with white stripes and enormous eyes typical of a nocturnal fish. It spends the day hidden.
textos.bb013004c7b7ff60: **Notes**: Marbled body with tufts. Nocturnal and elusive; may feed on small invertebrates.
textos.5a4c89123e042992: **Notes**: Two or three large black spots on the side. A blackwater fish that is very sensitive to water quality.
textos.2dacaa0223035eb8: **Notes**: An “eartheater” that spends the day sifting sand through its gills: it needs fine, soft sand. Sensitive to poor water quality.
textos.80958bc6435e84a7: **Notes**: Very similar to the jurupari, with blue lines on its face. It is often sold under that name.
textos.8c8d489e127a092f: **Notes**: Known as the Inle red-nosed rasbora: males are silvery blue and scaleless, with a red snout. Hard, cool water.
textos.b60f3a526451d6ce: **Notes**: A European fish found in shallow waters. Red fins, golden scales. Active at the surface. Feeds on insects, algae, and floating plants. Colorful and agile.
textos.ed9be085302a2254: **Notes**: Greenish body covered with dark spots. Eats practically everything, including plants. The spines on its fins are venomous: be careful when handling it.
textos.8612965f5bb5f268: **Notes**: Dark stripes on a golden background. A stream loach that requires a current and oxygen.
textos.766956c50d8b17df: **Notes**: Dark bands on a light background. A stream loach that requires oxygen.
textos.0ec55b074d47cdff: **Notes**: Larger than the “electric blue” (S. fryeri), with a reddish anal fin in males.
textos.eaa2bb5df5e48043: **Notes**: Males are a vivid electric blue with a white edge on the dorsal fin. A strong swimmer, it requires a long aquarium.
textos.e120d6e48a98e232: **Notes**: The largest of the “corydoras,” with the males’ heads covered in bristles. It requires cooler water than usual and good oxygenation.
textos.e99ed7c3d192480d: **Notes**: A relative of Corydoras barbatus, with golden spots. Cool, well-oxygenated water.
textos.88299588bdefd5a1: **Notes**: Known as L014. Black with golden-yellow spots and fins with yellow edges. Eats snails with its specialized teeth.
textos.f18e2fb88945f424: **Notes**: Tropical ferns require high humidity (>70%), which a paludarium naturally provides. Selaginella is more tolerant; Adiantum is more delicate but very ornamental. Perfect for creating the look of tropical undergrowth in the land area.
textos.64f641c68ecddf37: **Notes**: Silvery with dark vertical bands. A relative of the spotted scat, just as greedy and fond of brackish water.
textos.c1d53b88b50bd8d9: **Notes**: Silvery with a black-and-white striped tail and reddish fins. It scrapes algae and biofilm; it grows quite large.
textos.a919e08b71135110: **Notes**: Flat shell, like a limpet, that clings to rocks. It feeds on film algae very effectively.
textos.cdbcdacb87395348: **Notes**: Branches are thicker than those of Seriatopora hystrix, forming clumps resembling bird's nests. Very sensitive to changes in alkalinity.
textos.307e6d928f358be1: **Notes**: Extremely fine, dense branches resembling a bird’s nest. Very fragile structurally. Striking colors (pink, green, yellow). For aquarists with experience with SPS corals.
textos.eae1e4c61721a329: **Notes**: A relative of the bird’s nest coral, with thicker branches and a star-like appearance.
textos.e9955a292f72a7b4: **Notes**: Known as the “sunburst anthias”: orange-pink with yellow lines extending from the eye. It lives alone and is easier to care for than other anthias.
textos.83b85c5ee4531f2c: **Notes**: Known as “lantern bass”: body with orange spots and dark bands. Small.
textos.f5420070b7f966a3: **Notes**: Brown vertical bands and orange lines on the face. Mediterranean predator.
textos.c26d87c99d638a8d: **Notes**: The lines on its head resemble writing, hence its scientific name. It preys on small fish.
textos.c5d2f63db0754d85: **Notes**: Known as the chalk bass. Pale blue and orange bands. Unlike almost all groupers, it is small, peaceful, and can live in groups.
textos.1f501546a5836a1d: **Notes**: Red eyes and dark body. Unlike the red-bellied piranha, it must be kept alone. Be very careful with your hands.
textos.35f81b24d02f43e5: **Notes**: Body flattened like a suction cup to cling to rocks in fast-flowing rivers. Requires strong currents, cool, well-oxygenated water, and rocks covered with biofilm.
textos.ea280d6f3a868609: **Notes**: Lobed leaves like those of an oak. Easy to grow and fast-growing.
textos.4ff3ab336f35d440: **Notes**: The only truly blue goldfish (although the blue color is genetically unstable). Very hardy.
textos.ee6f56a48c16ac64: **Notes**: Blue and yellow lines and dark bands on the head. A good algae eater.
textos.8a85e5d5f247fa0b: **Notes**: Related to the foxface rabbitfish, with a black stripe along its side. Venomous spines.
textos.41fbbe08b0ae4dcb: **Notes**: Body covered with dark spots and a yellow tail. Large; venomous spines.
textos.3e8dc27b39ecd7f7: **Notes**: Yellow with a white and black face reminiscent of a fox. Its spines are venomous and cause very painful stings. Useful for controlling nuisance algae.
textos.90c0a1005e8b2579: **Reef Safe**: ⚠️ Use caution (may nip soft corals and zoanthids)
textos.eb299883f6395888: **Notes**: Known as the “crab-eye goby” because of the two ocelli on its fins, which resemble eyes. It often starves to death in aquariums without a mature sand bed.
textos.5f3fcce9a6a1c698: **Notes**: Greenish body with rows of dark spots. A rock-dwelling herbivore, related to the Tropheus genus.
textos.f1daf0ac36cdc417: **Notes**: Soft coral with short, star-shaped lobes. Easy to care for and attractive.
textos.f0221a0b4846031c: **Notes**: Known as “cabbage coral”: wavy lobes resembling cabbage leaves. Very hardy.
textos.e6af414d6384af30: **Notes**: Thin, flexible branches that sway with the current. Hardy and fast-growing. Like other leather corals, it sometimes closes up for a few days to shed a layer of skin.
textos.05f7f760df52d391: **Notes**: Soft coral with short lobes and green polyps. Easy for beginners.
textos.724321bed6093093: **Notes**: Males have irregular black spots on a golden background. An endangered goodeid, preserved by hobbyists.
textos.5017ab0023140965: **Notes**: A snout flattened like a shovel and a black lateral stripe. It spends the day motionless among roots, often upside down. Suitable only for very large aquariums.
textos.536a3ab3ec16a8b4: **Notes**: A cichlid goby with blue spots on a dark background. It lives in the surf zone; highly oxygenated water.
textos.304e58f4fe3a8a68: **Notes**: Black with small white spots. A rapids pleco that requires a current and warm water.
textos.444a2150e2da3e63: **Notes**: Yellow head, dark band down the center, and a red-speckled rear, like pajamas. Nocturnal but visible during the day. Very peaceful in groups.
textos.b990c3674bf31189: **Notes**: Silver with a dark vertical band and black spots. Very hardy; tolerates slightly less salty water.
textos.f758589554b8e024: **Notes**: Chocolate brown with golden bands. A peat swamp fish that requires very soft, acidic blackwater, dried leaves, and peaceful tankmates. Very susceptible to infections in hard water.
textos.a334e71015765440: **Notes**: Related to the chocolate gourami; the female turns red with green bands during courtship. Requires extreme blackwater conditions.
textos.04f45e228e4a86e3: **Notes**: Brightly colored spiral crowns emerging from tubes carved into Porites corals. They are sold attached to the rock or coral where they live.
textos.1edf40922c70fa24: **Notes**: Larger than common duckweed, with a purple underside. It absorbs a lot of nutrients and feeds herbivorous fish.
textos.222546800c396f7f: **Notes**: A small, stemmed plant that forms compact clumps in the foreground. Much easier to care for than traditional ground cover plants and does not come loose from the substrate easily.
textos.754ba104f449ec98: **Notes**: Males have a large hump on their heads. A rapids fish that hops along the bottom; it appreciates current and caves.
textos.4e39ca6bd6a6b2ba: **Notes**: Red and white stripes and long pincers. Keep only one per aquarium, unless they are a mated pair. It occasionally removes parasites from the fish.
textos.41c29c27ae3b54b5: **Notes**: Small, golden-colored boxer shrimp with red bands. One per aquarium.
textos.c8a24a184795f1c2: **Notes**: Triangular body with very long legs. Effective against fireworms, but may attack small, sleeping fish.
textos.9de3b2d0ba0bdae1: **Notes**: A very sticky carpet anemone capable of eating fish. Demanding and dangerous to other tank inhabitants.
textos.15f6749f5f6701dc: **Notes**: A carpet of short, sticky tentacles, often green or purple. Hosts clownfish such as A. clarkii and A. sebae.
textos.514cebe16081a9ef: **Notes**: The largest anemone on the reef; it can grow to over one meter. Suitable only for very large, dedicated aquariums.
textos.4ea30fa78d179e35: **Notes**: Three dark spots on the side; males have blue and yellow hues. Requires large tankmates.
textos.b6da04b72d66967e: **Notes**: Silvery body with black spots and tall dorsal fins. Mildly brackish water.
textos.bf8f06ff453dd8a9: **Notes**: Males are iridescent electric blue. A mountain stream goby that requires a current, rocks with biofilm, and a cover.
textos.42e1e2568efdf82e: **Notes**: A small snail whose shell does not cover its entire body. It arrives with live rock and reproduces without causing any problems.
textos.9dd67f2b8ae76ffa: **Notes**: Diagonal black stripes, yellow head, and a long filament on the dorsal fin. It lives with pistol shrimp.
textos.1b9161da99bb23e5: **Notes**: White with orange stripes and a tall dorsal fin. It lives in symbiosis with the pistol shrimp Alpheus randalli: she digs the burrow, and he stands guard.
textos.6e64b9801b51673b: **Notes**: Dark horizontal lines on a gold background. A peaceful softwater barb.
textos.440214e8c8c6b2e8: **Notes**: Elongated golden body with long filaments on the dorsal and caudal fins. Elegant but demanding in terms of water quality.
textos.c06438fc7740c6a2: **Notes**: Elongated body with a long filament on the tail. Requires very clean, well-oxygenated water and does not compete well for food with voracious fish.
textos.88507f90034595ac: **Notes**: Club-shaped branches with rounded tips. Very common in the Red Sea. Colors: pink, purple, green, brown. Light-colored tips indicate active growth; dark or brown tips indicate stress.
textos.aef42e2cf2c1b36f: **Notes**: Short, rounded branches in shades of pink or green. Tolerant for an SPS.
textos.1129fa940d30c1d0: **Notes**: Gray with a white line extending from the mouth and a dark mark behind the eye. One of the calmest triggerfish.
textos.bb3649fd771999ed: **Notes**: Brown with a bluish belly and a tail with a white edge. Relatively calm.
textos.724931b86457b673: **Notes**: Tiny, with blue-green and red iridescence in males. Extreme blackwater conditions; only for dedicated nano tanks.
textos.3c555645f34bbfdd: **Notes**: A small Mediterranean wrasse with a blue and red spot on its operculum. Very common in coastal seagrass beds.
textos.f7603d9f3524875f: **Notes**: The king of the tropical aquarium. Fry feed on their parents’ slime coat for 2 weeks: do not separate the family. Perform 30% water changes every 2–3 days. The temperature of 30°C severely limits the types of plants that are compatible. Many varieties: cobalt blue, red turquoise, pigeon blood, leopard.
textos.f019a41dbe9af474: **Notes**: A small, reddish, camouflaged dragonet with a tall dorsal fin. Requires plenty of microfauna.
textos.1262185814d589d8: **Notes**: A relative of the mandarin fish, with a tall, mottled dorsal fin. Like the mandarin fish, it requires a well-established aquarium with plenty of live rock and a population of copepods.
textos.104757d54025733b: **Notes**: Known as the spotted mandarin: green ocelli edged with black and orange. Requires an abundant population of copepods.
textos.f165961101ade858: **Notes**: The most colorful fish on the planet (structural color: blue, green, orange). Scaleless: skin covered in bitter mucus. Eats ONLY live copepods: the refugium must have an active breeding population. Only for experienced aquarists who culture copepods.
textos.d04aac2e6c170932: **Notes**: Dark stripes and spots on a yellowish background, and fins with spots. Territorial and large in size.
textos.413a7edd806d09f1: **Notes**: Thin greenish stripes on a golden background. One of the more aggressive loaches; best kept with hardy fish.
textos.e4f7554f8348f250: **Notes**: Very long barbels and a mottled body. Peaceful and nocturnal.
textos.930b4e4052b1a9f9: **Notes**: Dark body covered with white or golden spots and banded fins. One of the most beautiful and expensive Synodontis species.
textos.c4fa581a13dec8ff: **Notes**: Light vertical stripes on a dark background. Flattened body typical of a rapids fish; thrives in a current.
textos.1d70f332f9233abb: **Notes**: Large black spots on a light background and a long filament on the dorsal fin. It grows quite large but is very peaceful.
textos.0185e07e4399dd40: **Notes**: Known as the “featherfin synodontis” because of its tall, filamentous dorsal fin. Very hardy and long-lived.
textos.fe4bf229799fac2b: **Notes**: Yellow and brown horizontal stripes. Peaceful and active at dusk.
textos.db9b3eff6639c88d: **Notes**: Body with dark spots and banded fins. Sturdy and peaceful.
textos.74ed4fb72062aa21: **Notes**: Very similar to Synodontis petricola; often sold under that name. Black spots on a cream-colored background.
textos.0ac8db1438827e44: **Notes**: Black spots on a cream-colored background and fins with white edges. Famous for its “cuckoo” breeding behavior with Malawi and Tanganyika cichlids.
textos.498026b09e897e42: **Notes**: It almost always floats on its back to feed under leaves and at the surface; that’s why its belly is dark. Very social and nocturnal. Provide roots and driftwood where it can rest upside down.
textos.d6c33de1a72dce3e: **Notes**: The only Synodontis species from Lake Malawi, ideal for keeping with mbunas and peacocks. Dark spots on a grayish background.
textos.b9a4e11794c2083a: **Notes**: Light-colored body with dark, edged spots, resembling ocelli. Large but peaceful.
textos.9f18658c627adedb: **Notes**: Black spots on a cream-colored background and fins with white edges. A good tankmate for cichlids from Lake Tanganyika and Lake Malawi. Most active at dusk; needs crevices among the rocks.
textos.55e9965f8d07ad73: **Notes**: Medium-sized spotted Synodontis. Nocturnal and sociable.
textos.9f75fdbe294a38d9: **Notes**: Yellow and brown mottled pattern. Calm and nocturnal.
textos.74f2fc3d4dfb9938: **Notes**: An elongated dwarf cichlid, almost pencil-like, with sharply pointed fins. Requires extreme blackwater conditions and live food.
textos.e9e8dde038b2a3b4: **Notes**: Resembles a leaf swaying in the current. Sheds its skin periodically. Venomous spines.
textos.f8aa20cd866dbf6a: **Notes**: A small “cichlid goby” that lives among rocks on the wave-swept shore. It requires strong currents and plenty of oxygen; it moves by hopping along the bottom.
textos.85b808049c1e59b3: **Notes**: Ideal for aquariums without a heater. Golden stripe and fins with red edges. Nearly extinct in the wild, it survives thanks to the aquarium hobby. Continuous heat above 25 °C shortens its lifespan.
textos.509f1c229011f920: **Notes**: Related to the white cloud mountain minnow, with one golden stripe and one bright blue stripe. Suitable for nano tanks without a heater.
textos.fd49589266d1d39c: **Notes**: A relative of the Malaysian trumpet snail, with a dark, granulated shell. Invasive outside its native range: never release it.
textos.95b244b46ff252ea: **Notes**: Lavender-blue body with red spots and a black ocellus on the tail. One of the most beautiful and peaceful freshwater gobies for planted aquariums.
textos.14fe5028976df627: **Notes**: Spotted like a leopard. Hides in cracks in wood during the day.
textos.d9f1591b5584abdd: **Notes**: Known as “Taiwan moss.” Branches grow in triangular fans, more orderly than Java moss. Excellent shelter for fry and shrimp.
textos.9a0bfaf01a41f1e0: **Notes**: Goldfish eat it as a dietary supplement. It does not last as a main decorative plant but can be kept as a natural snack. It adds a natural touch.
textos.c90d91146866cf0d: **Notes**: The stems grow in a vertical spiral, resembling flames. Very decorative. It grows more slowly than Java moss.
textos.4fdf1aebdb626bbd: **Notes**: A moss with pointed, neatly arranged branches, more attractive than Java moss. Easy to care for and suitable for shrimp.
textos.8a7222a922123be5: **Notes**: A top snail with a conical shell that cleans film algae. It rights itself if it falls over.
textos.c0559941233b05a4: **Notes**: Elongated body like a goby; the female has a dorsal fin with a red edge. It lives among rocks in highly oxygenated rapids.
textos.d42bd028f1e0ba8c: **Notes**: The eyes are protruding and vulnerable to injury. Do not keep with elongated-bodied fish. Avoid decorations with sharp edges. The Black Moor may turn orange with age and higher temperatures (this is normal).
textos.0b2752d1b3219c26: **Notes**: A small cichlid with two dark horizontal stripes. It inhabits large shells and crevices; a good tankmate for shell-dwelling fish in small Tanganyika aquariums.
textos.1f30a2286b1435fa: **Notes**: Elongated body with a dark lateral line. It inhabits shells or crevices to breed.
textos.e3fb538552f5d7ed: **Notes**: The largest freshwater pufferfish. Very intelligent and full of personality, but it requires a huge aquarium and a very powerful filtration system.
textos.6a372ff8f54484ae: **Notes**: African freshwater pufferfish, yellowish with dark spots. Less aggressive than others.
textos.467e3f79c1f15ec8: **Notes**: A triangular-shaped boxfish with a hump on its back. Like all boxfish, it releases toxins.
textos.29da85d56c257a5d: **Notes**: A seagrass, a true plant with roots. Requires at least 10 cm of fine sand and bright light.
textos.cac2e81b2e4dab10: **Notes**: Terminal-phase males have blue heads, black and white bands, and green bodies. The initial phases are yellow.
textos.938103f91f8383d9: **Notes**: Green with short black bars along the back and pink lines on the head. A tireless swimmer.
textos.7a651a4399802493: **Notes**: Adults have mesmerizing colors: green with pink stripes on the head and a yellow tail with a lunule. One of the most active and conspicuous wrasses. It attacks other fish unpredictably, especially newly introduced ones. It eats all invertebrates. It buries itself in the sand to sleep.
textos.e42b268b19521c92: **Notes**: A relative of the moon wrasse, greenish-yellow in color with a pink head. Very active.
textos.10dcd7bde01e7b8a: **Notes**: Green Mediterranean wrasse with blue lines on the head; males have a vertical blue and red band. Very active.
textos.bf2d734ab2fce429: **Notes**: Large, waxy leaves and purple flower stalks. Adds height and a tropical touch to the pond.
textos.23ff346947fb43ad: **Notes**: A black line runs along the body and down the lower lobe of the tail. Swims at a slight angle with its head pointing upward. Active and a jumper: the aquarium needs a lid.
textos.5a3fe31db5d14e6e: **Notes**: Related to the penguin tetra, with the black stripe only on the rear of the body. Swims at an angle.
textos.5e2abc6865003e17: **Notes**: The smallest shrimp in the hobby. It’s called the “sexy shrimp” because it continuously moves its abdomen in a rhythmic manner. It takes refuge in anemones or soft corals. It’s very eye-catching when kept in a group.
textos.b11f363e37b7e643: **Notes**: The largest hatchetfish, silvery with a spotted dorsal fin. Jumps; a lid is essential.
textos.1ceca16f8cd49064: **Notes**: A relative of the firemouth, with golden and blue iridescence. Equally hardy.
textos.90cd6b69d2aee4ce: **Notes**: It has a bright red throat that it displays by puffing out its gill covers to intimidate others. It burrows in the sand. It is one of the Central American species most tolerant of other fish.
textos.4f28dda8e12c3b63: **Notes**: A European bottom-dwelling fish, dark green or golden in color. Feeds on debris from the bottom. Compatible with koi and goldfish. Does not compete aggressively for food. Very hardy.
textos.5741286d6d676f9d: **Notes**: Short, pointed leaves arranged in a spiral, with a very distinctive appearance. Very soft, acidic water.
textos.5130956d75822dfa: **Notes**: Freshwater archerfish with a zigzag-patterned body. It spits water at insects.
textos.6bcce5dcacc1b9f1: **Notes**: It spits jets of water to knock insects off leaves. Needs an aquarium with space above the water and overhanging plants.
textos.a38a132e338d164f: **Notes**: Known for spitting jets of water to knock insects off branches above the water. In captivity, it learns to spit at the caretaker during feeding. It needs space above the water level (emerged plants, branches) to practice its natural behavior. Requires a secure lid: it can jump and spit outside the aquarium.
textos.3594138f6a9387dc: **Notes**: Brown with spots and a broad head. Hardy and nocturnal.
textos.f901a0e89c900001: **Notes**: Very distinctive brain-like surfaces. Free-living (does not attach to rocks): place on sand. Responds well to direct feeding. Specimens with green, red, orange, and purple colors are the most highly valued.
textos.99057a1286b34aca: **Notes**: A sand-dwelling cichlid whose males dig large, volcano-shaped nests to attract females. Fine sand is essential.
textos.3691c37401dc2136: **Notes**: It lives among the branches of Pocillopora and Stylophora, which it defends from starfish. Red spots on a light background.
textos.d45b71d91372c5d0: **Notes**: The calmest gourami in the hobby. The male develops a vivid honey-orange coloration during the breeding season. Excellent for small, peaceful aquariums.
textos.a2a2c2a6577852bb: **Notes**: Bluish and orange oblique stripes on males. Related to the dwarf gourami, but larger and hardier.
textos.66e4d3ba4d03122c: **Notes**: Similar to the dwarf gourami but larger and hardier. Males are orange with bluish bands.
textos.4986ce66ffe40838: **Notes**: The most popular gourami for small aquariums. The male has blue and red stripes. Susceptible to iridovirus (DGIV). Buy from trusted suppliers.
textos.b4405e26953d73a8: **Notes**: Body covered with pearlescent spots and a dark line that extends to the tail. Males have an orange chest during the breeding season. One of the calmest and most elegant gouramis.
textos.2f5384e248d3b246: **Notes**: Silvery with moonlight-like iridescence and pelvic fins that resemble orange threads in males. Very calm; requires plants and peaceful tankmates.
textos.abeccdb6bd344502: **Notes**: The largest of the common gouramis, with a snakeskin-like pattern. Very calm despite its size.
textos.3788201a5a231e81: **Notes**: Breathes air from the surface thanks to its labyrinth organ. Very hardy and comes in golden, opal, and platinum colors. Only one male per aquarium.
textos.cf6cbc956e24f99b: **Notes**: Emits small, audible clicks during courtship. Blue eyes and speckled fins. Perfect for nano-aquariums planted with floating plants and without a current.
textos.499e7c66ec607d8e: **Notes**: Emits audible growls when fighting or courting. Dark stripes and blue eyes.
textos.bba24f23447b2517: **Notes**: Yellow with a black stripe and a red belly. Very colorful but with a strong temperament.
textos.932d7cac66505367: **Notes**: The smallest giant clam, with an electrically colored mantle. It burrows into rock; requires very bright lighting. Listed under CITES.
textos.06679e00078032ee: **Notes**: Giant clam with a smooth shell and a patterned mantle. One of the hardiest species, farmed in aquaculture facilities. CITES.
textos.bed5a58786f60a88: **Notes**: Mantle in intense blues, greens, and golds. Requires bright lighting and stable water conditions. Some dwarf angelfish and parasitic snails attack its mantle. Species listed under CITES: only captive-bred specimens.
textos.0a85ce28ec252e38: **Notes**: Shell with large scales and a patterned mantle. Slightly more tolerant of light than Maxima or Crocea. CITES.
textos.a3d8f5119099e644: **Notes**: Similar to the harlequin rasbora but more slender, with a coppery body and a narrower, axe-shaped black spot. Very calm when kept in a group.
textos.087f8e0c9cebb5c2: **Notes**: A mini version of the Harlequin Rasbora. Perfect for planted nano tanks and Asian biotope-style aquariums.
textos.4ffaf2fa248e4b4b: **Notes**: The triangular black spot on the rear half of the body is its defining characteristic. Very popular in planted aquariums.
textos.c6b15317e8838d2c: **Notes**: The smallest and rarest of the harlequin rasboras, with a thin black line on a pink background. Virtually extinct in the wild.
textos.b253b097aaa9a1ac: **Notes**: Similar to the harlequin rasbora, with a truncated black patch. Soft water.
textos.9185a5b027ba3de5: **Notes**: A small, red, spotted goby that hovers under rock overhangs. Perfect for nano tanks.
textos.5bee84acdfab1829: **Notes**: It uses shells and debris as camouflage. A voracious algae eater in medium and large aquariums.
textos.72d618224fb62896: **Notes**: Short white spines on a dark body. Heavy algae eater.
textos.6702dd9dbae1b508: **Notes**: Males in breeding season are bright yellow with black heads. A small fish of shaded rock walls.
textos.32fabf206070dc63: **Notes**: Conical shell. Excellent grazer of coralline and filamentous algae on rocks. It can right itself if it falls on its back (an advantage over Astraea). Can reproduce in the aquarium. Active both day and night.
textos.23d51ea7be3c62c6: **Notes**: Herbivorous Mbuna with many local variations: females are yellow or brown, and males are blue or black. A plant-based diet is essential.
textos.d9617a1d3c903c0a: **Notes**: A dark-bodied Tropheus with a light vertical band. Same care requirements as the moorii.
textos.7ae000b80ec91b1d: **Notes**: Many local forms with vertical colored bands. Herbivorous diet and pristine water.
textos.99b78d4afab18080: **Notes**: Juveniles are black with white spots; adults are dark blue with a yellow band. For experienced aquarists only: requires a strict plant-based diet and pristine water.
textos.16a38d2baeca847c: **Notes**: There are dozens of local varieties with very different colors (red, yellow, “Kaiser”). Never mix varieties in the same aquarium. Plant-based diet without red protein.
textos.f2f574b8df18ed7a: **Notes**: Bright orange polyps that open at night. It does not photosynthesize: it must be fed daily.
textos.1095fad152b5fdcf: **Notes**: An organ-like skeleton of red tubes, from which green or gray feathery polyps extend. It needs calcium to grow.
textos.ce029c0f579387f9: **Notes**: A tiny tetra with a dark stripe and orange highlights. A blackwater fish suitable for very well-maintained nano tanks.
textos.be57e46d912f0c1a: **Notes**: Vertical, wavy plates of a grayish-green color. Very hardy.
textos.a3dfbf4790ea1278: **Notes**: Gray or brown plates with large polyps that extend during the day. Very hardy.
textos.a812558561b2692e: **Notes**: Yellow or green plates shaped like a kidney or a cup. Very hardy, ideal for beginners in hard corals.
textos.f29a18d98f7f64ba: **Notes**: A voracious eater of filamentous algae. Prefers slightly cooler water; it has a shorter lifespan in very warm reef environments. May knock over poorly anchored corals.
textos.63648da627f13d6e: **Notes**: Elongated, spiral-shaped shell and a body with striking colors (orange, yellow, black). Requires warm, somewhat hard water. Eats very tender plants if hungry.
textos.c38f6c9fe6d46a88: **Notes**: The dwarf variety of cattail, with rounded spikes. Perfect for small ponds where it won’t take over.
textos.e17964d3cd04ae38: **Notes**: Enormous mouth and zigzag-patterned markings; males turn green and blue. Keep only with large haplochromines.
textos.0fd095e42b7d7bcf: **Notes**: Tall, rounded body with a teardrop-shaped black spot. A good tankmate for large discus. Eats soft plants.
textos.d91746431aeef6c2: **Notes**: The male has a highly developed pincer (violin-shaped) used in displays to attract females and in fights with other males. Semi-terrestrial: requires areas of exposed soil or sand above water (mangrove shoreline biotope). Very sensitive to copper. Not compatible with fish that could tear them apart.
textos.41adabad4de30687: **Notes**: Calcified green fans. A relative of halimeda, slow-growing.
textos.26ebc016bb57218e: **Notes**: Green, thin, and broad leaves. A natural food highly prized by surgeonfish and rabbitfish, and a great nutrient exporter in the refugium.
textos.ab2acaebc2e0fa9d: **Notes**: Carnivorous plant: It has small traps that capture microorganisms. It forms a very fine, dense carpet, but it is demanding and falls apart easily.
textos.ef09dd8bd3306df9: **Notes**: Known as the “comb-fin loach” because of its long dorsal fin. Nocturnal and secretive.
textos.ab256b61f21937a4: **Notes**: Two dark longitudinal stripes and a black spot on the dorsal fin. Scavenges the substrate.
textos.0fcf2ea96791fcdd: **Notes**: White body with orange spots. It constantly sifts through the sand, keeping it clean, but it strips the aquarium of small invertebrates. It requires a deep, mature sand bed.
textos.b540c6cc5a2cc3f1: **Notes**: Light-colored body with blue spots on the cheeks. Excellent sand cleaner; requires a mature substrate.
textos.708275f54cc3d1bf: **Notes**: Yellow head with a bright blue stripe. Constantly sifts through the sand; requires a mature substrate with microfauna.
textos.ca048c7b88585f34: **Notes**: Very long, ribbon-like leaves that float on the surface. Perfect for tall aquariums and for hard-water cichlids, which don’t usually eat it.
textos.5f4642e491503ae0: **Notes**: Very thin, almost thread-like leaves that form a dense background. Visually more delicate than spiral vallisneria and just as easy to care for.
textos.969292778b7bd3ea: **Notes**: It grows as fast as the goldfish eats it, remaining viable. It tolerates hard, alkaline water perfectly. A good strategy is to plant it in large quantities so the goldfish can nibble on it without depleting the supply.
textos.ac47c7c73aa59a15: **Notes**: One of the largest single-celled organisms in the world, resembling a bright green bubble. In aquariums, it is considered a pest; do not pop it when removing it, as it will spread spores.
textos.07c5fcb729937b47: **Notes**: Velvety black with blue-edged fins; fry are yellow. A pair claims a large portion of the aquarium.
textos.a4e8a63aa0f58cdb: **Notes**: Similar to Java moss but with more triangular and compact leaves. Very easy to care for.
textos.b7013b45f5d78034: **Notes**: Its branches hang down like those of a weeping willow. Looks beautiful on tall wooden branches. Excellent shelter for shrimp.
textos.75cf931c1b5cdb18: **Notes**: Its Christmas tree-shaped branches make it very ornamental. Highly prized in high-end shrimp aquariums (Caridina). It produces more biofilm than Java moss due to the greater specific surface area of its filaments.
textos.36c1ec9b08b23634: **Notes**: A more compact version of Christmas moss, with branches shaped like tiny fir trees. Ideal for nano tanks.
textos.81a16bae2b6fd98d: **Notes**: Known as the black-banded cichlid: dark band down the center of the body and a reddish throat.
textos.bdf31720e862274b: **Notes**: Red head and body with dark spots and green iridescence. It was sold as Cichlasoma synspilum. It eats plants.
textos.95acc276d58f29f6: **Notes**: Smooth, olive-green shell. Removes film-like algae from glass and leaves.
textos.dbb26a126711dfd6: **Notes**: A snail with a dark-banded shell that filters the water. Very useful in ponds; does not harm plants.
textos.7400ad799ccf8d20: **Notes**: Reddish-brown with yellow bands and ocelli on the fins. It lives hidden among the crevices.
textos.8795d6348691732b: **Notes**: The world’s smallest flowering plant, like green specks on the surface. Very difficult to eradicate once established.
textos.7073bdb794017bb2: **Notes**: Males have a blue throat. It feeds on plankton rather than bottom-dwelling invertebrates, making it one of the few triggerfish compatible with a reef tank.
textos.626f59987c475a80: **Reef Safe**: ⚠️ Use caution (may bite small shrimp)
textos.f39693cf4145e10d: **Notes**: Red tail and blue stripes on its face. It feeds on plankton, making it one of the calmest triggerfish.
textos.f82e9251279dfaa2: **Notes**: Long, slender jaws lined with teeth. It gets startled and jumps easily; it may injure itself against the glass.
textos.7ab172364c5da027: **Notes**: The tentacles contract and expand rhythmically (pulsing): hypnotic behavior. It reproduces rapidly and can overrun the aquarium: requires control. Very sensitive to water quality. Absorbs phosphate.
textos.8fcf47bd1bebbcf1: **Notes**: Uniform dark brown, without a dorsal fin. Nocturnal; emits small sounds using its swim bladder.
textos.e86ae10e254e591a: **Notes**: A golden sand-dwelling cichlid with a yellow dorsal fin. It lives in groups and forms pairs to breed.
textos.b4d6398d4fd5a7c1: **Notes**: Known as “Sunflower”: dorsal fin with yellow and blue edges. It lives among rocks, unlike other Xenotilapia species.
textos.0dc217d824e816b9: **Notes**: Males have an orange rear end with blue iridescence. This Goodeid is threatened in its natural habitat; keeping it helps conserve the species.
textos.1f6efe06ab90dedb: **Notes**: Greenish wild swordtail with a red line and a black-edged sword. Active and a good jumper.
textos.f6157557ec6908d9: **Notes**: The male has a sword-shaped extension on its tail. Active and a good jumper: a lid is essential. The red, black, and tuxedo varieties are bred in captivity.
textos.0b5da1611c5504db: **Notes**: More hardy than the guppy; tolerates hard, alkaline water. Many color varieties. Easy to care for and breed.
textos.5c9dd90199ea3426: **Notes**: Wild swordtail with dark spots and a long sword. Keeping the breed pure helps preserve the species.
textos.8a808e07f795763a: **Notes**: Males have dark vertical bars and a short sword. Related to nigrensis.
textos.5b0505ef19a85d68: **Notes**: A small wild swordtail with a short sword and dark bands. Studied for its different types of males.
textos.d52b4598f98bac87: **Notes**: Tiny swordtail, almost without a sword, with golden highlights. Suitable for nano tanks with hard water.
textos.102116eb6db37f63: **Notes**: Slightly slimmer than the common platy and more tolerant of cooler water. Very colorful in its breeding forms (parrot, marigold).
textos.f7ce402b34ba9ab6: **Notes**: Bluish-gray body with orange or red fins. It grows quite large and is lively.
textos.168de54eafc2da44: **Notes**: Silver-gray with a dark line running from the snout to the tail. It may nibble on long fins; best kept with fast-swimming fish.
textos.57ae6161194821bc: **Notes**: Reef icon, with black, white, and yellow bands and a very long filament. In aquariums, very few adapt to eating; the pennant butterflyfish is the recommended alternative.
textos.b59bfb79edb45487: **Notes**: Large, white, trumpet-shaped flowers. Widely used in Mediterranean ponds. Toxic if ingested.
textos.bc4f66e79789b9f3: **Notes**: Related to the sailfin surgeonfish, with spots on the head and vertical bands. Very large fins; requires a long aquarium.
textos.900030c101a4b889: **Notes**: The most recommended tang for beginners in marine aquariums. More resistant to ich than the Blue Surgeonfish. Very striking, intense yellow color. Supplement with nori seaweed several times a week.
textos.64243316cc99daf1: **Notes**: Bluish-black with white spots and a yellow tail. One of the most expensive surgeonfish.
textos.cf2a7cfaa8452222: **Notes**: Jet black with an elongated snout. Rare and highly sought after by collectors.
textos.4155a649b89c3cf3: **Notes**: A brown relative of the yellow surgeonfish, with a darker rear section. Just as hardy and slightly less expensive. An excellent algae eater.
textos.160766267e8cbd88: **Notes**: Vertical stripes and enormous dorsal and anal fins that it spreads out like sails. It grows quite large and needs a long aquarium.
textos.8c98539449723d45: **Notes**: Deep purple with a yellow tail. Requires a long aquarium for swimming and daily algae feeding. Prone to lateral line erosion with poor diets.
textos.ba25c791145404b0: **Notes**: A zoanthid with large polyps. The different color varieties have a wide range of commercial names.
textos.bdd7d3447ab474da: **Notes**: Small green and brown polyps with a lighter-colored disc. Easy to care for and fast-growing.
textos.d3607d8f70f8b518: **Notes**: Small green polyps in dense colonies. One of the easiest zoanthids to care for. Contains palytoxin: wear gloves when handling it.
textos.099ed3ce9a71acee: **Notes**: Colonies of polyps with a huge variety of colors. “Designer” Zoanthus (PPE, Utter Chaos, Rastas, Eagle Eye) can cost hundreds of euros per polyp. **WARNING**: Palythoa sp. contain palytoxin—which is extremely toxic to humans. Zoanthus may also contain it in small amounts: always wear gloves.
textos.c3ba31af0f556979: **Notes**: Translucent body with blue and gold iridescence. Lives in groups among coral branches.
